item.title: Wednesday, August 26, 2026
item.description:
Strong CP, one rung down

A diffuse, methods-heavy day whose clearest through-line extends yesterday’s strong-CP result. Li et al. arXiv:2608.23685 give the first direct lattice-QCD determination of the θ-induced CP-violating pion-nucleon coupling — the hadronic matrix element sitting one rung above the nEDM — landing at g̃_πNN=0.0306(56)(124) θ̅, consistent with the indirect estimate from the strong n–p mass splitting. Coming a day after Blum et al.’s nEDM extraction, it fills in the coupling side of the same calculation. Around it: an exclusive |V_cb| update that keeps the R(D^*) tension alive, neural amplitude analysis, and a rethink of the look-elsewhere effect.

Themes

CP violation and structure on the lattice

Li et al. arXiv:2608.23685 use overlap valence fermions on three domain-wall ensembles plus cluster-decomposition error reduction, and note precision is limited by the heavy sea-pion extrapolation — a direct hadronic-coupling complement to yesterday’s nEDM result and the season’s running strong-CP thread. Two structure papers ride alongside: Edwards et al. arXiv:2608.23737 propose impact-parameter Ioffe-time distributions and extract Compton form factors from lattice, and Asmaee et al. arXiv:2608.23788 compute the proton’s photon/gluon gravitational form factors via QCD sum rules.

Flavor: |V_cb| and a persistent R(D*)

Chen et al. arXiv:2608.24332 combine Belle II, updated B→D⁽) lattice form factors, and large-recoil LCSR to get |V_cb|=(39.18±0.47)×10⁻³, with R(D)=0.3069, R(D^)=0.2548 — and their SM 68% region shows “little overlap” with the experimental average. Against a flavor front that has otherwise been consolidating on nulls this month, this is the LFU tension refusing to soften.

Neutrinos, from quantum bounds to detector geometry

Lu arXiv:2608.23654 builds an operational quantum-estimation framework for three-flavor oscillations, arguing the propagated pure qutrit caps QFI rank at four and that some global sensitivity claims aren’t backed by local Fisher bounds — checked against a DUNE GLoBES config to 10⁻¹⁶. On hardware: Aguilar et al. arXiv:2608.23773 show ESSνSB’s near water-Cherenkov detector can shrink 8× in volume with GNN flavour ID, and Kim et al. arXiv:2608.24746 get percent-level reactor-spectrum normalization from directional recoil-electron reconstruction.

Neural amplitudes, honest significance

Smith et al. introduce S-matrix informed neural networks learning ππ amplitudes under unitarity/analyticity/crossing arXiv:2608.23750, then perform the first dispersive pole extraction (σ, ρ(770), f_0(980)) from analytically continued networks arXiv:2608.23738 — the ML-tooling wave reaching amplitude analysis with first-principles constraints. Separately, Han Zhang et al. arXiv:2608.24872 recast the look-elsewhere effect as a procedural-consistency correction: a 3σ global peak-search significance maps to ~4σ in a binary test at fixed statistic — a natural companion to last week’s Reisch et al. search-budget accounting.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.23685 — First direct lattice g̃_πNN; the hadronic coupling behind the nEDM, one day after the strong-CP confirmation.
  • arXiv:2608.24332 — Exclusive |V_cb| with LCSR constraints; SM R(D⁽*)) region barely overlaps data — the tension persists.
  • arXiv:2608.23750 — S-matrix informed neural networks: physics-constrained amplitude learning with a data-selection procedure, transferable well beyond ππ.
  • arXiv:2608.24872 — A cleaner statistical reading of the look-elsewhere effect and what a “5σ” actually buys.
  • arXiv:2608.24456 — Amin et al. calibrate axion-string birefringence to an AMR simulation, bounding |𝒜|<0.24 and excluding the minimal GUT anomaly coefficient.

From the community

Two PhD theses surface today — Schimmel Brener’s ATLAS lepton+jet BSM searches arXiv:2608.24717 and Kyriazis’s axion cosmic-string/superradiance dissertation arXiv:2608.23789 — the periodic review-and-consolidate output that thesis season brings.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.24677 Electron and Muon g−2 Constraints on Light Vector Bosons — Serao et al. (hep-ph) — the cesium-based electron g-2 closes an X_17 high-coupling window that the rubidium fit leaves open.
  • arXiv:2608.24161 Solar-Basin ALP Decay with XMM-Newton Blank-Sky Observations — Bo Zhang et al. (hep-ph) — first anti-solar search for the ALP solar basin, g_aγγ∼10⁻¹⁰–10⁻¹¹ over 1.4–16 keV.
  • arXiv:2608.23679 When the HL-LHC is blind, LISA is deaf — Moretti et al. (hep-ph) — type-I 2HDM: LISA-audible GW signals live almost entirely in HL-LHC–visible H→ZZ territory.
  • arXiv:2608.23931 Photogrammetry for Mu2e Tracker Alignment — Palo et al. (physics.ins-det) — touchless ~25 μm transverse module metrology in an hour.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.23685 — Direct lattice QCD calculation of the θ-induced CP-violating pion-nucleon coupling (Chuan-Yang Li et al.)

The χQCD collaboration reports the first direct lattice evaluation of the θ-induced CP-odd pion-nucleon coupling, extracting the forward proton matrix element of the isovector pseudoscalar density weighted by the topological charge to first order in θ̅. Working with overlap valence fermions on three RBC/UKQCD 2+1-flavor domain-wall ensembles at a single spacing (a=0.1105 fm), they use the index-theorem-consistent overlap definition of Q and cluster-decomposition error reduction (CDER) to tame the volume-enhanced noise, while explicitly including the θ̅-induced parity mixing of the external nucleon (the 2α_1 g_P term). A key simplification over their earlier nEDM work: the ratio at q²⁼⁰ directly isolates the full physical g̃_P with no zero-recoil extrapolation or separate α_1/g_P calculation, and Z_mZ_P=1 for overlap removes renormalization. An AIC-weighted average over 7 partially-quenched extrapolation forms yields g̃_πNN=0.0306(56)(124) θ̅; the full-volume cross-check gives 0.0305(87)(140) θ̅.

This supplies the hadronic-coupling rung above the nEDM, complementing yesterday’s Blum et al. extraction and testing the chiral matching relations that underpin EDM interpretations of light nuclei and diamagnetic atoms. The result is consistent with the indirect n–p mass-splitting estimate 0.0155(20)(16) θ̅, though the central value sits somewhat higher. The honest caveats are stark: the dominant second error is the extrapolation-form spread from heavy sea pions (no dedicated partially-quenched χPT expression exists), and the single lattice spacing means discretization effects are not quantified. Lighter-pion ensembles are underway.

arXiv:2608.24332 — Exclusive Determination of |V_cb| from Semileptonic Decays B→D⁽*)ℓν_ℓ (Xue-Wen Chen et al.)

Chen et al. perform a frequentist BGL global fit combining the latest Belle II B→Dℓν and B→D^ℓν spectra, updated lattice form factors (FNAL/MILC, HPQCD, JLQCD), and correlated large-recoil SCET/LCSR predictions with NLO and next-to-leading-power corrections, plus strong unitarity bounds from four heavy-to-heavy channels with HQET power corrections to 𝒪(ε_c²⁾. Three nested scenarios show LCSR constraints dramatically shrink high-order form-factor uncertainties. The full global fit yields |V_cb|=(39.18±0.47)×10⁻³, with the SM predictions R(D)=0.3069±0.0080 and R(D^)=0.2548±0.0043 from the lattice⊕LCSR theory fit. The correlated 68% theory ellipse in the (R(D),R(D^*)) plane shows “only modest overlap” with individual experimental measurements and a substantial deviation from the experimental average.

The takeaway for today’s flavor theme: even a state-of-the-art SM benchmark leaves the LFU tension intact, against a month where flavor has otherwise consolidated on nulls. The paper is candid about internal frictions — visible tension between the HPQCD B→D^ dataset and other lattice results, and mild lattice-vs-LCSR discord, though points overlap within errors. Their |V_cb| sits 1.7×10⁻³ below a recent Bayesian angular analysis, attributed to methodological choices (correlated LCSR inputs, dropping electron-mode data with known e/μ tension, frequentist vs. MCMC). Local angular deviations from Belle II exist but carry no significance. Whether the residual R(D⁽)) gap is theory systematics or new physics remains open pending better lattice/LCSR control and Belle II statistics.

arXiv:2608.23750 — S-matrix informed neural networks for amplitude analysis (Wyatt A. Smith et al.)

The Joint Physics Analysis Center introduces SINNs — neural representations of partial-wave amplitudes on the real axis that enforce S-matrix principles by construction. A shared trunk feeds channel-specific heads, with threshold barrier factors (q²ℓ+1) and the inelasticity map imposed algebraically in postprocessing (guaranteeing 0≤η≤1 and elastic unitarity below thresholds), while analyticity and crossing enter numerically through a twice-subtracted Roy-equation loss evaluated over 2m_π<√(s)<1.1 GeV. Training uses a six-phase curriculum with UPGrad multi-objective gradient handling to prevent the dispersive integrals from collapsing the fit to trivial solutions. Applied to ππ scattering, the framework recovers the expected σ/f_0(500), ρ(770), and f_0(980) features and yields scattering lengths a_0⁰⁼⁰.222⁺⁰.014_-0.014, a_0²⁼⁻⁰.041⁺⁰.005_-0.006 m_π⁻¹, consistent with Colangelo et al. and García-Martín et al. (with honestly larger bands, reflecting genuine amplitude-space sampling).

The methodological headline is “spectral response clustering”: each experiment is upweighted inside constrained ensembles, a symmetrized χ²-response matrix is spectrally embedded and Ward-clustered, and groups in tension are pruned automatically — replacing heuristic data selection. Two rounds cut the historically inconsistent ππ database to 18 experiments/621 points, dropping the deep-dip Protopopescu and several Grayer/Hyams solutions, lowering median loss from 7.2 to 3.1. Robustness is well-documented: a 100-architecture sweep shifts no central value by more than 0.42δx; closure tests recover a known CFD amplitude (|z|<0.4); and an ablation shows removing Roy constraints leaves data description untouched but degrades scattering lengths outside the universal band. Caveats acknowledged: the selected dataset implicitly depends on the selection architecture, unknown experimental systematics likely dominate, and the KK̅ cusp in the S_0 phase is deliberately not imposed. The workflow is presented as transferable to πK, πN, and beyond.

item.title: Tuesday, August 25, 2026
item.description:
Precision nulls, and a heavy tooling day

Two clean precision results anchor the day. Belle II sets ℬ(τ→μγ)<9.5×10⁻⁸ (arXiv:2608.23009), and a lattice-QCD nEDM calculation from Blum et al. (arXiv:2608.22587) confirms the strong-CP problem is real, bounding |θ̅|≲10⁻¹¹. Around them the weight is unusually infrastructural — a dense cluster of detector-simulation and fast-sim tooling — plus a top-sector SMEFT paper that continues the EFT-as-default thread the memory has tracked through the aTGC and top-FCNC fits, and yet another glut of exotic-hadron spectroscopy.

Themes

Precision nulls and low-energy CP

Belle II’s τ→μγ limit arXiv:2608.23009 is a clean null on 428 fb⁻¹, tightening the flagship LFV channel. The nEDM lattice result arXiv:2608.22587 is the more striking: a Feynman–Hellmann extraction from the topological-charge density in a background electric field, yielding d_n=-0.0050(4)(8) θ̅ e·fm and a statistically significant θ̅-induced signal. Alongside, Tomalak et al. arXiv:2608.22845 add explicit Δ(1232) contributions to QED radiative corrections in neutron/inverse-beta decay — restoring power counting and driving the g_A/g_A^QCD radiative shift to zero — extending the neutron-decay g_A thread from Gialidi et al. (08-18).

EFT reads the top and electroweak data

Englert et al. arXiv:2608.21510 organize the mild rate shifts in single-top and tH/tt̅H as a coherent SMEFT pattern — a weak top dipole plus a triple-gauge deformation — and then show no single scalar, vector, or vector-like-quark multiplet reproduces it under weakly-coupled matching. This is the EFT-as-default-language thread again, now used diagnostically rather than just for limit-setting.

Detector and fast-simulation tooling

An instrumentation-heavy day. Galgoczi arXiv:2608.21396 gets a 15× speedup in GPU optical-photon Monte Carlo via Shader Execution Reordering; Pierini arXiv:2608.22262 trains a regression that brings CMS scouting objects within offline calibration bands. On the fast-sim side, Butter et al. arXiv:2608.21509 build calibrated uncertainties into normalizing flows, Elabd et al. arXiv:2608.22873 make Parnassus’s parametric models differentiable, and Spinner et al. arXiv:2608.23022 recast early-universe Boltzmann equations with neural distribution functions and MC importance sampling — the autodiff-everything wave the memory has tracked, now reaching cosmology.

Exotic-hadron spectroscopy, again

Two independent takes on the X(2370) glueball question (arXiv:2608.22394 radial-hybrid; Zhu et al. arXiv:2608.23428 via η-η’-G-η_c mixing in radiative J/ψ,ψ(2S) decays), a resonance-continuum treatment of a tensor X(6900) arXiv:2608.23408, a CNN reanalysis of the Λ(1405) two-pole structure arXiv:2608.22747, and radiative signatures of a scalar DD̅ molecule arXiv:2608.23332. All propose discriminating measurements for BESIII/Belle II rather than settling anything.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.22587 — Blum et al.’s lattice nEDM from the topological-charge density; confirms strong-CP and demonstrates a method extendable to other CP-violating operators.
  • arXiv:2608.23009 — Belle II’s new τ→μγ limit; the reference number for the flagship LFV channel.
  • arXiv:2608.21510 — Englert et al. show current single-top/tH rate shifts fit a SMEFT pattern no minimal UV multiplet reproduces.
  • arXiv:2608.22845 — Tomalak et al.’s Δ(1232) contribution restores power counting and nulls the g_A radiative shift; relevant to the lattice-vs-experiment g_A debate.
  • arXiv:2608.22262 — Pierini’s regression closes the online-offline gap for CMS scouting; a practical route to treating scouting objects with standard calibrations.

From the community

Turner arXiv:2608.22087 Particle Dark Matter in the 1980s and 1990s — Michael S. Turner (astro-ph.CO) — a first-person history of how inner and outer space merged into ΛCDM; reflection, not result.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.21720 Thermal width shift of Δ⁺⁺ in a pion gas — Ying Zhang et al. (hep-ph) — collisional broadening reaching ~6 MeV at T≈160 MeV; the STAR extraction demands genuine hot-medium contributions.
  • arXiv:2608.23183 Search for Light Scalars in the Two Real Singlet Model at the LHC — Aman Desai et al. (hep-ph) — Vh_2→4b+ℓν reaching ~12σ at HL-LHC for light-scalar cascades.
  • arXiv:2608.21951 ALP production from kaon decays within U(3) chiral theory — Jinbao Wang et al. (hep-ph) — constraints from the latest NA62 K⁺→π⁺+invisible limit.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.23009 — Search for the lepton-flavor-violating decay τ→μγ at Belle II (Belle II Collaboration et al.)

Belle II sets ℬ(τ^±→μ^±γ)<9.5 (12.2)×10⁻⁸ at 90% (95%) CL on 428 fb⁻¹ (393×10⁶ ττ pairs), from an unbinned 2D extended maximum-likelihood fit in M_bc and ΔE/√(s) after a GBDT selection (final signal efficiency 5.97%, τ⁺τ⁻ rejection 99.8%). Eight events are observed in the signal region against a sideband-extrapolated background of 5.7±1.2; the fitted branching fraction (2.8⁺⁴.4_-2.6)×10⁻⁸ is consistent with zero. The observed limit is slightly weaker than the expected 7.6 (9.2)×10⁻⁸, attributed to a statistical upward fluctuation. Systematics are dominated by the 5.7% GBDT data/MC efficiency uncertainty (total 6.0% on the efficiency×luminosity×cross-section product); the dominant physical background is τ→μνν̅ plus an ISR/beam photon.

Why it matters: this is the flagship charged-LFV channel, where SM rates are ∼10⁻⁵⁴ and many BSM scenarios (SUSY, seesaw, Littlest Higgs) predict 10⁻¹⁰–10⁻⁸. The result does not yet beat Belle’s 4.2×10⁻⁸ (988 fb⁻¹) or BaBar’s 4.4×10⁻⁸, but on less than half the luminosity it achieves 41% higher signal efficiency and 81% lower background than the Belle analysis, and introduces a unified likelihood with profiled nuisance parameters — establishing the machinery for the far larger datasets to come. The honest caveat is scale: 428 fb⁻¹ is a fraction of Belle II’s design target, so this is a foundation-laying benchmark rather than a world-best number.

arXiv:2608.22587 — Calculation of neutron electric dipole moment from Lattice QCD (Thomas Blum et al.)

Blum et al. extract the θ̅-induced nEDM via a new Feynman–Hellmann route: rather than the noisy forward limit of the F_3 form factor, they compute the matrix element of the local (single-time-slice) topological charge density between nucleon ground states spatially polarized by a uniform background electric field. Because the dipole interaction is anti-Hermitian, these states have mixed parity and are constructed variationally through a non-Hermitian GEVP over a four-operator basis. On three 2+1-flavor domain-wall ensembles (a≈0.11 fm, m_π=340,420,576 MeV, electro-quenched), they obtain a statistically significant signal and extrapolate to d_n=-0.0050(4)(8) θ̅ e·fm. Comparison with the experimental bound gives |θ̅|≲10⁻¹¹, confirming the strong-CP problem.

Why it matters: previous F_3-based calculations at the physical point (Alexandrou et al., Bhattacharya et al.) yield no significant signal because the global topological-charge summation is too noisy; truncated-sum methods (Dragos et al., Liang et al.) introduce their own systematics. Sampling the topological charge locally sidesteps both global summation and the Q²→0 extrapolation, and the authors show the conventional positive-parity projection suffers large excited-state contamination that the GEVP removes — plausibly explaining a real discrepancy with the lighter-mass points of Liang et al. The method extends directly to Weinberg three-gluon and four-quark CP-odd operators. Caveats are explicit: single lattice spacing, electro-quenched approximation, and a physical-point extrapolation anchored at m_π=340 MeV — finite-volume and discretization effects remain to be quantified.

arXiv:2608.21510 — Electroweak and Single Top-Quark Conspiracy in Current LHC Data (Christoph Englert et al.)

Englert, Kogler, and Spannowsky ask whether recent above-SM central values in tWZ (μ=1.77±0.32) and tqγ (1.34⁺⁰.19_-0.17), plus a large ATLAS tHq (7.2⁺⁴.6_-4.0) alongside below-SM tt̅H (0.59⁺⁰.22_-0.20), form a coherent SMEFT pattern while VBS/triboson channels stay SM-like. A linearized (𝒪(Λ⁻²⁾) five-coefficient Warsaw-basis fit to eight LHC rates plus five Z-pole observables gives χ²_min=11.2 (8 d.o.f., p=0.19), improving on the SM by Δχ²⁼¹³.4 (local ∼2.1σ). The largest pulls are a triple-gauge C_W (∼1.9σ) and the weak top dipole C_tW (∼1.7σ), with positive C_Hq⁽³⁾; C_HW is poorly constrained. Fixing C_W=0 still fits (χ²⁼¹⁴.9, 9 d.o.f.). Notably, the fit absorbs the A_FB⁰,b anomaly — but only by shifting A_e ~4σ below LEP/SLD, a subset artifact flagged by the authors.

Why it matters: this is the EFT-as-diagnostic thread — using SMEFT not for limits but to test UV consistency. Under weakly-coupled renormalizable matching, no single scalar, vector, or vector-like-quark multiplet reproduces the pattern: currents need a charge-2/3 singlet, the dipole’s opposite chirality needs a hypercharge-1/6 doublet, and positive C_Hq⁽³⁾ demands triplet custodial partners protecting Zb_Lb̅_L. A benchmark multi-threshold VLQ sector (1.6–2.0 TeV) reproduces the current alignment with κ_t≃0.91, but the fit-preferred dipole must come from unspecified loop dynamics. Caveats: linearized truncation with no EFT uncertainty, no experimental covariances, and a preselected measurement set — the “2σ” is explicitly local and not a global SM improvement.

item.title: Monday, August 24, 2026
item.description:
New instruments for old dark-matter questions

The day’s weight sits on detection methodology, not results — two leading limits arrive from unconventional apparatus. POLONAISE (arXiv:2608.20464) runs the first ultraheavy-DM search with a magnetically levitated milligram ferromagnet, pushing seven orders of magnitude in mass past optical levitation; and a HFIR cold-neutron-beam search (arXiv:2608.21120) improves the n→n’ transformation limit by an order of magnitude — the same mirror-neutron channel that surfaced on 08-13. Flavor stayed quiet and consistent: LHCb’s first Λ_b⁰→Λ(1520)μμ angular analysis (arXiv:2608.21082) lands on the SM, and Pich et al. reaffirm the data-driven approach can’t reach the observed charm CPV. A tooling-heavy day rounds it out.

Themes

Dark matter: new detection handles

POLONAISE arXiv:2608.20464 resolves TeV-scale impulses with a levitated ferromagnet, setting leading composite-DM cross-section limits across 10⁶–10¹⁵ GeV. On the wave-like end, Moroi’s pedagogical review arXiv:2608.20745 lays out qubit-based DM sensing, and Liang et al. arXiv:2608.20715 finally compute the transverse dielectric response for light-DM–electron scattering in silicon — 4–6 orders below the longitudinal, giving the first rigorous justification for the standard approximation. With the HFIR n→n’ result arXiv:2608.21120, four distinct hardware routes into hidden sectors in one day.

Flavor nulls hold

LHCb’s Λ_b⁰→Λ(1520)μμ angular analysis arXiv:2608.21082 — A_FB and S_1cc over 0.1–12.5 GeV² — agrees with the SM, a baryonic complement to the mesonic b→sℓℓ picture that has been consolidating rather than tensioning since the mid-month C_9 flare. Pich et al. arXiv:2608.21212 tighten the two-channel rescattering treatment of charm CPV with a single well-determined strong-scattering input and conclude the Standard Model still falls short — the anomaly stays unexplained, not resolved.

Tooling: GPU, quantum simulation, RL

Bothmann et al. arXiv:2608.21338 present the first end-to-end GPU-resident event generator with normalizing-flow proposals feeding Pepper, turning billion-event high-multiplicity samples from multi-week to sub-day jobs. Davoudi et al. arXiv:2608.21258 strip a factor of ~10¹⁴ from product-formula QCD quantum-simulation cost estimates — a reminder the field’s headline gate counts are still algorithm-limited. And Jha et al.’s CDRL arXiv:2608.20686 uses symbolic certificates to steer reinforcement learning through a >10²⁶ neutrino-flavor-model space, extracting reusable rules along the way.

Precision for lepton colliders

Frixione et al. arXiv:2608.21181 compute the electron PDFs at NNLO in QED, and show the Δ scheme kills the MS soft-log enhancement — arguing NNLO is needed for the 10⁻⁴ precision targets of hundred-GeV lepton colliders. This feeds directly into the season’s running FCC-ee precision thread.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.20464 — POLONAISE: first ultraheavy-DM search with a levitated magnet; leading composite-DM limits and a genuinely new mass reach.
  • arXiv:2608.21082 — LHCb’s first Λ_b→Λ(1520)μμ angular analysis, SM-consistent; the baryonic b→sℓℓ counterpart.
  • arXiv:2608.21120 — Order-of-magnitude improvement on n→n’ from a cold-neutron beam; the mirror-neutron channel again.
  • arXiv:2608.21181 — NNLO QED electron PDFs and an all-order Δ scheme; enabling infrastructure for lepton-collider precision.
  • arXiv:2608.21258 — A ~10¹⁴ cut in QCD quantum-simulation gate cost; algorithmic headroom that matters for near-term feasibility.

From the community

Moroi arXiv:2608.20745 Qubits for Dark Matter Hunting — Takeo Moroi (hep-ph) is an introductory review of qubit- and quantum-sensing-based DM detection — pedagogical field-building for a subfield that keeps recurring in these pages.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.21006 Evidence for η_c(2S)→pp̅π⁺π⁻π⁰ — BESIII Collaboration (hep-ex) — plus first observation of the χ_cJ modes and improved χ_cJ→pp̅ω.
  • arXiv:2608.20458 Poles in πN scattering from forward dispersion relations — Peláez et al. (hep-ph) — model-independent Roper and Δ(1232) poles from revised total cross sections.
  • arXiv:2608.21145 Unraveling QCD dynamics with heavy quark energy correlators — Vitev (hep-ph) — dead-cone imprint on EECs and its medium modification.
  • arXiv:2608.21033 The ABC of RPV III — Dreiner et al. (hep-ph) — LHC coverage of LQD̅ signatures, flagging gaps for wino/higgsino LSPs and unconstrained slepton LSPs.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.20464 — First Search for Ultraheavy Dark Matter Using a Magnetically Levitated Particle (Dennis G. Uitenbroek et al.)

(abstract only) POLONAISE uses a milligram-scale ferromagnet levitated in a superconducting trap as an impulse sensor, reaching a force sensitivity of 0.07 fN Hz⁻¹ᐟ² and resolving momentum kicks as small as 1 TeV/c. Treating every candidate impulse as a possible DM scatter, the collaboration sets optimum-interval upper limits on the neutron coupling for DM interacting via a light mediator: for masses 10⁶–10¹⁵ GeV/c² and mediators below 30 meV/c², they exclude couplings down to α_n = 3.2×10⁻⁹ at 95% CL, giving leading constraints on the DM–neutron cross section for composite DM.

The headline is the apparatus, not a signal. Magnetic levitation extends the mass reach of levitated-sensor DM searches seven orders of magnitude beyond optical levitation, opening the ultraheavy frontier where composite/dark-nugget candidates deposit resolvable single-scatter impulses. This is the mechanical-sensor counterpart to the day’s other hidden-sector hardware routes (qubit sensing, the HFIR mirror-neutron beam). With only the abstract available, the exposure, background model, and impulse-candidate treatment can’t be assessed here — but the quoted sensitivity and mass span are the concrete takeaways.

arXiv:2608.21082 — Angular analysis of the decay Λ_b⁰ → Λ(1520)μ⁺μ⁻ (LHCb collaboration et al.)

First angular analysis of this baryonic b→sℓℓ mode, using LHCb’s full Run 1+2 9 fb⁻¹ sample. The leptonic forward-backward asymmetry A^ℓ_FB,3/2 and the CP-averaged S_1cc are extracted in four narrow q² bins (0.1–12.5 GeV²/c⁴) plus the wide [1.1,6.0] bin, with the Λ(1520) reconstructed in pK⁻ and spin-1/2 Λ* contributions plus their interferences modelled explicitly. All measured values agree with SM predictions built on lattice-QCD and dispersive form factors — e.g. A^ℓ_FB,3/2 = 0.16±0.15±0.06 and S_1cc = 0.19±0.30±0.18 in [1.1,6.0]. The single mild outlier is S_1cc = 1.35±0.54±0.17 in [6.0,8.0], but statistics dominate throughout.

This is the baryonic complement to the mesonic b→sℓℓ program, probing the same FCNC transition with different hadronic structure and spin content — a useful cross-check as the mesonic picture has consolidated rather than sharpened since the mid-month C₉ discussion. Caveats are candid: the measurement is statistics-limited, the fit sits near physical boundaries (biases up to ~18% of the statistical error, corrected via pseudoexperiments), and systematics are dominated by combinatorial and Λ_c⁺-feeddown backgrounds. Discriminating among form-factor predictions awaits larger samples.

arXiv:2608.21120 — New Limits on n→n′ Transformation from HFIR Cold Neutron Beam (James M. Rogers et al.)

A neutron-regeneration search at HFIR’s CG-2/GP-SANS cold beam pushes the mirror-neutron transformation limit an order of magnitude below the prior SNS results. A 3.5 mm cadmium wafer at the center of a 6.6 T split-pair magnet absorbs all beam neutrons (to <10⁻²⁰); any n→n′ conversion in the first magnet half lets sterile n′ pass the cadmium and regenerate to detectable neutrons in the second half, caught by the low-background ³He detector 20 m downstream. No signal appears above background: 95% CL regeneration-probability limits reach ~1.25×10⁻¹¹ per neutron (B=0) up to a few×10⁻¹¹ at nonzero field, translating to an order-of-magnitude improvement in 2θ₀² across Δm = 0.1–1000 neV.

The gains come from HFIR’s ~400× higher average intensity, colder/wider spectrum, and the facility ³He detector. This is the same mirror-neutron channel flagged on 08-13, and one of four hidden-sector hardware routes in the day’s digest. Honest caveats: the 2021 run (~40 h) suffered detector activation of ⁵⁵Mn→⁵⁶Mn, raising and time-varying the background, so it carries reduced weight; the 2024 run (~90 h) is cleaner but background still crept up ~8% over the run. Beam-intensity normalization carries ~4–6% systematics reconciled across multiple monitors. Further reach demands higher intensity, longer beam time, and hard background reduction.

item.title: Friday, August 21, 2026
item.description:
Toponium, confirmed

The day’s anchor is unambiguous: CMS observes an excess at the tt̅ production threshold in the single-lepton channel at 6.1σ (arXiv:2608.19546), a 5.1±0.9 pb cross section consistent with a color-singlet pseudoscalar toponium — and an independent confirmation of the dilepton-channel excess. A theory interpretation lands the same day. Around it, CMS also posts its first global top-FCNC EFT fit, the flavor-numerology genre resurfaces, and Ke et al. offer a clean way to read hadronization off conserved-current flows. A collider-heavy day after a week that ran on flavor and heavy ions.

Themes

The tt̅ threshold excess, now in single leptons

arXiv:2608.19546 uses relative tt̅ velocity plus two spin/parity-sensitive angular observables to pin the excess to a simplified NRQCD pseudoscalar toponium, cross-checking the dilepton result in a statistically independent channel. Matsuoka arXiv:2608.19651 takes the elementary-scalar reading: identify the enhancement with a top-philic Type-III 2HDM CP-odd Higgs, and ask whether the same region drives electroweak baryogenesis — finding explicit CP violation scheme-dependent and no viable transitional branch. Two readings of one bump, worth watching as more channels report.

CMS in the top-EFT sector

arXiv:2608.19547 is the first global top-FCNC search constraining all 24 relevant SMEFT operators simultaneously in one fit — the most stringent limits to date on two-quark–two-lepton FCNC decays. This continues the drift the memory has tracked toward EFT as the default collider language (last seen in the 08-20 aTGC merged-jet bounds). The tooling backbone arrives alongside: Aebischer et al. arXiv:2608.19316 give basis-independent two-loop current–current renormalization for arbitrary dimension-six four-fermion operators, a step toward complete NLO anomalous dimensions for general EFTs.

Flavor-mixing numerology returns

The genre that dominated early in the week (the Barger commensurate-mixing papers) is back. Rousselle arXiv:2608.19277 derives the Koide relation from a U(3)→U(1)×ℤ_3 topological condensation locking the flavor angle at -2/9; Sharma et al. arXiv:2608.19691 fix a rigid TBM deformation to the Cabibbo angle, predicting θ_23=49.19^∘ and a near-π Dirac phase with sharp falsifiability. Parametrization, not dynamics — but each stakes out testable numbers.

Hadronization from conserved currents

Ke et al. arXiv:2608.19708 show color triality forces jet charge, baryon-number, and strangeness flows to obey a Gell-Mann–Nishijima relation, with the net jet baryon number directly measuring the diquark-to-quark vacuum production ratio. This shares the logic of the LEP one-point charge correlator that ran through last week — new precision observables built from conserved currents rather than jet algorithms.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.19546 — CMS confirms the tt̅-threshold excess in single leptons at 6.1σ; the toponium story now has two independent channels.
  • arXiv:2608.19547 — First global top-FCNC EFT fit, all 24 operators in one likelihood; the reference framework for future combinations.
  • arXiv:2608.19708 — Ke et al. turn conserved-current jet flows into a scale-invariant probe of diquark and strange vacuum pair production.
  • arXiv:2608.19316 — Universal two-loop four-fermion running, basis- and scheme-agnostic; EFT tooling that many later fits will import.
  • arXiv:2608.19651 — Matsuoka reads the tt̅ excess as a top-philic 2HDM CP-odd Higgs and tests it against baryogenesis.

From the community

Reisch et al. arXiv:2608.19764 The Search Budget of the BSM Resonance Program — Reisch et al. (hep-ex) counts the ATLAS resonance program’s trials factor in effective resolution elements: 104 spectra cost a 5σ global discovery a local Z=6.55, and a fully combinatorial four-object scan only 7.11 — a factor-46 more looks for 0.56σ. And Doglioni et al. arXiv:2608.19994 Green BOA (cs.LG) works out the carbon break-even point for ML-based data compression, weighing training/inference against storage savings.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.19330 QCD crossover temperature from unbiased exponential resummation — Mitra (hep-lat) — T_pc≈158–160 MeV, consistent with Taylor-expansion results.
  • arXiv:2608.19912 Distilling Normalizing Flows for Real-Time Anomaly Detection — Tahseen et al. (hep-ex) — flow likelihoods distilled to FPGA-deployable students for the hardware trigger.
  • arXiv:2608.19319 Solar Constraints on HNLs with ν_τ Mixing — Brdar et al. (hep-ph) — SOHO data improve |U_τN|² limits by over an order of magnitude near 5 MeV.
  • arXiv:2608.19287 Energy-dependent entanglement in muon decay — Carneiro et al. (hep-ph) — an entanglement-motivated g-2 shift the current binned data can’t distinguish from a constant offset.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.19546 — Observation of an excess at the top quark pair production threshold in the single-lepton channel (CMS Collaboration)

(Abstract only available.) CMS reports a 6.1σ excess near the tt̅ production threshold in single-lepton (e/μ + jets) final states using the full Run 2 dataset (138 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV). The analysis exploits the relative top–antitop velocity plus two angular observables sensitive to the parity and spin of the tt̅ system, comparing to an NNLO QCD baseline. The excess maps onto an observed total cross section of 5.1±0.9 pb and is consistent with a simplified NRQCD-motivated color-singlet pseudoscalar toponium state.

The significance here matters as much as the central value: the single-lepton channel is statistically independent of the dilepton measurement that first flagged the threshold enhancement, so this constitutes a genuine confirmation rather than a re-analysis of the same events. With two channels now converging on the same ∼5 pb, pseudoscalar-consistent signal, the “toponium” reading moves from a single anomaly toward a coherent picture — and sets up the competing elementary-scalar interpretation (Matsuoka’s top-philic 2HDM CP-odd Higgs) as the live alternative to test. The caveat is intrinsic to the modeling: the “toponium” is extracted against a fixed NNLO tt̅ prediction and fit to a simplified single-state NRQCD template, so the inferred cross section and its pseudoscalar identification are only as robust as that threshold-region theory baseline.

arXiv:2608.19547 — Search for top quark FCNC in multilepton final states using an EFT approach (CMS Collaboration)

CMS performs the first global top-FCNC search in which all 24 relevant dimension-six SMEFT Wilson coefficients (12 for tu, 12 for tc) are constrained simultaneously in one likelihood, using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data in same-sign dilepton and trilepton final states. Signal is probed in both single-top production and tt̅ decay via Higgs-, Z-, photon-, gluon-, and directly lepton-pair-mediated FCNC vertices; BDT discriminants (binary for 2ℓss, multiclass jigsaw-reconstructed for 3ℓ) feed a maximum-likelihood fit where signal yields are quadratic polynomials in the WCs. No excess is seen; 68% and 95% intervals are set on all 24 coefficients and translated to branching-fraction limits.

The headline is methodological and archival: this is the first simultaneous treatment of the complete FCNC operator set — including the first-ever direct constraints on two-quark–two-lepton FCNC operators — rather than the usual single-mediator-at-a-time approach that ignores interference. The resulting ℬ(t→Hq) and ℬ(t→Zq) bounds are quoted as similar to or more restrictive than prior anomalous-coupling results, and the framework is explicitly pitched as the reference for future LHC combinations. This fits the digest’s EFT-as-default-language theme. Caveats are candid: chiral partners are assumed equal-strength and lepton flavors share common WCs to keep the fit tractable; gluon (c_tG) and photon (c_tA) operators are included only “for completeness” given the multilepton channel’s weak sensitivity; and a 50% uncertainty on tt̅W reflects a known modeling tension.

arXiv:2608.19708 — Tracing Vacuum Hadronization with Conserved Currents (Weiyao Ke et al.)

Ke, Li, Li, Liu, and Shao argue that color triality — the requirement that an anti-fundamental Wilson-line endpoint be screened by matter of conjugate triality — forces the net electric-charge, baryon-number, and strangeness flows into a jet (or celestial region) to satisfy a jet-level Gell-Mann–Nishijima relation, ⟨Q_flow⟩_f ≃I_3,f + 12(⟨S_flow⟩_f + ⟨B_flow⟩_f). Because these are moments of conserved currents, they are IR-safe and renormalization-scale independent at leading power: any shift from the initiating parton’s charge is purely nonperturbative “defect-charge” screening. The net jet baryon number directly reads out the diquark-to-quark vacuum ratio, ⟨B_flow⟩_f ≃r_qq/(1+r_qq), and the strangeness flow encodes the strange-to-light ratio r_s.

Pythia 8.3 (Lund string) and Herwig 7.3 (cluster) validate the relations in e⁺e⁻ dijets across E_CM=50–1000 GeV: parton-level flows recover Q_f; hadron-level flows shift but obey the Gell-Mann–Nishijima diagonal in both generators. Scanning probStoUD recovers r_s≈ the input value across three independent slope projections; scanning probQQtoQ gives ⟨B_flow⟩ largely independent of the strange parameter, as predicted. This is the conserved-current-observable program (cf. the DELPHI one-point charge correlator) applied to hadronization microphysics, offering a flavor-resolved probe complementary to inclusive yield fits. Honest caveats: the extraction rests on a minimal one-quark/anti-diquark screening truncation (validated only to ∼9% by the event-level r_topology check), assumes light-flavor symmetry and independent flavor sampling, and the extracted r_qq deliberately does not equal probQQtoQ because of the state-dependent fragmentation history. Everything so far is generator-level; experimental tests are left to future work.

Citation radar

This week’s radar catches two very different flavors of “quietly essential” physics. One is a theory proposal riding the surging quantum-information-at-colliders wave; the other is the kind of infrastructure measurement that underwrites nearly every cross section the LHC produces. Both are accumulating citations fast for reasons that say something about the field’s current priorities: extending quantum-correlation studies to new systems, and pinning down the reference numbers everyone builds on.

arXiv:2606.30759 — Quantum Information of Photon Pairs at Lepton Colliders (Kun Cheng et al.)

Cheng, Han, Li, and Yan extend the collider quantum-information program to photon pairs, a system that pioneered entanglement and Bell tests at low energy but had not been tackled at high energy. Their trick is to exploit near-on-shell photon conversion (γ*→ℓ⁺ℓ⁻): in the small-virtuality limit the conversion factorizes from the hard process and the two transverse photon polarizations form an effective qubit, with linear polarization reconstructed from the dilepton azimuthal distributions. Using existing Belle data they project a 7.4σ CHSH violation, plus measurements of quantum discord (5.6%) and nonstabilizerness/magic (1.6%), and demonstrate consistency with the kinematic approach for virtual photons.

At ~7 citations in about a month, the pace reflects a crowded, fast-moving subfield rather than a singular result—the reference list itself is dominated by 2025–2026 quantum-information-at-colliders papers, many by overlapping author groups. The appeal here is a concrete, data-ready proposal in a new channel (photons) with a clean qubit reduction that the authors note extends to h→γγ and other spin-1 systems.

arXiv:2606.26832 — Precision luminosity measurement in proton-proton collisions at √s = 13 TeV with the CMS detector (Arzunik Gevorgyan et al.)

This is CMS’s legacy Run 2 luminosity measurement, delivering 0.73% precision on the full 2015–2018 pp data set (140.22 ± 1.02 fb⁻¹)—described as the most precise ever at a bunched-beam hadron collider. The paper details the van der Meer calibration machinery and a battery of new refinements: residual orbit-drift corrections from BPM data, a two-step tracker-to-nominal length-scale calibration, an improved luminous-region treatment of transverse nonfactorization, better beam-beam modeling, and combination of four independently calibrated luminometers (HFET, HFOC, PLT, PCC). Long-term stability is validated against the Z→μμ rate, with the extracted σ_fid = 708 ± 12 pb consistent with theory.

The citation logic here is structural, not provocative: luminosity is the normalization for every cross section and, as the paper itself notes, the dominant systematic in several CMS measurements. At ~5 citations in six weeks, it is on track to become the standard reference that Run 2 CMS analyses cite for their luminosity uncertainty—the number everyone downstream simply has to quote. Its sub-percent milestone also sets the baseline going into HL-LHC.

item.title: Thursday, August 20, 2026
item.description:
Deconfinement in oxygen, and CMS at large

No single anomaly anchors the day, but CMS supplies its spine — three papers ranging from heavy ions to EFT to trigger performance. The cleanest result is the first observation of baryon-to-meson enhancement in oxygen-oxygen collisions (arXiv:2608.18256), the Λ/K⁰_S ratio showing the coalescence/radial-flow signature of a deconfined medium in a genuinely small system — the payoff the season’s OO and small-system flow program (EPOS4 scaling, ALICE ultra-central) has been building toward. Around it sit two takes on LHC Higgs-sector excesses, a collider quantum-information program that has moved past entanglement into “magic,” and a scatter of new dark-matter detection concepts.

Themes

CMS on multiple fronts

Beyond the OO result arXiv:2608.18256, CMS reports the most stringent aTGC/EFT bounds to date from WW/WZ single-lepton production with merged-jet reconstruction (arXiv:2608.18245) — another entry in the season’s steady drift toward EFT as the default language for diboson searches — and documents deep-learning heavy-flavour jet identification in the high-level trigger (arXiv:2608.18331), the unglamorous infrastructure behind the HH→4b and VBF/tt̅ H programs.

Two roads to an LHC excess

Dobrescu et al. arXiv:2608.18506 show a 10-GeV-scale ALP with h⁰→A_hA_h→(gg)(γγ) can reproduce the 3.5σ CMS diphoton excess near 13.6 GeV, with a 4g companion mode giving wide two-prong jets. Separately, Uttayarat et al. arXiv:2608.18738 propose Hγ, Hj, Hjj channels to distinguish mixing from leptophilic production behind the 146-GeV eμ excess. Two excesses, two concrete follow-up strategies — worth flagging together as the kind of loose corners current data can’t yet close.

Quantum information beyond entanglement

The collider-QI thread the memory has tracked all season takes two fresh turns. Li et al. arXiv:2608.19095 study “quantum magic” (nonstabilizerness) in QED and electroweak scattering, finding — as in earlier lab-basis work — that the physical weak mixing angle sits near the value minimizing magic production, and now tracking how the helicity basis changes the count. Yamagishi arXiv:2608.18732 argues genuine tripartite entanglement uniquely selects gauge- and diffeomorphism-invariant theories where bipartite measures were ambiguous — an extension of the entanglement-selects-symmetry line to three particles.

New handles for dark matter

Three distinct detector ideas. Matas et al. arXiv:2608.18204 give the first ab-initio calculation of DM-electron scattering in quantum dots, proposing an array of tuned morphologies whose relative rates form a “barcode” discriminating interaction operators — a genuinely new method. Scopel arXiv:2608.18609 argues JUNO’s mass plus annual modulation can reach world-leading sub-GeV spin-dependent sensitivity via the Migdal effect, and Kyriazis et al. arXiv:2608.18200 turn X-ray binary disk heating into an axion-electron probe competitive with XENONnT.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.18256 — CMS’s first observation of baryon-to-meson enhancement in OO; deconfinement signatures in a small system, the season’s OO program paying off.
  • arXiv:2608.18245 — CMS’s most stringent aTGC bounds to date from merged-jet WW/WZ; EFT as the standard diboson language.
  • arXiv:2608.18506 — Dobrescu et al. fit the CMS 13.6-GeV diphoton excess with a 10-GeV ALP from Higgs decays; a clean, testable story.
  • arXiv:2608.19095 — Quantum magic in electroweak scattering, with the weak mixing angle again near a magic-minimizing value; QI moving past entanglement.
  • arXiv:2608.18204 — Quantum-dot “barcodes” for DM-electron scattering; a novel, industrially-scalable target concept with operator-discrimination power.

From the community

The AICE proto-collaboration (57 institutions) posts a technical proposal for a ~100 m vertical atom interferometer in an LHC access shaft (arXiv:2608.18743), targeting ultralight DM and mid-band GWs — a mature, showstopper-free site pitched for LS3. On the tooling side, Kreczko’s FAST-HEP/Flow (arXiv:2608.18745) applies compiler techniques to declarative analysis workflows for long-term reproducibility.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.18920 Unified spectroscopy of P-wave flavor-sextet heavy baryons — Zhang et al. (hep-ph) — QCD sum rules tying the new Ξ_c(2882)⁰ into a coherent Ξ_c/Ω_c multiplet, with bottom-sector predictions.
  • arXiv:2608.18281 CosmoPyro: Gradients for GW Cosmology — Leyde et al. (astro-ph.CO) — differentiable hierarchical H_0 inference from GWTC-5 with Gaussian-process mass distributions; the autodiff-tooling wave reaching GW cosmology.
  • arXiv:2608.19019 Quantifying uncertainty in the neutron-star EoS — Gonçalves da Silva et al. (astro-ph.HE) — point-estimate MLPs understate high-density uncertainty; a caution that pairs with yesterday’s diffusion-model EoS.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.18256 — Observation of enhanced baryon production using strange hadrons in oxygen-oxygen collisions (CMS Collaboration)

CMS measured p_T-differential K⁰_S and Λ cross sections in OO and pp collisions at √(s_NN)=5.36 TeV (6.8 nb⁻¹ and 1.06 pb⁻¹), reconstructing the neutral strange hadrons via displaced two-track vertices. The nuclear modification factor R_OO for K⁰_S tracks that of inclusive charged hadrons, but Λ baryons are enhanced over both in the intermediate range 2<p_T<8 GeV; above 10 GeV all three converge and sit well below unity, consistent with nPDF effects plus parton energy loss. The headline is the Λ/K⁰_S cross-section ratio, which shows a pronounced enhancement in OO versus pp for 2.3<p_T<5.2 GeV, with a significance of 5.0–6.3σ across bins after accounting for correlated systematics. The ratio’s peak also shifts from p_T≈2.3 GeV in pp to ≈2.8 GeV in OO.

This is the first observation of a baryon-to-meson enhancement in OO — the quark-coalescence/radial-flow signature of a deconfined medium — in a genuinely small system, without the event-activity selections that complicate high-multiplicity pp/pPb interpretations. It caps the season’s OO program (CMS charged-hadron suppression, ALICE/ATLAS flow, Υ suppression) with a clean coalescence handle. The qualitative trends mirror PbPb and AuAu, though “less pronounced in the smaller OO system.” Caveats are honest: the Λ feed-down correction (∼18% at 5 GeV) relies on scaling ALICE Ξ/Ω ratios to the OO multiplicity, and the pp comparison inherits pileup and secondary-track corrections.

arXiv:2608.18245 — Search for anomalous couplings in WW and WZ production with single-lepton final states at √s = 13 TeV (CMS Collaboration)

Using the full Run 2 dataset (138 fb⁻¹), CMS searched for dimension-six EFT effects in boosted WV (WW/WZ) production where one W decays leptonically and the hadronic boson merges into a single large-R jet, tagged with mass-decorrelated ParticleNet (43% V-tag efficiency, ∼1% mistag). The m_WV spectrum (950–4550 GeV) is fit simultaneously with W+jets and tt̅ control regions, with the SM WV cross section floated (constrained to 0.32±0.1 times the NLO prediction — a notable tension the authors attribute to large LO-to-NLO K-factors and flag for dedicated measurement). Data are SM-consistent, and the analysis is statistics-limited.

The payoff is the strongest constraints to date on aTGC operators: in the HISZ basis the observed 95% intervals are c_WWW/Λ²∈[-0.93,0.93], c_W̃ WW∈[-0.37,0.49] TeV⁻², improving 30–70% over the previous 36 fb⁻¹ result. In SMEFT, c_W and c_W̃ reach [-0.08,0.08] TeV⁻² — the tightest triple-gauge bounds available — while the light-quark operators are competitive with, but not surpassing, inclusive-jet limits. This entrenches EFT with merged-jet substructure as the default diboson language, matching the digest’s theme. The main limitation is statistical, plus the approximate treatment of SMEFT operators potentially affecting background shapes (exact only in the HISZ triple-gauge case), and strong c_qq⁽³,1)–c_qq⁽³,8) degeneracy from insensitivity to color flow.

arXiv:2608.18506 — Axion-like particle at the 10 GeV scale: Higgs decays to wide jets and photons (Bogdan A. Dobrescu et al.)

Dobrescu and Roy build a renormalizable model where an ALP A_h couples to the SM only through the Higgs portal (-μ_Hϕ2v_ϕH^†H A_h A_h), with TeV-scale charge-2/3 colored scalars generating loop-induced A_h→gg (BR ∼99%) and A_h→γγ (BR ∼0.15%, fixed by 8α²/9α_s²). An effective portal coupling μ_Hϕ/v_ϕ≈10⁻² yields B(h⁰→A_hA_h)≈10%, below current undetected-width limits (<12% from ATLAS under |κ_V|≤1). The key claim: h⁰→A_hA_h→(gg)(γγ) produces an automatically boosted diphoton at M_A≈13.6 GeV that satisfies existing low-mass diphoton selections. Delphes-level cutflows give acceptance×efficiency of 12.7% (CMS) and 11.9% (ATLAS), and the model’s 1σ bands overlap both the CMS 3.5σ excess and the milder ATLAS ∼1.8σ at the same mass — reconciling the two, which under a singly-produced-ALP hypothesis appeared inconsistent.

If it holds, the CMS excess is not a lone diphoton resonance but a Higgs cascade with distinctive hadronic activity: the second A_h yields a wide jet J_gg with 2-prong substructure, and combining it with the diphoton reconstructs a 125-GeV peak (broad, from their simulation) — a background-suppression handle CMS/ATLAS could exploit. The companion h⁰→A_hA_h→4g mode (two wide jets, or (2+2)-prong when boosted) is unsearched. Caveats: the fit relies on order-of-magnitude kinematic estimates and simplified isolation proxies (large PTRatioMax to bypass rejection), not a full experimental reproduction, and the ALP mass formula requires tuned but “natural” cutoffs.

item.title: Wednesday, August 19, 2026
item.description:
Entanglement from gluons to gravitons

No single collaboration result anchors the day — the weight is spread across theory and phenomenology. The one thread that runs through it is the collider quantum-information program the memory has tracked all season, which surfaces three times: gluon-pair polarization correlations, three-qubit states in Bethe–Heitler scattering, and — from the gravity side — a third entry in the run of graviton-squeezing no-go arguments. The other cluster worth opening is a first phenomenological look at the quartic Higgs self-coupling via four-Higgs production. LHCb supplies the day’s clean null with a multimuon search.

Themes

Entanglement, from partons to gravitons

Yang et al. arXiv:2608.17685 compute the polarization density matrix of back-to-back gluon pairs, finding a maximally entangled Bell state in qq̅→gg at perpendicular emission (and a separable-but-nonzero gg→gg channel), extractable via the cos2ΔΦ energy-correlator modulation. Cao et al. arXiv:2608.18030 recast the familiar e+p→e+p+γ Bethe–Heitler process as a source of GHZ and W states. Meanwhile Fang et al. arXiv:2608.17015 show astrophysical graviton squeezing gets washed out at far-field detectors — global squeezing looks classically thermal locally. That is the third graviton-quantumness no-go in the memory, after Bao et al. and Miyauchi et al.; the wall keeps holding from new directions.

Higgs self-coupling and its CP structure

Papaefstathiou et al. arXiv:2608.16998 give the first HL-LHC study of quadruple-Higgs production in the eight-b-jet channel, setting simultaneous bounds on c_3 and d_4 — the quartic coupling, previously untouched by phenomenology. Two companion papers from Hernández-Juárez et al. probe CP structure in Higgs vertices: the SM one-loop CP-odd HWW form factor arXiv:2608.17106 (tiny, ∼10⁻⁵) and a forward-backward asymmetry in H→Zγ→f̅fγ arXiv:2608.17126 reaching 10⁻¹ at HL-LHC. Read alongside the ATLAS Higgs combination from 08-10, this is the coupling program pushing into the corners loose data can’t yet constrain.

Dark baryons and dense matter

A neutron-star cluster. Espriu arXiv:2608.17395 proposes Peccei-Quinn domain walls sweeping up quarks to seed primordial quark pellets as dark matter; Kalita et al. arXiv:2608.17409 track density-induced neutron→dark-baryon conversion in hyperon/Δ-admixed stars, with the pulsar-mass constraint disfavoring lighter χ. Panteleeva et al. arXiv:2608.17457 reconstruct the EoS with a denoising diffusion model that keeps prior, physics, and data separate — a clean template for ill-posed inverse problems. Blaschke et al. arXiv:2608.18038 add thermal twin stars as a supernova-explodability criterion.

Quantum simulation of gauge theory

Draper arXiv:2608.17115 gives an efficient block encoding of the plaquette operator in the irrep basis, removing a longstanding matrix-element scaling wall — a concrete advance for lattice-QCD quantum simulation. Hayashi et al. arXiv:2510.15493 argue for deconfinement-Higgs continuity in the SU(2) adjoint Higgs model.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.16998 — First HL-LHC phenomenology of the quartic Higgs self-coupling via four-Higgs production; opens territory single- and double-Higgs rates can’t reach.
  • arXiv:2608.17685 — Gluon pairs as a maximally entangled Bell state, read off from the energy-correlator azimuthal modulation.
  • arXiv:2608.17015 — Astrophysical graviton squeezing hidden in the far-field; the third quantum-gravity no-go in a month.
  • arXiv:2608.17457 — Diffusion-model EoS reconstruction that separates prior, physics, and data — future data reweight the posterior without retraining.
  • arXiv:2608.17855 — LHCb’s search for B→ four/six muons; a clean null with limits down to 6×10⁻¹⁰.

From the community

Grosso et al. arXiv:2608.17724 VERaiPHY — Validation & Evaluation for Robust AI in PHYsics — (hep-ph) opens a PHYSTAT series on statistical standards for ML in physics, a natural continuation of the season’s ML-methodology reckoning (the Living Guide, “Unknown Unknowns”). And Drees arXiv:2608.17864 Resolved Photon Processes: A Tribute to Rohini Godbole — (hep-ph) reviews resolved-photon physics in her memory.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.17676 Precise Measurement of δ at LBNE Using Only The Neutrino Sector — Ciuffoli (hep-ph) — trades the antineutrino sector for energy-dependence plus tight external priors on the other mixing parameters.
  • arXiv:2608.17681 An axion constraint from the diffuse supernova neutrino background — Mori et al. (hep-ph) — |g_ap|<1.3×10⁻⁹ from the recent Super-K DSNB hint, rivaling the SN 1987A bound without relying on a single event.
  • arXiv:2608.17491 An Exact Analytical Bridge from Complex Yukawa Couplings to Fermion Masses and CKM/PMNS Mixing — Lin (hep-ph) — a commutation hypothesis reducing the mass matrix to a closed-form diagonalization.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.16998 — Quadruple-Higgs boson production at the high-luminosity LHC (Andreas Papaefstathiou et al.)

First phenomenological study of gg→hhhh as a probe of the Higgs self-couplings, targeting the eight-b-jet final state at √(s)=14 TeV, 3000 fb⁻¹. The SM LO rate is tiny — σ(gg→hhhh)≃1.24×10⁻⁴ fb, a factor ∼350 below triple-Higgs — but the four-Higgs amplitude carries more quartic-coupling structure. An XGBoost classifier trained on 52 reconstructed observables, combined with a five-bin Poisson likelihood over the (c_3,d_4) plane (where c_3=κ_3-1, d_4=κ_4-1), yields simultaneous 95% bounds -10.3<c_3<11.2 and -222<d_4<234. The signal hypothesis actually combines hhhh, hhh+bb̅, and hh+4b; at the SM point it expects only 0.39 signal vs 21.9 background events. They also show hhhh→8b events with ≥6 tags feed the ATLAS hhh→6b region — with ∼89.5% tag probability the four-Higgs contribution can reach 10–100% of the hhh rate in parts of the plane.

Why it matters: the quartic coupling κ_4 is essentially unconstrained by phenomenology; this opens a channel and argues for jointly treating hhh and hhhh in inclusive multi-b analyses, complementing the ATLAS Higgs-combination push into loose corners. Caveats are heavy and honest: statistics-only limits, no detector/PDF/scale systematics, the hh+4b piece computed in m_t→∞ with only c_3 dependence, forced-splitting approximations, and sub-unit expected counts making asymptotic contours approximate. On a like-for-like basis the reach is comparable to ATLAS hhh in c_3 but weaker in d_4.

arXiv:2608.17685 — Entanglement of back-to-back gluon pair (Lei Yang et al.)

Full polarization density matrices for back-to-back gluon pairs in unpolarized pp collisions, computed at tree level for the qq̅→gg and gg→gg channels. For qq̅→gg, chirality conservation plus the MHV structure restrict the state to the |Ψ^±⟩ Bell sector; at perpendicular emission (θ=π/2) the pair becomes the pure Bell state |Ψ⁻⟩ — maximally entangled, concurrence 𝒞=-c_q(θ) reaching unity and S_max>2 (CHSH-violating) across 0<θ<π. In contrast, gg→gg is separable at all angles (𝒞=0, S_max≤10√(2)/9<2) but retains an appreciable linear-polarization correlation, c_g(π/2)=1/9≈11%. The observable link is the four-point energy correlator (E4C): contracting the pair density matrix with collinear splitting kernels maps the correlation onto a cos2ΔΦ azimuthal modulation between the two branching planes, with asymmetry 𝒜^κ=12(C_xx’+C_yy’)a^κ(n).

Why it matters: it extends the collider quantum-information program into the gluon sector, showing entanglement is generated purely by QCD helicity structure rather than a color-singlet vertex as in H→gg. The distinction between an entangled qq̅-initiated state and a merely correlated gg-initiated one is physically sharp. Caveat: the inclusive E4C signal suffers strong cancellations among qq̅ qq̅, qq̅ gg, gggg splitting channels; heavy-flavor tagging in both jets is needed to isolate QQ̅ QQ̅ and recover sensitivity. Extraction relies on the one-step collinear-splitting approximation, and the tagged sample is expected to be gg→gg-dominated with qq̅→gg as irreducible Born contamination.

arXiv:2608.17015 — Astrophysical Graviton Squeezing Can Be Hidden in the Far-Field (Cheng-Jun Fang et al.)

Using spatial quantum-optics methods extended to gravity, the authors compute the second-order coherence g⁽²⁾ accessible to a single far-field detector for gravitons emitted in a macroscopically squeezed state from a localized astrophysical source. An EFT description of squeezed-graviton generation yields Bogoliubov coefficients that inherit the source’s momentum envelope; the far-field projection (retarded pole extraction, angular stationary phase) shows a local observer effectively measures the asymptotic out-state along a single line of sight. The key result is a “same-cone” kinematic conflict: for a non-relativistic source the squeezing matrix peaks on the anti-diagonal (𝐩+𝐪≈0, back-to-back pairs), so the anomalous coherence M_D requires one internal momentum simultaneously near 𝐩 and -𝐩’ — incompatible for same-direction detection. The result is g⁽²⁾⁻²∼𝒪[exp(-2d ℰ/k_*)]+𝒪(L_D/r), so a globally squeezed state appears classically thermal (g⁽²⁾⁼²) locally.

Why it matters: this is the third graviton-quantumness no-go the memory has tracked (after Bao et al. and Miyauchi et al.), attacking macroscopic squeezing from the far-field-observability angle rather than production. Global squeezing does not guarantee local detectability. The authors frame it as a conditional no-go requiring three conditions: non-relativistic source, single localized detector, near-flat propagation. Each suggests an escape: relativistic/collinear sources (BH binaries, jets) could restore ℰ/k_*∼1; multi-detector networks probing both partner cones recover cross-correlations (feasible for a nearby solar axion halo); and strong-curvature lensing near compact objects can redirect back-to-back pairs into one cone. A concurrent independent preprint (ref. 51) reached consistent conclusions via a different framework.

item.title: Tuesday, August 18, 2026
item.description:
An old dataset, a new observable

The most distinctive work today is a three-paper package from Zhang et al. proposing and measuring the one-point charge correlator — a jet-free reformulation of the electroweak forward-backward asymmetry — extracted from archival DELPHI LEP-1 open data (arXiv:2608.14779, arXiv:2608.15357, arXiv:2608.15367). Around it sits a heavy hadron-spectroscopy load, from a lattice continuum-limit exotic-B_s result to Dudek’s review of gluonic excitations, and the usual dark-matter/axion spread. The day’s wild card is Gharibyan et al. arXiv:2608.14703, claiming evidence for parity violation in gravitational fields from HERA Compton-polarimeter spectra — an extraordinary claim that will draw extraordinary scrutiny.

Themes

A new electroweak observable from LEP open data

Zhang et al. formulate the charge flux of hadronic Z decays as a parity-odd sin(2θ) modulation measured directly against the beam axis, with no jet charge or reconstructed quark direction (arXiv:2608.14779 the theory Letter, arXiv:2608.15357 the first measurement, arXiv:2608.15367 the analysis note). The measurement, from just 61 pb⁻¹ of DELPHI data, agrees with PYTHIA and is pitched explicitly at the longstanding hadronic-asymmetry tensions. Nothing in recent memory anticipated this — it’s a genuinely new handle on precision EW, and the archival-data route is itself the point.

Hadron spectroscopy, from lattice to gluonic excitations

A dense cluster. Hudspith et al. arXiv:2608.15377 show the B_s0^* and B_s1 stay deeply bound in the continuum limit with a nonperturbatively-tuned heavy-quark action; Dudek arXiv:2608.16784 reviews glueballs and hybrids, complemented by Huang et al.’s constituent-gluon-model charmonium hybrids arXiv:2608.16250. Zhang et al. arXiv:2608.16875 ask whether the radial quarkonium ladder truncates, locating operational upper limits at n≈8–10 (cc̅). Dong et al. arXiv:2608.16266 tie X(3872) isospin breaking to a nearby partner pole. BESIII contributes throughout — the Σ⁰→Λe⁺e⁻ Dalitz decay arXiv:2608.16076, ψ(2S)→pp̅ phase arXiv:2608.15074, and new Σ⁰Σ̅⁰η modes arXiv:2608.16214.

Dark matter and axion searches

XENONnT arXiv:2608.15149 reports a null for magnetic and spin-independent inelastic DM using novel directional/kinematic selections on the recoil-plus-delayed-photon topology. Feng et al. arXiv:2608.15699 argue xenon experiments can beat Borexino on monochromatic 5.49 MeV solar axions via e⁺e⁻ pair production. Rounding out: IndIGO-D deci-Hz ultralight-DM projections arXiv:2608.15240, an ALP mono-photon channel at a muon collider arXiv:2608.15656, and a dark-charge-conjugation analysis of rare D⁰ decays arXiv:2608.15275.

QCD precision and methods

Generet et al. arXiv:2608.14793 propose projected energy correlators on the recoil against a Z/γ as a jet-algorithm-free precision-QCD benchmark, with the first NLO+NNLL matched LHC predictions. Boughezal et al. arXiv:2608.15898 establish calculable kinematic dependence of hadronization in DIS 1-jettiness event shapes; Lange et al. arXiv:2608.16744 present two-loop tensor reduction for OpenLoops.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.15357 — First measurement of the one-point charge correlator (with theory in arXiv:2608.14779); a new, jet-free EW precision observable from LEP open data.
  • arXiv:2608.14703 — Gharibyan et al.’s claimed evidence for gravitational parity violation from HERA polarimetry; extraordinary, and worth reading skeptically.
  • arXiv:2608.16875 — A first quantitative estimate of where the radial quarkonium ladder truncates; a sharp, testable challenge to the qq̅ picture.
  • arXiv:2608.14793 — Energy correlators in V+X as a clean precision-QCD benchmark, first NLO+NNLL LHC results.
  • arXiv:2608.15149 — XENONnT’s inelastic-DM search with novel directional cuts; a clean null across GeV–TeV.

From the community

Agarwalla et al. arXiv:2608.15231 Deep Earth imaging through neutrino and seismic tomography — Agarwalla et al. (hep-ex) — a report from the DENSITY 2026 mini-workshop bridging seismology, geochemistry, mineral physics, and neutrino physics; interdisciplinary field-building rather than a result.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.14785 Unveiling Neutrino Nature with the Diffuse Supernova Background — Manno et al. (astro-ph.HE) — DSNB as a Dirac/Majorana discriminant via resonant chirality flips, given magnetic moments ≳10⁻¹⁴μ_B.
  • arXiv:2608.14794 Radiative corrections to neutron β decay with explicit Δ(1232) — Gialidi et al. (hep-ph) — the EM axial-coupling shift halved versus the Δ-less result; relevant to lattice-vs-experiment g_A.
  • arXiv:2608.16783 Quantum Simulation of QCD in Axial Gauge — Yao (hep-lat) — polynomial qubit and gate scaling for 3+1D SU(3) with fermions by solving Gauss’s law away.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.15357 — First measurement of the one-point charge correlator in e⁺e⁻ collisions at √(s)=91.2 GeV with DELPHI Open Data (Jingyu Zhang et al.)

Zhang et al. deliver the first-ever measurement of the one-point charge correlator — the net electric-charge flux 𝒬(θ) into the detector as a function of polar angle relative to the e⁻ beam — from 61 pb⁻¹ of archival DELPHI Open Data (46 pb⁻¹ in 1994, 15 pb⁻¹ in 1995). This is a jet-free, hemisphere-free, IRC-safe reformulation of the hadronic forward-backward asymmetry: the parity-odd cosθ coupling structure shows up directly as a sin(2θ) modulation in the charge-weighted track density (tracks with p_T>2 GeV, 20°≤θ≤160°). Detector effects are handled in two stages — a PYTHIA 8.3-based correction for track-finding, fakes and charge misID, then a data-driven tag-and-probe measurement of the residual data–MC charge-misreconstruction bias in Z→τ⁺τ⁻ events, where charge conservation fixes the probe’s true sign. The fully corrected result exhibits the expected sin(2θ) shape, negative in the forward hemisphere, crossing zero at 90°, and agrees with PYTHIA 8.3 within uncertainties.

Why it matters: this establishes experimental viability of a genuinely new precision-EW handle, one whose relation to the Z couplings is not mediated by jet-charge model dependence — the very ambiguity blamed for the persistent A_FB^b tension. The construction extends to heavy-flavor currents where tensions are largest, and prefigures Tera-Z programs at FCC-ee/CEPC. The honest caveat is prominent: this is a proof-of-principle, not a competitive extraction. Systematics (27.6%/35.6% at θ=55°/125°) dominate over statistics and are set by the τ control-sample size; the parity-odd bias component is bounded, not measured to vanish. Sagitta and photon-conversion calibrations are the named next steps.

arXiv:2608.14703 — Evidence for parity violation in gravitational fields (V. Gharibyan et al.)

Gharibyan et al. analyze 314,896 Compton spectra from the HERA transverse polarimeter (2004–2007), tagged by 514.5 nm laser helicity, and report a laser-helicity-dependent asymmetry in the Compton-edge energy (ω_max=13.9 GeV) of A=(4.89±0.52)×10⁻⁵, claimed at 9σ. Within a phenomenological framework where the gravitational coupling acquires a helicity-dependent term G_s=G+(𝐬·𝐏/P)ΔG_𝒫, the modified energy-momentum relation shifts ω_max oppositely for the two helicities, and the γ² amplification factor sets the sensitivity. They translate the asymmetry into a helicity-dependent gravitational-potential difference ΔU_𝒫=(1.71±0.036±0.187)×10⁻¹⁴, i.e. ΔG_𝒫/G=(5.7±0.6)×10⁻¹⁰ using summed local potentials (dominated by the Virgo Supercluster). The signal is isotropic in right ascension (constant fit checked against 64 bins), which they argue excludes Lorentz-violating vector theories, and they estimate instrumental false asymmetries from transverse/longitudinal beam polarization and linear-light contamination to be sub-dominant.

Why it matters: if real, this would be the first high-energy test of a discrete symmetry in gravity showing violation, with speculative implications for galactic rotation curves via a chiral-gravity shift of the 21 cm line — potentially bearing on dark matter. But this is an extraordinary claim resting on a 5×10⁻⁵ edge shift in a polarimeter never built to measure absolute energy asymmetries. The authors themselves flag “hidden systematic factors”: helicity-dependent detector gain (estimated opposite-sign from bremsstrahlung fits, but uncorrected due to unknown beam offsets on an inhomogeneous calorimeter) and helicity-correlated laser spatial jitter convolved with the lepton phase space. The digest’s “read skeptically” is well-earned.

arXiv:2608.16875 — Truncation of the Radial Ladder in Heavy Quarkonia (Wen-Xuan Zhang et al.)

Zhang, Luo and Liu ask whether the radial excitation ladder of quarkonia terminates, solving a screened relativized Godfrey–Isgur Hamiltonian for cc̅ and bb̅ via the Gaussian expansion method (N_max=20, r_max=30 fm) up to n=14. Screened confinement replaces the linear term’s unbounded rise with a plateau M_∞=m_1+m_2+b/μ+c, giving limiting masses of 4.74 GeV (cc̅) and 11.67 GeV (bb̅). Crucially, while masses saturate — adjacent gaps dropping below 10 MeV — RMS radii keep diverging to ∼10–50 fm, an order of magnitude past the confinement scale. This “mass–radius decoupling” defines a breakdown of the qq̅ picture. A threshold criterion (min gap <10 MeV with radius increments >3/2 fm), corroborated by CUSUM/two-segment changepoint analysis of log(ΔR/ΔM) and a resolvability index χ_n=ΔM_n R_n collapsing below unity, locates operational upper limits at n≈8–10 for charmonium (D-waves first, then P, then S) and n≈12–13 for bottomonium. Staged χ² fits give RMS mass residuals of 34/24 MeV (10/4 MeV for low-lying states), with the charmonium screening length μ⁻¹≈1.4 fm inside the lattice string-breaking range.

Why it matters: this is the first quantitative answer to a long-standing spectroscopy question, and it is directly testable — no new charmonia should appear above ∼4.7 GeV, and BESIII/Belle II/LHCb can probe this. Caveats are candidly stated: high-n bottomonium shows round-off artifacts; the thresholds are empirical; and the truncation value is model-input-dependent (alternative fits give 4.61–4.83 GeV). Formal parameter errors are not quoted. The manuscript was substantially AI-drafted (Grok, GPT-5.4), per the authors’ declaration.

item.title: Monday, August 17, 2026
item.description:
Flavor, precision not tension

After a week where the flavor front ran on anomalies, today it runs on consolidation. LHCb posts an improved ϕ_s from B⁰_s→J/ψπ⁺π⁻ (arXiv:2608.14119), landing squarely on the SM; Huang et al. arXiv:2608.14341 supply the last missing factorization ingredient for b→sℓℓ at leading power — the theory-side counterpart to the C_9 story that peaked mid-week; and a kaon global fit (arXiv:2608.14474) folds in the new K⁺→π⁺νν̅ and LFU observables. The standout curiosity is elsewhere: Alves et al. arXiv:2608.13736 argue neutrino oscillations are not blind to absolute mass after all. A lighter day overall, weighted toward theory and tooling.

Themes

Flavor: penguins, kaons, and a clean φs

Three complementary entries. LHCb’s arXiv:2608.14119 gives ϕ_s=-0.041±0.017 rad in the full combination — precise and SM-consistent, a null against the week’s flare. Huang et al. arXiv:2608.14341 complete the twist-3 three-particle B-DA contribution to B→{K,π}ℓℓ at NLO, exactly the theory control the C_9 interpretation needs. D’Ambrosio et al. arXiv:2608.14474 show KOTO-II can discriminate the two surviving NP minima in the kaon sector, with NA62 complementary.

ML tooling meets model misspecification

Three ML papers, with a rare conceptual center. Cruz-Martinez et al. arXiv:2608.13633 is a methodology piece on “unknown unknowns” — when misspecification is the discovery and when it must be absorbed (see community). Jia et al.’s ORCA arXiv:2608.13652 attacks the interpretability problem in anomaly detection via contrastive embeddings that support template attribution; Hermansen et al.’s Pairton arXiv:2608.14278 reframes decay reconstruction as iterative masked edge prediction, SOTA on hadronic tt̅.

Vector-like fermions at future e+e-

Two independent takes on VLFs as an e⁺e⁻ target. Liu et al. arXiv:2608.14195 study single first-generation singlet-VLL production, reaching 900 GeV (ILC) to 1400 GeV (CLIC) via boosted fat-jets. Marzo et al. arXiv:2608.14538 compute one-loop VLF effects on Higgs-strahlung and find Yukawa-driven scenarios shift σ(ZH) at the per-mille FCC-ee level — mixing-driven ones already killed by EWPO. This extends the season’s FCC-ee precision thread.

Axion cosmology and strong CP

Kitajima et al. arXiv:2608.13650 show axion isocurvature from inflationary fluctuations survives domain-wall scaling and annihilation. Benincasa et al. arXiv:2608.13692 use a dim-6 PQ operator to trigger a first-order transition with observable GWs. Liu et al. arXiv:2608.13796 tie θ̅=0 and quark mass hierarchies to non-Abelian modular invariance.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.13736 — Oscillations do carry absolute-mass information at NLO in m_i/E; JUNO reaches few-hundred-keV sensitivity to a novel mass combination. A genuinely surprising conceptual point.
  • arXiv:2608.14341 — The last missing leading-power factorization piece for b→sℓℓ; the theory side of the week’s C_9 story.
  • arXiv:2608.14119 — LHCb’s improved ϕ_s in B_s→J/ψππ, precise and SM-consistent.
  • arXiv:2608.14474 — Kaon global fit showing KOTO-II can discriminate viable NP scenarios; a concrete near-term target.
  • arXiv:2608.14538 — VLF loop effects reaching per-mille Higgs-strahlung shifts; Yukawa couplings, not mixing, as the FCC-ee target.

From the community

Cruz-Martinez et al. arXiv:2608.13633 Unknown Unknowns: Model Misspecification in Machine Learning for Physics (physics.data-an) — less a technique than a disposition: robustness against being wrong in unanticipated ways, framing detection and mitigation as an iterative loop. A natural companion to this season’s ML-methodology reckoning (the Living Guide, RooAgent).

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.14268 W+charm in GM-VFNS — Alanko et al. (hep-ph) — charge-ratio observable favors zero strangeness asymmetry (CT18A) over MSHT20/NNPDF4.0 against ATLAS data.
  • arXiv:2608.14419 NNLO QCD corrections to WWγ — Garbarino et al. (hep-ph) — +16% over NLO, uncertainties down to ±4%; a quartic-gauge-coupling input.
  • arXiv:2608.13710 Optical characterization of commercial PVT scintillators — Huggins et al. (physics.ins-det) — measured n(λ) shifts photon counts 7% versus manufacturer values; a Geant4 calibration reference.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.13736 — Beyond Δm²: Absolute Mass Sensitivity in Neutrino Oscillations (Gustavo F. S. Alves et al.)

The headline is conceptual: the oscillation phase, expanded beyond leading order in mᵢ/E, contains a term ∝ (mᵢ⁴−mⱼ⁴)L/E₀³ = Δmᵢⱼ²(mᵢ²+mⱼ²)L/E₀³, so oscillations do carry absolute-mass information through the mass-squared sum. The authors show this cannot be recovered from naive plane-wave prescriptions — equal-energy, equal-momentum, and various t↔L replacements disagree at NLO — and derive it properly with a wave-packet treatment that fixes each eigenstate’s mean energy/momentum from beta-decay kinematics (an effective two-body decay N_A→(N_B e)+ν̄). The production-dependent correction enters only at the per-mille level (E₀/m_A ≲ 10⁻⁴). Applied to JUNO’s 52.5 km reactor baseline, a χ² fit to ~9.5×10⁴ IBD events over six years yields sensitivity m₁ < 305 keV (1σ), 434 keV (2σ) with oscillation parameters profiled; the solar channel dominates because its broad dip lands in JUNO’s high-statistics band and survives energy smearing intact.

Why it matters: this overturns the textbook statement that oscillations measure only Δm². It is a genuinely new, mechanism-independent absolute-mass probe, sensitive to a different combination than beta decay (m_νe), 0νββ (m_ββ), or cosmology (Σmᵢ). The honest caveat is scale: at few-hundred-keV, this is ~10⁴× weaker than KATRIN (0.45 eV) and ~10⁷× weaker than cosmology (0.053 eV), and the sensitivity is limited by a degeneracy in which the NLO shift mimics a rescaling Δm₂₁²→Δm₂₁²(1+m₁²/2E₀²), broken only by the 1/E₀² energy dependence.

arXiv:2608.14341 — Enhanced Three-Particle Contribution to Electroweak Penguin B-Meson Decays (Yong-Kang Huang et al.)

Using SCET with two-step QCD→SCET_I→SCET_II matching, the authors compute for the first time the subleading-twist correction to B→{K,π}ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ from the three-particle twist-three B-meson distribution amplitude at NLO, plus new NNLO corrections to the spectator-scattering (C-type) and weak-annihilation topologies and the O(α_s) D-type spectator term. This is billed as the last missing ingredient for a complete leading-power factorization proof of the b→{s,d}ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ matrix element. The three-particle convolution integrals over the two soft momenta are shown to converge, and the new jet function J_C^(3P) is validated by a second, method-of-regions calculation. Numerically, the newly included leading-power effects shift both real and imaginary parts of the top-sector amplitude T_π⁰ by O(30%) in q²∈[1.5, 4.0] GeV², driven by cancellation among A- and B-type pieces; the largest phenomenological impact is on the direct-CP-asymmetry differences ΔA_CP(B→Pℓℓ), shifted 15–20% at large recoil, where the nontrivial strong phase of J_C^(3P) dominates.

Why it matters: this is the theory-side counterpart to the week’s C₉ story — tightening the leading-power factorization control that any short-distance NP interpretation of b→sℓℓ requires. The honest caveat is that it does not resolve the anomaly: branching fractions for B⁰→K⁰ℓℓ and B⁺→K⁺ℓℓ “remain in sharp tension” with Belle/CDF/LHCb/CMS at large recoil, and the new B⁺→π⁺ℓℓ predictions actually favor old LHCb data over the latest full-Run-1+2 result (1.1–2.5σ).

arXiv:2608.14119 — Improved measurement of CP violation in B⁰ₛ→J/ψπ⁺π⁻ decays (LHCb collaboration et al.)

LHCb performs a time-dependent, flavour-tagged amplitude analysis of ~94,000 B⁰ₛ→J/ψπ⁺π⁻ signal decays from the full Run 2 6 fb⁻¹ sample (38 fs decay-time resolution, 4.5% tagging power), extracting φₛ = −0.077 ± 0.034 ± 0.007 rad, |λ| = 0.993 ± 0.026 ± 0.007, and Γ_H = 0.610 ± 0.002 ± 0.004 ps⁻¹. The π⁺π⁻ spectrum is modelled with six resonances plus a nonresonant term — adding an f₂(1565) contribution to a small ~1.6 GeV peak relative to earlier work — with the CP-odd f₀(980) carrying 72.5% fit fraction. Combining with Run 1 gives φₛ = −0.046 ± 0.031 rad; folding in all other LHCb channels yields φₛ = −0.041 ± 0.017 rad (χ²/ndf = 35/30), consistent with the J/ψφ average and improving precision by ~15%.

Why it matters: against a week where the flavour front ran on anomalies, this is a clean null.
