The result sits squarely on the SM prediction φₛ^SM = −0.0376₋₀.₀₀₀₅⁺⁰·⁰⁰⁰⁶ rad, and no direct CP violation is seen (|λ| compatible with 1). The main caveat is explicit in the text: subleading penguin contributions are neglected throughout — externally constrained to a Δφₛ = 5.0 ± 4.6 mrad shift from B⁰→J/ψρ⁰ — and the production asymmetry A_P is fixed to zero (a ±2% variation is taken as systematic). Systematics remain subdominant to the 34 mrad statistical uncertainty on φₛ.

item.title: Friday, August 14, 2026
item.description:
LHCb’s CP-violation harvest

The day’s weight sits squarely on a trio of LHCb papers dissecting B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻ on the 2011–12 dataset (arXiv:2608.12612, arXiv:2608.12613, arXiv:2608.12614) — an amplitude analysis that lands six CP-violation phenomena as significant for the first time and reorders the Kππ S-wave picture in favor of QCD factorization. This lands the day after yesterday’s twin B-anomaly flare (C_9 transversity and the B→PP SU(3) fit); the flavor front stays hot, but this is measurement, not tension. Around it, a dense cluster of weak-scale dark-matter model-building, a tomographic-CP top paper extending the season-long QI thread, and two differentiable neutrino toolkits posted the same day.

Themes

LHCb’s charmless three-body CP violation

The three companion papers share the 3 fb⁻¹ sample but split the story: arXiv:2608.12612 delivers the amplitude analysis with three independent S-wave treatments (isobar, K-matrix, quasi-model-independent) that agree; arXiv:2608.12613 resolves the long-standing K^*_0(1430) S-wave puzzle by relaxing unitarity assumptions, eliminating the ad-hoc f_X(1300); and arXiv:2608.12614 is the headline — discovery of CP violation in ρ(770)⁰K⁺, first evidence in ππ rescattering and in a spin-3 resonance, and CP violation in S–P and S–D wave interference driven by long-distance dynamics. This is the data-side counterpart to yesterday’s semileptonic and non-leptonic anomalies.

Weak-scale dark matter, revisited economically

A notable pile-up of DM model-building. Bhattiprolu et al. arXiv:2608.12480 map the singlet-doublet fermion model across freeze-out, co-scattering, freeze-in and SuperWIMP, emphasizing the small-Yukawa regime where detection goes collider-only. Borah et al. arXiv:2608.12483 reuse singlet-doublet fermions for an inverse first-order EW phase transition plus radiative Dirac neutrino mass, and Belfkir et al. arXiv:2608.12646 present a new one-loop Majorana-mass topology with viable fermionic/scalar DM. Datta et al.’s spontaneous scoto-leptogenesis arXiv:2608.12497 extends the running baryogenesis/scotogenic thread.

Tomography turned toward CP

Perelstein et al. arXiv:2608.12463 use top-pair spin tomography to build CP-sensitive observables for (chromo-)electric dipole operators, reaching 40–200 TeV scales at the LHC/HL-LHC and 10–15 TeV at FCC-ee — beating traditional observables. This is the collider-QI program the memory has tracked from tt̅ to TauPolaris, now aimed at CP violation rather than entanglement per se.

Differentiable neutrino engines

Two autodiff oscillation packages the same day: Granger’s MANGO arXiv:2608.13429, which differentiates through geometry and Earth-shell densities for tomography and experimental-design metrics, and Eller et al.’s Newtrinos.jl arXiv:2608.12940, a modular Julia global-fit framework. Both bet on gradient-based inference as the default for the next round of oscillation analyses.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.12614 — LHCb: six CP-violation phenomena in B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻ established at once, including the first in wave interference and in a spin-3 state. The day’s result.
  • arXiv:2608.12463 — Perelstein et al. turn spin tomography into optimal CP-dipole observables; the QI program’s CP turn, with concrete FCC-ee/LHC reach.
  • arXiv:2608.12793 — BESIII’s space-like η’ transition form factor, sub-3% below Q²⁼¹.5 GeV² and a first at Q²<0.3 — a clean input for hadronic light-by-light in g-2.
  • arXiv:2608.13429 — MANGO: fully differentiable oscillation engine that gets all 369 Earth-model gradients at the cost of six parameters.
  • arXiv:2608.12480 — A clean map of singlet-doublet DM across all production mechanisms; likely the reference for the small-Yukawa regime.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.12616 Axion-Like Particle Search with a Hybrid Cherenkov-Scintillation Detector — Aguilar-Arevalo et al. (hep-ex) — CCM beam-dump ALP search, surpassing CCM120 with less exposure via optical discrimination.
  • arXiv:2608.13525 A pion-driven near-threshold enhancement in the π T_cc system — Brandão et al. (hep-ph) — a predicted πT_cc resonance at ~4055 MeV, molecule-as-building-block, searchable in D⁰D⁰π⁺π⁻.
  • arXiv:2608.12706 Scalar induced gravitational waves as probes of dark QCD — Feng et al. (hep-ph) — a dark-confinement crossover imprints a frequency-shifted SIGW distortion.
  • arXiv:2608.12467 Soft Collinear Effective Theory for Heavy QCD Axions — Bisht et al. (hep-ph) — SCET factorization for B→Ka, quantifying when spectator scattering matters.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.12614 — Observation of several sources of CP violation in B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻ (LHCb collaboration et al.)

Working the full 3 fb⁻¹ Run 1 sample (115,102 candidates, 88.7% purity), LHCb performs an amplitude analysis of B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻ with three independent treatments of the troublesome Kπ and ππ S-waves (isobar/GLASS, K-matrix, and a first-of-its-kind quasi-model-independent binning of two crossing partial waves). All three agree, and six CP-violation phenomena clear observation-level significance at once. The headline first observations: quasi-two-body CPV in B⁺→ρ(770)⁰K⁺, 𝒜_CP=+0.280±0.022±0.029 (minimum 5.9σ across S-wave models); and in B⁺→f_2(1270)K⁺, rejected at 8.2–9.1σ at amplitude level. First evidence appears for CPV in the elastic ππ-ππ rescattering S-wave below the 4π threshold (𝒜^S_CP=+0.665±0.032±0.053), in S–P interference with ρ(770) (5.4σ), in S–D interference near the f_2(1270) (≥4.4σ), and — a genuine first — in a spin-3 state, ρ_3(1690)⁰ (≥3.3σ).

Notably, no CPV is seen in ρ⁰–ω mixing, contrary to several predictions; this dilution explains why the fitted ρ(770) asymmetry exceeds the model-independent P-wave value (0.150±0.022). A large positive asymmetry immediately above ππ threshold resists all three models, hinting at sizeable cc̅-loop or isospin-2 contributions. Systematics are comparable to statistical uncertainties throughout — good model control, but a signal that Run 1 statistics can no longer fully exploit. This is the measurement-side counterpart to the season’s flavor anomalies, sharpening reference points for γ extraction and B→Kπ-type isospin sum rules.

arXiv:2608.12463 — Probing CP-violating top-quark dipole moments with tomographic observables (Maxim Perelstein et al.)

Perelstein, Shaik and Youn recast tt̅ spin tomography as a CP-violation search. Symmetry fixes which Fano coefficients a CP-odd (chromo-)electric dipole can populate: the normal polarization difference ΔB_n and the antisymmetric normal-plane correlations A_rn, A_kn, all exactly zero in the SM (three-loop suppressed). They compute the production density matrix in closed form for e⁺e⁻, qq̅ and gg, build the statistically optimal CP-odd observable O_opt=f_1/f_0 (proven to saturate the Cramér–Rao bound), and carry the analysis to Delphes detector level. Projected 95% CL reach on inverse couplings: 10–15 TeV for the electroweak electric dipoles d_γ,d_Z at FCC-ee (365 GeV, 3 ab⁻¹), and 40 (200) TeV for the top chromo-EDM at LHC Run 2 (HL-LHC) — exceeding the conventional triple/quadruple-product observables (e.g. the CMS O_1 search) used today. d_γ projects mainly onto A_rn, d_Z onto ΔB_n; the optimal weight combines them for ~40 TeV parton-level FCC-ee reach.

A sharp negative result accompanies this: they prove a no-go theorem that the top–antitop discord asymmetry Δ𝒟 (and geometric discord, steering asymmetry) vanishes identically for the dipoles, contradicting a recent claim that advertised it as a CP probe — the reported nonzero values are CP-even absorptive artifacts. Caveats: reach at FCC-ee threshold is diluted by poor top-direction reconstruction (∼40^∘, dilution factors 0.24–0.40); systematics are assumed subdominant, and the EFT-consistent linear-order truncation neglects dimension-eight-degenerate terms.

arXiv:2608.12793 — High-precision measurement of the space-like η’ transition form factor (BESIII Collaboration et al.)

BESIII measures the single-virtual space-like η’ TFF via single-tag two-photon fusion e⁺e⁻→e⁺e⁻η’ on 20.3 fb⁻¹ at 3.773 GeV, reconstructing η’→π⁺π⁻γ and π⁺π⁻η. The result spans Q²∈[0.1,6.0] GeV² in 18 fine bins, reaches better than 3% precision below 1.5 GeV², and provides the first direct determination at Q²<0.3 GeV² — filling the gap between BaBar (>4 GeV²) and L3 (<0.15 GeV², which inferred Q² indirectly from the η’ transverse momentum). Tight control of the untagged-photon virtuality (Q²_miss∈[0,0.08] GeV², with a +1.0% correction to Q²_miss=0) is the key improvement; total systematics run 2.5–4.7% on the cross section, halved on the TFF.

The extracted values are the most precise to date and lie systematically above earlier data — attributed to the larger, less-controlled Q²_miss of prior measurements. Crucially, the data agree with lattice QCD (BMW) and holographic (LMR) predictions while sitting above data-driven dispersive models. Since LQCD and holographic approaches also predict a larger a_μ^η’ than the data-driven evaluation, this input feeds directly into the hadronic light-by-light contribution to muon g-2 — where LQCD HLbL now runs ~50% above the 2020 white-paper number — and the authors flag that existing data-driven analyses may warrant re-evaluation. The result also constrains the η’ gluonic component and η’ production models.

Citation radar

This week’s radar points to the speculative frontier of flavor model-building, where a single-paper octonionic construction is drawing early attention less for a confirmed result than for staking out sharply falsifiable predictions in the neutrino sector.

arXiv:2606.27836 — Leptonic CP Conservation and the Quark CP Phase from Octonionic Flavor Structure (Bishnu Gupta Teli et al.)

Working within the octonionic unification programme — one Standard-Model generation realized on complexified octonions via the Clifford algebra 𝒞l(6), extended to three generations by G_2 automorphisms and ladder-operator rotors — Teli and Singh prove a localization theorem for where a CP-violating phase can live. Their central claims are asymmetric and clean: the quark (1,2) transport is the occupation flip of a single ladder mode, forcing A_d = A_u^* and the exact one-parameter law ϕ_12 = -2χ, with the programme’s geometric rotor sitting at the maximal, quadrature-balanced point |ϕ_12|=π/2. For leptons they prove a “reality theorem”: every charged-lepton and neutrino transport amplitude is real for the entire admissible transport class, so leptonic Dirac CP is conserved (J_ℓ=0, δ^ℓ_CP∈{0,π}) unless a Higgs “bridge” mixes the identity line with the lepton-flavor plane — the sole, uncomputed loophole. A minimality assumption on the neutrino Jordan spectrum (-δ_ν,0,+δ_ν) then selects inverted ordering, m_ββ≃19 meV and Σm_ν≃0.10 eV.

Notably, the authors themselves quantify “the lean,” conceding that current global fits disfavor their inverted-ordering-plus-conserved-CP package at roughly 3σ per axis, with DESI cosmology also in tension. The ~5 citations two months out most plausibly reflect internal traffic within this tightly-knit programme (many references are the authors’ own companion papers), amplified by the paper’s unusually explicit falsification table tied to JUNO, DUNE, Hyper-K, and next-generation 0νββ. The reason for broader uptake is not yet visible from the text; the appeal is a concrete, near-term-testable prediction rather than an established measurement. (The acknowledgments also flag heavy reliance on AI tools in the derivations.)

item.title: Thursday, August 13, 2026
item.description:
The B anomalies come back, from data

After a week of neutrino mixing numerology, the weight today swings to flavor — but from the data side, not model-building. LHCb posts a model-independent measurement of the B⁰→K^*0μ⁺μ⁻ transversity amplitudes arXiv:2608.12215 with the C_9 deviation landing at 4.3–4.8σ depending on binning, and Bouchard et al. arXiv:2608.11298 find the B→PP global fit under SU(3)_F off by 4.1σ, with SU(3)-breaking parameters that make no sense in the SM. Two independent hadronic/semileptonic B anomalies in one day is the story. Around them sit a precision NOvA antineutrino–hydrogen cross section, an FCC-ee Higgs-mass study reaching the natural width, and a clean Majoron EFT.

Themes

B-physics anomalies, data-driven

The LHCb amplitude analysis arXiv:2608.12215 is the one to open: rather than fitting angular observables in fixed q² bins, they reconstruct the transversity amplitudes from Legendre polynomials, letting global fits choose their own binning and disentangling hadronic contamination from a genuine C_9 shift — which survives at 4.3–4.8σ. Bouchard et al. arXiv:2608.11298 attack from the non-leptonic side: their B→PP fit demands ~1000% SU(3)_F breaking, worsening to ~5σ under theory constraints. Different sectors, same direction. Nothing in the recent memory anticipated a data-side flare-up of this size.

Neutrino cross-sections and Majorons

NOvA arXiv:2608.12293 delivers the most precise ν̅_μH→μ⁺ⁿ CCQE cross section to date (35,509 events, systematics four times below the flux uncertainty) — directly usable to constrain the absolute antineutrino flux. That speaks straight to last week’s DUNE cross-section-systematics warning (Puhan et al.): the field is starting to pin down the very inputs that were shifting sensitivities 25–30%. On the model side, Biggio et al. arXiv:2608.11522 build a Majoron EFT from Type I/II/III seesaws with a single VEV, so invisible Higgs width, Majoron–lepton coupling and leptonic non-unitarity all become locked relations — falsifiable even if the new states sit far out of reach.

Collider precision and EFT matching

Eysermans et al. arXiv:2608.12071 show FCC-ee can reach 4 MeV Higgs-mass precision in leptonic ZH recoil — comparable to the natural width, the enabling step for resonant electron-Yukawa production. This extends the SMEFT-precision thread the memory has tracked (Haisch’s NLL EWPO, Celada’s FCC-ee accounting). Dittmaier et al. arXiv:2608.11306 give a functional one-loop matching recipe for the Higgs singlet extension, noting the emergent EFT only maps to SMEFT at the cost of fermionic operators; Deng et al. arXiv:2608.12079 resum a quasi-collinear divergence in the missing-mass spectrum of invisible dark-photon production.

Dark matter and exotic-state searches

Two NaI(Tl) hardware papers land together — temperature-dependent SiPM readout arXiv:2608.11303 and the COSINE-100U encapsulation upgrade arXiv:2608.11678, both chasing lower thresholds for low-mass DM. LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA arXiv:2608.11620 excludes ultralight scalar/vector bosons via black-hole superradiance, and a mirror-neutron search arXiv:2608.12173 sets the first lab limit on peV-scale n–n’ splitting that beats the neutron-star-cooling bound.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.12215 — LHCb’s model-independent C_9 from transversity amplitudes, 4.3–4.8σ and binning-flexible; the flavor result of the day.
  • arXiv:2608.11298 — Bouchard et al.’s B→PP fit demanding absurd SU(3)_F breaking; a second, independent B-anomaly hint.
  • arXiv:2608.12293 — NOvA’s most-precise ν̅_μ–H CCQE cross section, poised to constrain absolute flux.
  • arXiv:2608.11522 — Biggio et al.’s Majoron EFT: seesaw scale falsified through locked relations, not direct production.
  • arXiv:2608.12071 — FCC-ee reaching 4 MeV Higgs-mass precision, the gateway to the electron Yukawa.

From the community

Xiao et al. arXiv:2608.11712 Physics of the Electron-Ion Collider in China — Bo-Wen Xiao et al. (hep-ph) lays out the EicC physics case, deliberately foregrounding newer directions — nucleon mass decomposition, energy-energy correlators, quantum information, ML — over the well-reviewed 3D-structure staples.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.11316 Particle Production, Equilibration, and Quantum Recurrences from Classical Fields — Cuntín et al. (hep-ph) — lattice λϕ⁴ as a quantum-computable route to non-equilibrium QFT, with Poincaré recurrences after equilibration.
  • arXiv:2608.11467 First polarized SDMEs in ω photoproduction — Hu et al. (nucl-ex) — CLAS pushes into the Regge regime, first measurements for -t>0.6 GeV².

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.12215 — Model-independent measurement of the transversity amplitudes of the B⁰→K^*0μ⁺μ⁻ decay (LHCb collaboration et al.)

LHCb reconstructs the full set of B⁰→K^*0μ⁺μ⁻ transversity amplitudes unbinned in q² over 1.1<q²<8.0 GeV²/c⁴, expanding each P-wave amplitude in four Legendre polynomials (32 parameters, S-wave as nuisance) fitted to 8.4 fb⁻¹. The orthogonality of the Legendre basis reduces amplitude correlations relative to earlier empirical parametrisations, and CP-averaged observables (S_5, A_FB, etc.) are then built as continuous functions of q². Systematics run 0.09–0.35 of the statistical error, dominated by kinematic/trigger corrections. Profiling in flavio with the Ref. [14] baseline binning gives Re(C_9^NP)=-1.17⁺⁰.21_-0.20, a 4.3σ pull; quartering the bins tightens to -1.17⁺⁰.19_-0.18 and 4.8σ.

The key point is methodological: because hadronic (long-distance) contributions and a genuine NP C_9 shift have distinct q² dependences, the unbinned amplitude reconstruction lets global fits choose their own binning and, in principle, disentangle the two. The C_9 deviation surviving this more flexible treatment — and growing with finer q² resolution — is exactly what one expects from a real short-distance effect rather than a mismodelled charm-loop contamination. Results agree with the latest binned angular analysis [14]. Caveat: the interpretation still fixes all other Wilson coefficients to SM values and imports SM hadronic nuisance parameters through flavio’s covariance; the significance is a one-parameter statement, and the amplitude fit assumes no scalar/timelike contributions and a uniform-in-q² S-wave. The disentangling of hadronic versus NP awaits improved theory predictions to compare against the measured amplitudes.

arXiv:2608.11298 — Anomalies in Hadronic B Decays (Marianne Bouchard et al.)

This BEACH 2026 proceedings summarises SU(3)_F global fits to B→PP (P∈{π,K,η,η’}) in the topological-diagram basis, using EWP-tree relations to reduce 10 complex amplitudes to seven effective diagrams (13 real parameters). Individually the ΔS=0 (χ²/dof=1.1/2, p=58%) and ΔS=1 (1.6/2, p=45%) fits are excellent, but the combined SU(3)_F-symmetric fit collapses to χ²/dof=43/17, a 3.6σ SM discrepancy. The cause: best-fit diagram magnitudes differ across sectors by ~10×, e.g. |T̃’/T̃|=13.1±2.1, |C̃’/C̃|=8.9±1.3 — nominally 1000% SU(3)_F breaking versus the ~20–30% (f_K/f_π-1) expected. Adding η,η’ (25 parameters) worsens the fit to 4.1σ; the B→VV extension exceeds 7σ.

Imposing theory-motivated constraints makes things worse, not better: forcing |C̃/T̃|=0.2 (QCD-factorisation colour-counting) against the fitted 0.85±0.12 pushes to 4.9σ, and setting the annihilation diagram Ã=0 (expected ∼f_B/m_B-suppressed, yet fitted ∼|T̃|) gives 5.2σ. The claim to near-rigour rests on the EWP-tree relations being modified only ~10% by neglected c_7,8. This is the day’s second, independent B-anomaly hint, from the non-leptonic sector. Caveat: it is a proceedings, results drawn from Refs. [6–9]; the central assumption is exact SU(3)_F with a fixed θ_η=19.5°, and the authors themselves flag that whether a genuine ~30% breaking could accommodate the data “has to be checked” — work in progress.

arXiv:2608.12293 — Measurement of the ν̅_μ–Hydrogen CCQE cross section using the NOvA Near Detector (The NOvA Collaboration)

NOvA isolates ν̅_μH→μ⁺ⁿ from the 10.8%-hydrogen scintillator/PVC near detector (1.2×10²¹ POT), exploiting the nuclear-effect-free kinematics of a free-proton target: two BDT discriminants (topological HitID, kinematic KineID) plus data-driven control regions yield 35,509 background-subtracted signal events — the highest-statistics (anti)neutrino–hydrogen sample ever. The result, σ=0.538±0.009(stat)±0.010(syst)±0.055(flux)×10⁻³⁸ cm² at ⟨E⟩=1.9 GeV, is the most precise total QEH cross section to date, superseding the 13±6-event BNL bubble-chamber measurement. The decisive feature: the combined stat+non-flux systematic (2.5%) is more than four times below the 10.2% flux uncertainty, so the measurement can invert the usual logic and constrain the absolute ν̅_μ flux.

This lands squarely on the digest’s theme: the same cross-section systematics that were shifting DUNE sensitivities 25–30% (Puhan et al.) are precisely what a nuclear-effect-free reference process pins down. The data-correction scheme is validated by 10,000 fake-data throws showing background predictions stable against ~60% MC variations, with k_cut factors anticorrelated with the model shifts. Caveats are candidly stated: QEH purities are only ~41%/36% and signal efficiencies 3.6%/4.8%, so the analysis leans heavily on control-region-driven background subtraction; FSI weights are derived solely from neutrino-mode inclusive CC data and applied unchanged to antineutrino mode. The flux uncertainty still dominates the cross section itself — the payoff is prospective, once this becomes a flux standard candle.

item.title: Wednesday, August 12, 2026
item.description:
A muon limit amid flavor numerology

The cleanest standalone result is a number: the Fermilab g-2 collaboration sets a new direct muon EDM limit, |d_μ|<1.1×10⁻¹⁹ ecm (arXiv:2608.11124), consistent with zero. Around it the day’s bulk sits in two familiar places — neutrino/flavor model-building (a second Barger commensurate-mixing paper in as many days, plus two seesaw constructions) and QCD matter (a first Bayesian extraction of baryon susceptibilities, small-system scaling, the ultra-central flow puzzle). The collider-QI thread the memory has tracked all season reappears in a concrete tool for tau polarimetry, and a small cluster of AQN/warp-drive papers supplies the exotica.

Themes

Flavor structure, from seesaw to numerology

Barger arXiv:2608.10312 follows up his π/12 model (08-11) with a broader claim: quark and lepton mixing both collapse onto powers of a single parameter ε=|V_ub|³/10 and a π/24-quantized “digital clock” unitarity triangle, again pinning δ_CP≃296^∘ (or 244^∘) for DUNE/Hyper-K to test. He is explicit that this is parametrization-level, no dynamics. On the seesaw side, Han et al. arXiv:2608.10062 build texture-zero structures where arbitrarily large lepton-number violation coexists with sub-eV masses, predicting accessible HNLs, while Akita et al. arXiv:2608.10123 show a lepton-asymmetry mechanism that lets HNLs evade the BBN bound and enter SHiP’s reach.

QCD matter and small systems

Pihan et al. arXiv:2608.10238 report the first Bayesian extraction of baryon-number susceptibilities from RHIC BES proton cumulants, with χ_2^B tracking lattice up to μ_B∼300 MeV and a hint of enhancement beyond — notably, the nonmonotonic Ĉ_3/Ĉ_1 needs no irreducible multi-baryon correlations. Alongside, EPOS4 scaling from Pb to O (arXiv:2608.10578), ALICE’s ultra-central v_3/v_2 puzzle arXiv:2608.11199, and vorticity effects on HRG yields arXiv:2608.10561 keep the small-system/transport program that ran through last week’s OO results ticking.

Collider precision and quantum information

Beyond the muon EDM, CMS posts the first dedicated four-top resonance search in the dilepton channel arXiv:2608.10148 (SM-consistent, vector mediators excluded to 850 GeV). Haisch et al. arXiv:2608.10064 push SMEFT electroweak precision observables to NLL with the full 210-coefficient dependence — the reference basis for future e⁺e⁻ global fits, continuing the SMEFT-precision thread (Celada’s FCC-ee accounting, 08-07). And Winterbottom et al.’s TauPolaris arXiv:2608.10961 uses conditional normalizing flows to reconstruct tau polarimetric vectors, distinguishing entanglement in H→ττ at 4.3σ and improving CP sensitivity 18% — the collider-QI program moving from top tomography into a deployable analysis tool.

Speculative dark-matter astrophysics

Zhitnitsky revives the axion-quark-nugget framework twice: to explain the VASCO “mysterious transients” as ball-lightning cousins arXiv:2608.10061, and to repurpose the LHC superfluid-helium cooling system as an AQN detector arXiv:2608.10761. Paired with a warp-drive atmospheric-signature paper arXiv:2608.10800, the day’s tail is unusually speculative.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.11124 — New direct muon EDM limit from Fermilab g-2 tracker data; the day’s one clean number.
  • arXiv:2608.10961 — TauPolaris: normalizing-flow tau polarimetry, with a 4.3σ entanglement discrimination in H→ττ; the QI program made practical.
  • arXiv:2608.10064 — Full NLL SMEFT electroweak precision observables across all 210 Wilson coefficients; the basis future global fits will build on.
  • arXiv:2608.10312 — Barger’s commensurate quark-lepton mixing, one parameter to the 18th power; numerology, but with a falsifiable δ_CP.
  • arXiv:2608.10148 — CMS’s first dedicated four-top resonance search in the dilepton channel.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.10112 Calibrated correlation between heavy-quark masses and HVP observables — Beltran et al. (hep-ph) — ties m_c,m_b and their a_μ contributions to one spectral function; m_c(m_c)=1267.1(6.8) MeV.
  • arXiv:2608.10826 Muon-tagged D_s1(2460)⁺ and D_s1(2536)⁺ decays — LHCb (hep-ex) — first D_s1(2536)⁺→D_sππ branching fraction and evidence of exotic D_sπ contributions.
  • arXiv:2608.10292 ALPHA Phase I plasma haloscope — ALPHA Collaboration (hep-ex) — wire-array resonators targeting 40–80 μeV post-inflation axions near KSVZ.
  • arXiv:2608.10988 High-energy e⁻e⁺ collisions with large-angle disruptions — Zhang et al. (physics.acc-ph) — a new ε≳1 regime legacy beam-beam codes miss.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.11124 — An improved direct limit on the muon electric dipole moment (2 Collaboration et al.)

The Fermilab Muon g−2 collaboration sets d_μ⁺⁼⁽⁻⁰.35±0.19_stat±0.34_sys)×10⁻¹⁹ ecm from its 2019–20 straw-tracker data (2.34×10⁹ positrons across Run-2, Run-3a, Run-3b), yielding |d_μ|<1.10×10⁻¹⁹ ecm at 95% CL — a factor 1.5 improvement on the BNL E821 limit. The measurement uses the traceback method: a muon EDM tilts the spin-precession plane, producing an oscillation in the average vertical decay angle ⟨θ_y⟩ that is π/2 out of phase with the anomalous precession. Data are fit in 8 momentum bins × 2 stations × 3 runs (48 measurements, average reduced χ²⁼¹.08), combined via BLUE. Combining with BNL tightens the bound to |d_μ|<0.98(0.86)×10⁻¹⁹ ecm at 95(90)% CL.

Why it matters: the result stays ~19 orders of magnitude above the SM prediction (∼10⁻³⁸ ecm), so it functions as a clean BSM null test on a CP-violating source independent of the anomalous-moment program, complementing the model-dependent indirect bound (1.9×10⁻²⁰).

Caveat, honestly flagged: this is systematics-limited, dominated (by far) by the vertical-alignment false-signal correction (3.12×10⁻²⁰, vs. 1.87 statistical). Notably, the analysis failed the initial soft-unblinding 3σ check, triggering the internal review that uncovered the vertical-misalignment and longitudinal-field systematics; a data-driven correction was then developed while still blinded. The alignment uncertainty is itself statistics-limited and should shrink with Runs 4–6 (2.5× the present dataset).

arXiv:2608.10961 — TauPolaris: reconstructing tau lepton polarimetric vectors with conditional normalizing flows (Daniel Winterbottom et al.)

TauPolaris estimates the undetected neutrino momenta in τ decays with a conditional normalizing flow (nine spline-coupling blocks, transformer conditioning network), modeling the full joint density p(ν|𝐜) rather than a point regression. This preserves the correlations between momentum components — crucially reconstructing the τ mass at the physical 1.78 GeV, where an MSE-trained transformer biases low and pushes the neutrino collinear with the visible τ. A gradient-ascent MAP estimate in the flow’s latent space gives per-event neutrino configurations with ~40% better angular resolution than the transformer and ~20% better than sampling. On simulated LHC pp collisions with Delphes+CMS-HPS detector modeling, three applications are demonstrated: distinguishing quantum entanglement from a classically-correlated null in H→ττ at >4.3σ (and Bell witness m_12 at 4.0σ) with 3 ab⁻¹; improving CP-violation sensitivity via ϕ_CP by 18% overall (up to 88% in 3π^±0π⁰–3π^±0π⁰, and enabling 3π^±1π⁰ reconstruction for the first time); and new polarimetric variables to suppress Z→ττ.

Why it matters: this moves the collider-QI program from top-quark tomography toward a deployable analysis tool, extending the optimal polarimetric-vector method to every τ decay topology (previously restricted to 3-prong modes with secondary vertices).

Caveats: entirely simulation-based, with hand-added track smearing to patch Delphes; the entanglement 4.3σ is an upper limit set by finite pseudoexperiments, and yields are extrapolated from a single BDT window assuming preserved S/B. The 𝒞/m_12 estimators are biased on finite data, requiring pseudoexperiment calibration.

arXiv:2608.10064 — Electroweak precision observables at NLL order in the SMEFT (Ulrich A. Haisch et al.)

Haisch and Stefanek upgrade SMEFT predictions for electroweak precision observables to next-to-leading-logarithmic accuracy by combining one-loop EW matching with two- and one-loop RG evolution from Λ to m_Z, leveraging the newly available two-loop SMEFT beta functions. A key methodological point, proven via the T-parameter contribution of the right-handed four-top operator Q_uu³³³³: two-loop matching is not needed for NLL — higher-order matching cannot generate ln(Λ/m_Z) logarithms, so one-loop matching plus NLL running suffices. The headline deliverable is numerical NLL expressions encoding the full dependence on all 210 independent Wilson coefficients (excluding only Q_H, which enters at NNLL), released as ancillary files, with explicit results tabulated for five benchmark operators.

Why it matters: whereas tree-level matching reaches only 23 operators, NLL running opens EWPO sensitivity to the entire operator set — including operators contributing only at two-loop order (Q_G, Q_HG, Q_uH³³), which have no one-loop EWPO effect at all. For the top chromomagnetic dipole Q_uG³³, the genuine two-loop L (green) terms actually dominate the L²/L (red) terms, driven by a large y_t³ beta function mixing into Q_HD. This is positioned as the reference basis for FCC-ee/CEPC global fits at sub-permille precision, continuing the SMEFT-precision thread.

Caveats: the framework is illustrated on current LEP/SLC fits and projections rather than delivering a full global result here; couplings are fixed at m_Z (differences are NNLL). The authors note complementary concurrent work (Mantani et al.; Born et al.), and stress that a complete analysis must retain both oblique and non-oblique observables.

item.title: Tuesday, August 11, 2026
item.description:
Flavor models and a quantum-gravity rerun

The day’s weight sits in the neutrino sector — a dozen-odd papers on textures, mixing predictions, oscillation systematics, and lepton-number violation. The cleanest standalone result is de Vries et al.’s arXiv:2608.07657 complete one-loop SMEFT RG analysis of neutrinoless double-beta decay, which turns operator mixing into the most stringent bounds to date on numerous dimension-seven operators. Set against that experimental-adjacent rigor, Miyauchi et al. arXiv:2608.08803 re-run the “can we see gravitons” argument that Bao et al. closed off on July 31 — the same coarse-grained-mode obstruction, now with a small opening for detector-side squeezing. Axions keep their steady uncoordinated spread, and low-energy detection hardware fills out the rest.

Themes

Neutrino flavor and oscillation observables

The load is broad but two papers stand out. Barger arXiv:2608.08394 proposes a π/12 model — trimaximal first-column mixing with charged-lepton μ–τ breaking — that pins δ=272^∘±2^∘ and predicts an ε_2 of opposite sign to the current central value, a sharp test Hyper-K resolves at 3σ. Puhan et al. arXiv:2608.08609 make the less glamorous but consequential point that DUNE’s cross-section model choice (HF-CRPA+BS over the TDR tune) shifts CP/octant sensitivity by 25–30% — systematics as decisive as the oscillation physics. Kakoti et al. arXiv:2608.07623 (modular two-zero textures), Razzaghi arXiv:2608.08179 (open-path geometric phases in layered matter), and Kar et al.’s honestly-labeled “reproducible negative result” arXiv:2608.07602 round out the model-building.

The quantum nature of gravitational waves, again

Miyauchi et al. arXiv:2608.08803 ask whether squeezing can witness a quantized GW, and reach the by-now-familiar verdict: source squeezing washes out in any realistic single-mode detector, and while a pre-squeezed detector state can produce a witness a classical field cannot, the signal is throttled by the graviton coupling. This is the second such no-go in two weeks, extending the Bao et al. arXiv:2607.27313 argument from haloscopes to gravity — the program is converging on a wall from multiple directions.

Axions from lab to lattice

Lynn arXiv:2608.07718 reports a real search: a photonic-bandgap cavity with sapphire shells reaching Q>10⁵, constraining g_aγγ over 10.25–10.45 GHz. Chen et al. arXiv:2608.08602 show small-instanton effects across KSVZ models can break the standard m_a–f_a–g_aγγ relation, opening new search regions; Masjuan arXiv:2608.08209 flags correlated large-N_c low-energy constants relevant to U(3) axion phenomenology.

Low-energy detection hardware

A cluster on pushing thresholds down: CMOS image sensors for reactor CEvNS arXiv:2608.07676, the SuperEM sub-meV architecture for the CνB and light DM arXiv:2608.08592, and table-sized spin-transparent storage rings for EDM/axion searches at JLab arXiv:2608.08551.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.07657 — de Vries et al.’s full one-loop SMEFT RG for 0νββ; operator mixing gives the leading bounds on many dim-7 operators, beating meson decays.
  • arXiv:2608.08394 — Barger’s π/12 model: a falsifiable δ and ε_2 prediction Hyper-K can decide.
  • arXiv:2608.08803 — The quantum-GW no-go extended to squeezing; the detector-side loophole and why it doesn’t help.
  • arXiv:2608.07718 — A photonic-bandgap haloscope constraining new axion parameter space at 10.25–10.45 GHz.
  • arXiv:2608.08609 — DUNE cross-section model dependence shifting sensitivities 25–30%; a systematics warning worth heeding.

From the community

Krause et al. arXiv:2608.09531 The Living Guide of Machine Learning for Particle Physics — (hep-ph) freeze the six-year HEP-ML Living Review as an archival record (to 1 June 2026) and replace exhaustive bibliography with a curated, annotated guide — an honest admission that the field outgrew the comprehensive-list model.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.09203 Silent coverage failures in rare-event searches and a degeneracy index that predicts them — Pagno (hep-ex) — a Poisson–Fisher index diagnosing when model misspecification quietly breaks frequentist coverage in upper-limit searches.
  • arXiv:2608.09897 The Fate of Large Scale White Noise in Second-Order Cosmological Perturbation Theory — Ireland (astro-ph.CO) — rebuts a recent claimed IR enhancement in R_2 as an artifact of a linear Poisson relation.
  • arXiv:2608.08769 Near-threshold resonances in e⁺e⁻ annihilation — Salnikov et al. (hep-ph) — a review arguing final-state interactions explain essentially all known near-threshold enhancements.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.07657 — Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decays from Operator Mixing (J. de Vries et al.)

(abstract only) A complete one-loop SMEFT renormalization-group analysis shows that dimension-seven operators which do not contribute to 0νββ at tree level nonetheless generate sizable contributions via operator mixing under RG running. Accounting for the full one-loop evolution, the resulting 0νββ constraints become the most stringent bounds to date on numerous dim-7 operators — improving on limits from meson decays. The authors stress that effects beyond the first leading logarithm can dominate for specific operators and flavor combinations.

Why it matters: this is the day’s most experiment-adjacent rigor, converting the extreme sensitivity of 0νββ into a systematic constraint on the broader lepton-number-violating operator basis rather than a single-parameter mass bound. Caveat: only the abstract is available, so the numerical bounds and the flavor/operator specifics cannot be verified here.

arXiv:2608.08394 — The π/12 model: trimaximal first-column lepton mixing with charged-lepton μ–τ breaking (Vernon Barger)

Barger decomposes the first PMNS column into two independent conditions — the trimaximal norm |U_e1|²⁼²/3 (ε_1) and the μ–τ balance |U_μ1|=|U_τ1| (ε_2) — and shows that including the first JUNO result the data treat them asymmetrically: ε_1=+0.014±0.010 (consistent with zero at 1.4σ) while ε_2=+0.29⁺⁰.07_-0.13, large in central value but disfavoring zero only at 1.5σ because the profile likelihood in δ is shallow. A TM_1 neutrino sector with the electron-row condition |U_e2|/|U_e3|=2+√(3) fixes sin²θ_13=(2-√(3))/12=0.02233 and sin²θ_12=0.31811; a single charged-lepton 2–3 rotation (angle θ_e≃-1.9^∘, phase forced to α=0 by flavon alignment in an S_4×C_4×C_3×C_2 realization) generates ε_2=sin2θ_ecosα and pins δ=272^∘±2^∘, with ε_2=-0.066 — opposite in sign to the measured central value.

Why it matters: the framework is unusually falsifiable. The predicted δ sits 1.7σ from the current central value on the present profile likelihood, and Hyper-Kamiokande’s 20^∘ design precision resolves it at 3σ; a confirmed second octant (δ≈177^∘) would exclude it at >4σ. Caveat: the rigid mass sum Σm_ν=65.6 meV sits at/just beyond the DESI ΛCDM bound (64.2 meV), requiring dynamical dark energy if cosmology tightens; m_ββ=5.4 meV is below current 0νββ reach.

arXiv:2608.08803 — The Challenge of Detecting Quantum Nature of Gravitational Waves (Yu Miyauchi et al.)

Working with Gaussian states and a linear single-mode detector coupling, Miyauchi et al. use a squeezing witness W=|M|-N (W>0 certifies sub-vacuum quadrature variance impossible for any coherent-state mixture) to track whether source squeezing survives projection onto the detector-accessible wave-packet mode. Three source scenarios all fail: inflationary two-mode squeezing reduces to a thermal marginal (W_A=-N_A<0); a single-mode-squeezed stochastic background has random phases across coherence patches, washing out |M_A|; an isolated source is suppressed geometrically by W_A≤ΔΩ(ℓ_eff+1)²/8π, giving ΔΩ∼(3 km/100 Mpc)²∼10⁻⁴² for ground detectors unless emission is collimated to ℓ_eff≳10²¹.

They then show source squeezing is inessential: a pre-squeezed detector state acquires a positive witness W⁽Q)_b̃<sin²ϵ/2 from a quantized wave even when the incident mode is unexcited, whereas a classical c-number field only displaces the detector (W⁽C)_b̃=0). But the witness is throttled by the graviton–detector coupling ϵ̅=h_QG/h_th, which their strain-sensitivity table gives as ∼10⁻¹⁷–10⁻³³ across nHz–THz; detection needs ϵ≳N_trial⁻¹/4, and coherent integration (ϵ∝√(ωT)) reaches only ∼10⁻⁸.5 for a THz signal over a year.

Why it matters: this is the second no-go in two weeks, explicitly extending the Bao et al. (2607.27313) coarse-graining/weak-transfer argument to gravitational waves. The detector-squeezing loophole is real but doesn’t defeat the coupling suppression — the program’s wall is confirmed from another direction. Caveat: results are restricted to Gaussian states and linear single-mode coupling, which the authors argue is the optimistic case.

item.title: Monday, August 10, 2026
item.description:
The Higgs combined, the CMB rotated

Two precision results carry the day, from opposite ends of the field. ATLAS posts its full Run 2 Higgs combination arXiv:2608.07332 — inclusive signal strength 0.990⁺⁰.053_-0.051, now signal-theory-limited, plus κ_λ=1.3⁺³.1_-1.6, Γ_H=3.6⁺².1_-1.6 MeV, and a first ATLAS extraction of the running b-mass at m_H. And Eskilt’s joint ACT DR6 + Planck DR4 analysis arXiv:2608.06480 pushes the cosmic-birefringence hint to β=0.277^∘±0.057^∘ — 4.8σ, or 3.5σ after dust mitigation. Underneath sits the usual spread: a dark-matter detection-methods cluster, in-medium QCD, and hadron spectroscopy responding to a fresh LHCb state.

Themes

Two precision benchmarks

The ATLAS combination arXiv:2608.07332 is a reference document — every coupling, the self-coupling, the total width, and STXS in 44 regions, with sensitivities up 35% and the leading uncertainty now theoretical. It closes the incremental HH and tH updates the memory has tracked (last week’s bb̅ττ pull, the tH combination). Eskilt’s birefringence result arXiv:2608.06480 is the more provocative: two independent hints from ACT and Planck now cross-correlated into a 4.8σ parity violation, which — if it survives systematics — points at an axion-like Chern-Simons coupling. Read alongside CMB-S4’s N_eff forecast arXiv:2608.07453, the CMB is doing double duty as a particle-physics instrument.

Dark matter’s detection toolkit

A methods-heavy cluster, all hardware and computation. Li et al. arXiv:2608.06452 introduce a logarithmic Haar wavelet basis (and VectorPhonoDark) that cuts DM-phonon rate scans by orders of magnitude across six decades of momentum transfer. Liu et al. arXiv:2608.07136 propose an asymmetric spin-wave interferometer for 10⁻⁸–10⁻⁶ eV axions; Rosenzweig et al. arXiv:2608.07456 work out the optimal calibration-free observable for a dual-alkali comagnetometer; and Kodroff et al. arXiv:2608.06661 calibrate a compact β-momentum detector for the QuIPS levitated-nanosphere neutrino experiment. This continues the steady haloscope/reactor hardware drumbeat (VORTEX, TEXONO) rather than any single result.

Neutrino mass and light fields

Chathirathas et al. arXiv:2608.06460 test the hypothesis that neutrino mass comes from coupling to ultralight scalar DM, and use T2K/RENO/JUNO to cap the scalar-sourced fraction at 9–54% (JUNO reaching 1%) — a clean bound on a much-discussed mechanism. Around it: IceCube Upgrade sensitivity to Earth’s interior via atmospheric oscillations arXiv:2608.06543, and semi-analytic subgrid ansätze for supernova neutrino flavor conversion arXiv:2608.06464.

In-medium QCD and a new beauty-strange state

Tiwari et al. arXiv:2608.06731 solve the in-medium two-body T-matrix directly in the lab frame rather than the pair CM frame, finding 25–40% corrections to heavy-quark drag at low momentum — a real reduction in QGP transport-extraction uncertainty. On spectroscopy, Nowak et al. arXiv:2608.07268 read the new LHCb B_s0^*(5700)⁰ candidate as the chiral-doubling partner of the B_s⁰, and predict a still-unseen narrow 1⁺ state at 5747±2 MeV — a sharp, falsifiable follow-up.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.07332 — ATLAS’s full Run 2 Higgs combination; the new reference for couplings, κ_λ, Γ_H, and the running b-mass.
  • arXiv:2608.06480 — Cosmic birefringence at 4.8σ from a joint ACT+Planck analysis; the day’s most argue-worthy hint.
  • arXiv:2608.06731 — Lab-frame in-medium T-matrix shifts heavy-quark drag 25–40%; a concrete cut in QGP-transport theory uncertainty.
  • arXiv:2608.07268 — Chiral doubling reads the new LHCb B_s0^*(5700)⁰ and predicts a narrow 1⁺ partner at 5747 MeV.

From the community

Wojtsekhowski et al. arXiv:2608.06505 The Super Bigbite Spectrometer physics program — (nucl-ex) lays out the JLab SBS science case (elastic form factors, TMDs at high Q²) and a proposed solid-angle upgrade. Separately, the Nowak et al. spectroscopy paper is dedicated to the memory of Mannque Rho (1936–2026).

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.06515 Quantum Computers will constrain the Equation of State of Neutron Stars — Castaño-García et al. (hep-ph) — a canonical-quantization QCD Hamiltonian at finite μ, small-scale classical simulation as proof of concept.
  • arXiv:2608.07085 Extraction of Pion Unpolarized Quark and Gluon GPDs using Deep Neural-Networks — Puhan et al. (hep-ph) — physics-informed nets for pion tomography, validated against lattice.
  • arXiv:2608.06983 Leptogenesis via Resonant Sequential Dominance and TBC3 Mixing — Fodroci et al. (hep-ph) — a fresh entry in the running baryogenesis/leptogenesis thread.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.07332 — Combination of Higgs boson measurements at √s = 13 TeV and their interpretations by the ATLAS experiment (ATLAS Collaboration)

(Abstract only available.) ATLAS combines its full Run 2 (up to 140 fb⁻¹) Higgs measurements into a single reference, reporting an inclusive signal strength of 0.990⁺⁰.053_-0.051 — split as ±0.027 (stat.), ±0.024 (exp.), ⁺⁰.037_-0.035 (sig. theo.), ⁺⁰.016_-0.015 (bkg. theo.). The signal-theory term, dominated by missing higher-order QCD and parton-shower modelling, is now the leading uncertainty, so precision is theory-limited rather than statistics-limited. Sensitivities improve up to 35% over the previous combination. Combining single-Higgs and HH rates gives κ_λ=1.3⁺³.1_-1.6 ([-1.5,6.5] at 95% CL); the on-/off-shell rates yield Γ_H=3.6⁺².1_-1.6 MeV; and the H→bb̅ partial width delivers a first ATLAS running b-mass at the Higgs scale, m_b(m_H)=2.73⁺⁰.27_-0.25 GeV (MSbar). Kinematics are probed via STXS in 44 regions and interpreted in SMEFT.

Why it matters: this is the document every future coupling, self-coupling, and width comparison will cite, closing out the incremental HH/tH updates the memory has tracked. The signal strength sitting on unity at percent-level with theory now dominant sharpens where the community must invest — better fixed-order and shower predictions rather than more luminosity. The b-mass extraction demonstrates the Higgs as a running-mass probe. Caveats are structural: κ_λ and Γ_H remain broad, and the width relies on the on-/off-shell interpretation with its model assumptions.

arXiv:2608.06480 — Cosmic birefringence from a joint analysis of ACT and Planck (Johannes R. Eskilt)

Eskilt performs the first joint isotropic-birefringence fit to ACT DR6 and Planck DR4 polarization, exploiting cross-power spectra between the two experiments — which break the α+β miscalibration degeneracy in independent ways (Planck via Galactic foreground EB, ACT via optics-model priors on α, probing only ℓ>600). Sampling 17 miscalibration angles, three dust-EB amplitudes, and one β, the baseline gives β=0.277^∘±0.057^∘, excluding zero at 4.8σ. Crucially, positive EB appears in all three blocks separately: ACT×ACT (0.207^∘±0.073^∘), ACT×Planck (0.178^∘±0.078^∘, 2.3σ), and Planck×Planck (0.387^∘±0.094^∘). A conservative dust-mitigation test — masking Planck to 30% Galactic cut, keeping only ℓ>600, dropping foreground-dominated bands — still yields 0.236^∘±0.067^∘ at 3.5σ, so recovering β=0 requires both the α priors and the dust-EB model to fail simultaneously.

Why it matters: a frequency-independent β≠0 is the signature of an axion-like field coupled to electromagnetism via a Chern-Simons term — parity violation beyond ΛCDM, a direct window on the dark sector. Two independent hints now cross-correlate into the strongest signal yet. Caveats are candidly stated: the ACT×ACT block fits poorly (PTE 0.1%, an unexplained PA5 f090/f150 angle discrepancy the ACT team flagged), there is 1.5σ Planck–ACT tension in preferred β, the HFI priors are pre-flight, and the author’s pipeline underestimates ACT EB errors by ~7%. Unresolved systematics preclude a firm cosmological conclusion.

arXiv:2608.06731 — Laboratory-frame T-matrix and heavy quark drag in the quark-gluon plasma (Anurag Tiwari et al.)

Tiwari and He solve the in-medium two-body T-matrix directly in the medium rest (laboratory) frame rather than the pair center-of-mass frame, where the standard partial-wave reduction assumes the total pair-momentum P⃗ dependence is negligible. Since a thermal medium breaks Lorentz invariance and defines a preferred frame, physical observables must be built from lab-frame amplitudes. Exploiting the residual azimuthal symmetry about the P⃗-axis, they decompose the five-dimensional scattering equation into uncoupled integral equations for azimuthal components T_m, making it numerically tractable. For charm–light-quark scattering (m_Q=1.3 GeV, m_q=0.4 GeV, T=190 MeV, screened Cornell potential), the lab- and CM-frame amplitudes coincide at P=0 but diverge sharply as P grows: in non-forward regions |T_CM|² overshoots by 40–150% at P=1–1.5 GeV, and the relativistic normalization R_E further distorts the forward peaks. Folded into the drag coefficient, the lab-frame result exceeds the CM baseline by 25–30% at T=190 MeV (low p_Q) and 30–40% at T=258 MeV across most momenta.

Why it matters: heavy-quark drag is the key transport parameter extracted from charm-hadron flow to characterize the near-ideal QGP. A previously unquantified 25–40% frame-mismatch bias directly reduces the theory uncertainty in inferring QGP transport properties — a concrete tightening. Caveats: the calculation uses constant quark widths (Γ=100–200 MeV, itself a 20–30% spread) rather than a self-consistent spectral function, treats only heavy–light-quark (not quark–gluon) scattering, and has not yet been propagated through Langevin transport to observables.

item.title: Friday, August 7, 2026
item.description:
Can the CKM matrix do baryogenesis?

A theory-heavy day, with the weight in early-universe model building and the sharpest single claim a provocation: Bigaran et al. arXiv:2608.05269 argue that the usual “SM CP violation is insufficient for baryogenesis” verdict has a counterexample — a leptoquark with minimal-flavor-violating couplings whose decays generate the asymmetry from CKM phases alone, no time-varying parameters required. It anchors a three-paper baryogenesis cluster that ties directly to the flavor/CP top-down thread the memory has tracked for two weeks. On the experimental side the clean results are elsewhere: BESIII pushes a CLFV limit down three orders of magnitude, and ALICE turns three-proton femtoscopy into an effective 3→3 scattering experiment.

Themes

Baryogenesis and leptogenesis, three routes

Beyond Bigaran et al.’s CKM/MFV scenario arXiv:2608.05269, Kuckenberg et al. arXiv:2608.05279 revisit axion-driven spontaneous leptogenesis with fully flavor-dependent Weinberg-operator rates, finding standard Majoron misalignment under severe tension from late-decay dilution while strong/weak-sphaleron couplings survive near the GUT scale. Ogawa et al. arXiv:2608.05950 add dimension-8 CP-violating operators to sphalerogenesis and show loop-order counting can matter as much as mass-dimension counting. Three different mechanisms, all circling the same target — the origin of the baryon asymmetry — and the CKM-phase entry is the one worth arguing about.

Dark matter: fundamental limits and exotic signatures

Barker et al. arXiv:2608.05282 derive material-agnostic upper bounds on DM-electron scattering rates from condensed-matter sum rules, fixing a fundamental ceiling on any density-coupled direct-detection experiment from just ω_p, ρ_T and the static dielectric function. Davoudiasl et al. arXiv:2608.05284 propose matter-induced DM decay giving non-collinear double-muon vertices in IceCube/KM3NeT, and CMS arXiv:2608.05323 posts the first constraints on lepton-enriched semivisible jets, excluding a Z’ mediator up to 4.7 TeV. Bounds and signatures from both ends of the same problem.

Entanglement reaches Compton scattering

Hatta et al. arXiv:2608.05330 study photon-nucleon spin entanglement in Compton scattering, proving a no-go theorem (no entanglement in unpolarized scattering with real amplitudes) and then finding maximally entangled Bell states across the polarized kinematic plane — with the neutron’s electric/magnetic polarizabilities controlling whether entanglement exists at all. The collider-QI program the memory has followed from tt̅ tomography to hyperons now has a low-energy nucleon-structure entry, with entanglement pitched as a probe of nucleon EM properties.

QCD and hadron structure, the numerical ballast

ALICE arXiv:2608.05708 measures the three-proton correlation function in 13.6 TeV pp, isolating the p-p-p contribution and accessing the isospin-3/2 three-body continuum for the first time — femtoscopy as a genuine 3→3 scattering experiment. Around it: Ding et al. arXiv:2608.05752 reconstruct the chiral crossover line from Lee-Yang edge singularities, Albuquerque arXiv:2608.05322 systematizes QCD sum-rule window selection for a 2⁺⁺ fully-charmed tetraquark, and the ePIC collaboration arXiv:2608.05377 lays out its early-running EIC science case.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.05269 — Baryogenesis from CKM CP violation alone via an MFV leptoquark; a claimed counterexample to conventional wisdom, worth scrutinizing.
  • arXiv:2608.05330 — Photon-nucleon entanglement in Compton scattering, with a no-go theorem and neutron-polarizability control; the QI program’s low-energy turn.
  • arXiv:2608.05708 — ALICE’s three-proton femtoscopy as an effective 3→3 scattering experiment; first access to the isospin-3/2 three-body continuum.
  • arXiv:2608.06109 — BESIII’s η’→eμ CLFV search, <6.3×10⁻⁷, improving the previous bound by nearly three orders of magnitude.
  • arXiv:2608.05282 — A material-agnostic first-principles ceiling on DM-electron scattering rates; a fundamental limit for the whole direct-detection program.

From the community

Krämer et al. arXiv:2608.05812 Machine Learning is Good for Physics - and Vice Versa (hep-ph) — a reflection on how scientific AI challenges the methodology of fundamental physics, focused on statistical validation and generalizing theory. And Celada et al. arXiv:2608.05874 Descoped and Upscoped FCC-ee Running Scenarios in the SMEFT (hep-ph) — a concrete SMEFT accounting of what removing the top run, cutting beam power, or dropping interaction points costs the FCC-ee physics case; timely input for the collider-strategy debate.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.06163 Diffuse neutrino search with 2 years of KM3NeT/ARCA data — KM3NeT Collaboration (astro-ph.HE) — an all-sky flux fit (γ=3.0); the Galactic Ridge unconstrained at current sensitivity.
  • arXiv:2608.05795 / arXiv:2608.05801 Information-Theoretic Black Hole Entropy I & II — Kehagias (hep-th) — a Nernst-compatible entropy as a KL divergence, with area law as the leading 1/N term.
  • arXiv:2608.05401 HiggsTools for LHC Run 3 and Beyond — Bahl et al. (hep-ph) — updated BSM-scalar toolbox with di-Higgs and 13.6/14 TeV predictions.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.05269 — Baryogenesis via the CKM Matrix with Minimal Flavor Violation (Innes Bigaran et al.)

Bigaran, Krnjaic, Langhoff and Xiao construct an explicit counterexample to the folklore that SM CP violation is too small for baryogenesis. The model adds a scalar leptoquark 𝒮∼(3̅,1)_1/3×3_d̅ whose baryon- and lepton-violating couplings are built entirely from Yukawa spurions under MFV, so the only CP phase is the Jarlskog invariant J. Flavor breaking splits the three 𝒮_i masses (m_i²⁼M²⁽¹⁺γy_d_i²⁾), which lets tree–propagator interference in 𝒮_i decays generate a CP asymmetry per decay that peaks near resonance at ϵ_1^max≈0.15 — vastly above the naive Y_B∼10⁻²⁰ estimate. Crucially, no time-varying parameters are needed, distinguishing it from Mesogenesis. Two cosmologies are offered: low reheat (T_RH<130 GeV) with non-thermal 𝒮 production, requiring m_𝒮≲10¹¹ GeV; or high reheat with right-handed-neutrino ΔL=2 washout converting B+L into surviving B-L, viable for ϵ_i≳10⁻⁷.

Why it matters: it directly challenges the “SM CP violation is insufficient” verdict that motivates much BSM baryogenesis, and anchors the digest’s flavor/CP top-down thread. The honest caveats are prominent: the vertex-correction contribution vanishes and the entire asymmetry rides on the propagator term, which dies at mass degeneracy; the B-L-preserving decays require an extra ingredient (a late-decaying scalar or RH neutrinos) to escape sphaleron washout; and proton decay forces M≳10¹⁴ GeV for electron couplings (relaxed to ∼6×10⁹ GeV for τ). The authors explicitly frame it as a proof of principle, not a classified model.

arXiv:2608.05330 — Photon-nucleon entanglement in Compton scattering at low and high energies (Yoshitaka Hatta et al.)

Hatta and Martínez-Fernández extend the collider quantum-information program to elastic Compton scattering, treating the final photon helicity and nucleon spin as two qubits. Their central analytic result is a no-go theorem: in unpolarized scattering off any spin-12 target with real amplitudes, the partially-transposed density matrix cannot have a negative eigenvalue, so no entanglement is possible — proven generally, extending an earlier numerical electron-only observation. To generate entanglement they turn to polarized initial states. Below the pion threshold (ω<140 MeV) all six helicity amplitudes are real, yet with polarized beams they find a rich pattern of maximally entangled Bell states (and unitary equivalents, including a cyclic-anticorrelation Ψ^↻) distributed across the (θ,ω) plane, with proton and neutron showing distinct structure. They also compute the high-energy wide-angle regime at NLO in pQCD via GPD-based soft form factors, where an 𝒪(α_s) imaginary part gives entanglement everywhere but never maximal (λ_min≈-0.36 at best).

The striking physics point is diagnostic: for the neutron, where the Thomson term is absent, the electric and magnetic polarizabilities α_Eⁿ,β_Mⁿ control not just the pattern but the very existence of entanglement — setting α_Eⁿ⁼β_Mⁿ⁼⁰ makes the (x̂,x̂) configuration separable. This positions entanglement as a probe of nucleon EM structure, measurable at MAMI, JLab and a future EIC. Caveat: measuring final-state spin correlations is acknowledged as experimentally challenging, and the free-neutron extraction relies on deuteron subtraction, left to future work.

arXiv:2608.05708 — Three-baryon femtoscopy as an effective 3→3 scattering experiment (ALICE Collaboration)

ALICE measures the three-proton correlation function in 13.6 TeV pp collisions (Run 3, 53.1 pb⁻¹, with dedicated software triggers selecting triplets at Q_3<1.4 GeV/c, found once per 30000 minimum-bias events). A data-driven decomposition isolates the genuine p–p–p signal (79% of triplets) from Λ/Σ⁺ feed-down and misidentification backgrounds, with the source size ρ_0=(2.54±0.04) fm fixed by the companion two-proton measurement (r_0=1.27 fm). Comparison to hyperspherical-adiabatic three-body continuum calculations (AV18 + Coulomb, three-body force negligible by Pauli blocking) reproduces the data at n_σ=2.5. The headline sensitivity result: removing the NN p-wave interaction produces a 22.2σ disagreement, proving the correlation function resolves the partial-wave structure of the nuclear force. Two novel continuum signatures emerge — the nuclear interaction stays relevant up to grand-angular momentum K≤7 (far slower convergence than the two-body case, since large K still admits pairs in l_x=0), and the correlation stays above unity as it approaches the uncorrelated limit, the first experimental signature of an effective long-range attraction (∝ζ/ρ³, with ζ tied to the two-body scattering length).

This establishes femtoscopy as a genuine 3→3 scattering experiment and gives the first direct access to the isospin-3/2 three-body continuum, previously reachable only in isospin-1/2 via nucleon–deuteron scattering. Caveats acknowledged by the collaboration: the three-body Coulomb problem is treated approximately (no exact solution), feed-down modeling could be sharpened, and the 2.5σ agreement leaves room for theory improvement. The clear payoff is extension to p–p–Λ, p–p–Σ, p–p–Ξ for the strangeness sector.

Citation radar

This week’s radar leans toward methodological reckoning rather than new measurements. Two entries are LLM/ML tooling for physics workflows (one autonomous ROOT agent, one scaling-law study for jet generation); two are theory papers that reframe or correct existing formalisms (a control theorem for string inflation, a partonic rethink of bubble-collision particle production); and one proposes a new collider observable for quantum-correlation tests. The common thread: papers offering filters, corrections, and invariants that let the community decide which existing approaches to trust.

arXiv:2605.17318 — RooAgent: An LLM Agent for Root-Based High Energy Physics Analysis (Aman Desai)

RooAgent wraps PyROOT routines (inspection, cutflows, fitting, significance, CLs) as tools an LLM invokes from plain-language prompts, supporting both a LangGraph agent (GPT-4.1 via Copilot, DeepSeek-V3 via Ollama) and an MCP server for Claude. The paper benchmarks it on simulated pp→ZH events, a toy statistical search, and ATLAS H→ZZ^*→4ℓ open data, reporting 19/20 single-task successes with runtimes of 7–225 s and consistent numerical results across backends.

With ~6 citations since posting, its pull is timing rather than a headline result: the reference list shows a burst of “agentic AI for HEP analysis” papers in late 2025–2026, and RooAgent is a concrete, PyPI-installable entry in that fast-moving conversation. It is the kind of tool paper that accumulates citations by being cited alongside peers as evidence that LLM-driven analysis is becoming practical. The candid documentation of failure modes (case-sensitive tree lookups, model-dependent binning choices) also makes it a useful honest datapoint.

arXiv:2605.10197 — Controlled Penumbral Inflation from Monodromic Valleys (Pirzada et al.)

The paper derives a covariant “control theorem” for single-field inflation in the penumbra — the near-boundary region of complex-structure moduli space. It shows that a monodromy-preserving odd branch term rotates the light trajectory saxionically and produces a plateau when Δ≡p+2ν-q>0, with single-clock control requiring p<2 (or p=2 with a large entropy-mass prefactor). The benchmark predicts r∼10⁻³ with correlated running α_s≃-r/2, a target for LiteBIRD/CMB-S4, and provides an exactly solvable “invariant attractor equation.”

At ~6 citations in a few months, the appeal is that it turns a qualitative regime into a decision principle: a local EFT filter that flags which monodromic valleys deserve expensive global string embedding before that work is attempted. That framing — “filtered search” over the landscape — plus a falsifiable observable corridor gives both string phenomenologists and CMB modelers something to cite. Honestly, with such a specialized construction and dense formalism, some early citations are likely from the immediate collaborators/community around the cited penumbra literature (Lanza–Westphal, Grimm) rather than broad uptake.

arXiv:2605.13250 — Determining the Spin-Analyzing Powers via Invariants of the Spin Correlation Matrices and Probing the Bell Non-Locality at the Lepton Colliders (Dianwei Wang et al.)

For two-fermion production via single-mediator exchange at e⁺e⁻ colliders, the authors prove that Tr[C] of the spin correlation matrix is a rotation-invariant, scattering-angle-independent quantity, equal to +1, +1, -3 for gauge-boson, CP-even scalar, and CP-odd scalar exchange respectively. This lets one fix the product of spin-analyzing powers α_F_aα_F_b and reconstruct C from angular correlations alone — thereby evading the no-go theorem that otherwise blocks Bell tests at colliders. They apply it to e⁺e⁻→J/ψ→ΛΛ̅ at BESIII, finding CHSH-Horodecki violation for |cosθ_Λ|<0.44.

The ~5 citations reflect a hot, crowded subfield (the reference list runs past 130 collider-entanglement papers) where the no-go theorem on measuring spin-analyzing powers is the central obstruction. A claimed clean invariant that circumvents it is exactly the kind of tool the community was waiting for. Given the authors’ own dense self-citation cluster (Pei, Wu, Li et al.), a share of early citations is internal, but the observable’s generality gives it broader traction potential.

arXiv:2605.28940 — Neural Scaling Laws for Jet Generation (Oz Amram et al.)

This is the first systematic study of neural scaling laws for generative jet modeling, training the autoregressive OmniJet-α on ~180M real jets from the CMS-derived Aspen Open Jets dataset. Clean power-law scaling appears with model size N (with the SWD physics metric monotonically tracking the next-token-prediction loss), but scaling with dataset size and compute is weak and saturates early. The authors introduce a learnable window diagnostic and show it is dramatically smaller for jet NTP (W=3.2 nats, effective perplexity 1330) than for language (W=8.7, perplexity ~5), attributing the rapid saturation to QCD stochasticity and the mismatch between p_T-ordering and parton-shower causality.

At ~5 citations, the draw is a genuinely surprising negative-ish result on real detector data: scaling laws — the organizing principle of modern foundation models — behave qualitatively differently for generic QCD jets. That directly informs anyone planning large pretraining runs on collider data, and the “learnable window” concept is a portable, quotable diagnostic. The authorship overlap with the AOJ dataset and OmniJet ecosystem also naturally seeds citations from that active foundation-model community.

arXiv:2607.15279 — Particle production from bubble collisions (Anish Ghoshal et al.)

Ghoshal, Pal, and Strumia argue that the standard “off-shell” Schwinger-like formalism for heavy-particle production in ultra-relativistic bubble collisions is unphysical: the off-shell propagator Im Π(p²⁾ depends on field-space parameterization (manifesting as gauge dependence for vectors) and can give nonzero rates even in free theories, while the perfectly-elastic collision assumption parametrically overestimates hard production. They propose instead a partonic picture — Lorentz-contracted walls undergo near-free passage, and hard production arises from on-shell scatterings among wall quanta, giving rates suppressed by 1/γ² in the hard regime. They recompute scalar/fermion/vector/graviton cross sections and revisit dark matter, leptogenesis, and gravitational-wave implications, finding substantially reduced (though not negligible) yields.

The ~5 citations in a couple of months signal a provocative correction to a whole line of work (13 papers are grouped as using the flawed approach). Any claim that a widely-used mechanism was overestimated — and that DM/leptogenesis/GW signals must be revised downward — forces responses from exactly those authors, which is a reliable citation driver.

item.title: Thursday, August 6, 2026
item.description:
Neutrino handles and axion channels

The day’s weight sits in neutrino experiment design and a broad axion spread, with hadron spectroscopy as the numerical ballast underneath. DUNE recasts its oscillation sensitivity in a Bayesian framework and, as a byproduct, produces the first study of its sensitivity to the leptonic Jarlskog invariant (arXiv:2608.04059) — a parametrization-independent CP measure. Alongside it, two genuinely different experimental ideas: turning detector motion into interaction spectroscopy at Hyper-K (arXiv:2608.04091), and using positron-emitting neutrinoless modes to fingerprint the underlying lepton-number-violating operator (arXiv:2608.04187). The muon-collider thread persists in a minor key (a top-partner study, arXiv:2608.04399), and the automation drumbeat continues with an LLM-driven SMEFT tool.

Themes

Neutrino experiments reach for new levers

Three methods papers, no overlap. DUNE’s Bayesian MCMC (arXiv:2608.04059, DUNE Collaboration) maps four-parameter posteriors, shows a sharp θ23-octant gain from a reactor θ13 prior, and delivers the first Jarlskog-invariant sensitivity. Schwemberger et al. arXiv:2608.04091 argue that sliding IWCD through the off-axis beam breaks NSI degeneracies a single spectrum can’t. Harz et al. arXiv:2608.04187 use double-beta/electron-capture half-life ratios (NuDoubt++) to isolate right-handed currents.

Axions from every angle

A wide, uncoordinated spread. Chathirathas et al. arXiv:2608.04139 run kinetic-misalignment lattice histories into a post-inflationary attractor; Khan et al. arXiv:2608.04990 derive a thermal-alignment covariance bound; Gontcharov et al. arXiv:2608.04801 push the TRGB globular-cluster limit to g_ae<3.8×10⁻¹⁴; Debnath et al. arXiv:2608.05150 tie the PQ scale to seesaw neutrino mass across DFSZ/KSVZ; and Bręczewski et al. arXiv:2608.05082 extend the generalized Glauber theorem to axion/graviton detection — a formal companion to last week’s quantum-detection no-go debate.

Hadron spectroscopy, the numerical bulk

The count leans on exotics. Brambilla et al. arXiv:2608.04105 organize quarkoniumlike states above open-flavor thresholds in Born-Oppenheimer EFT with a single calibrated parameter — the most systematic multiplet assignment of the day. Around it: D_s1(2700) as a P-wave DK^ molecule (Lu et al. arXiv:2608.04069), in-medium open-charm vectors (arXiv:2608.04236), B_c→χ_c1 probes of χ_c1(3872) (arXiv:2608.04693), Glozman’s model-independent pion swelling above T_ch arXiv:2608.04563, and first CLAS N^ electrocouplings in the third resonance region (arXiv:2608.04997).

Production-side CP violation

Two proposals that read CP off the production vertex rather than the decay. Situ et al. arXiv:2608.04437 use the naive-T-odd Drell-Yan coefficients A_6,A_7 as SMEFT CP-dipole probes, reaching 𝒪(10⁻³⁾ at HL-LHC. Chang et al. arXiv:2608.05034 turn double-tagged forward protons into event-by-event photon polarimeters — a decay-analyzer-independent CP phase for spin-zero resonances.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.04059 — DUNE’s first Jarlskog-invariant sensitivity, plus a striking θ23-octant gain under a reactor θ13 constraint.
  • arXiv:2608.04091 — Detector motion as interaction spectroscopy: a genuinely new use for a movable neutrino detector.
  • arXiv:2608.05150 — A unified PQ-scale/seesaw analysis predicting axion-neutrino couplings across six neutrino-mass models — a testable common origin.
  • arXiv:2608.04105 — Brambilla et al.’s BOEFT survey of quarkoniumlike states; likely the reference organization for near-threshold exotics.
  • arXiv:2608.05034 — Production-side CP polarimetry from double-tagged protons; a clean, decay-independent handle on ALP-like resonances.

From the community

Hammad et al.’s arXiv:2608.04100 Language-Guided Hypotheses Generation for Sparse SMEFT Analyses (hep-ph) — an open, locally-run LLM fine-tuned on the SMEFT literature with retrieval from SMEFiT fits, proposing relevant operators with Fisher information. The latest entry in the running hep-ph-agent thread (LeWRON, CLVisc, SFitter).

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.04182 Bare effective potential and Goldstone boson anti-resummation — Martin (hep-ph) — a clean route around Goldstone IR problems, three-loop SM results included.
  • arXiv:2608.04362 CDM and SIDM interpretations of Cloud-9 — Ohana et al. (astro-ph.GA) — a RELHIC halo ∼7σ below the concentration-mass relation in CDM, eased to ∼3σ by self-interactions.
  • arXiv:2608.04102 Consistent Thermal Resummation with 2PI Methods — Banik et al. (hep-ph) — resummation-scheme choice visibly shifts the predicted phase-transition GW spectrum.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.04059 — A Bayesian approach to the long-baseline neutrino oscillation sensitivity of DUNE (DUNE Collaboration et al.)

DUNE recasts its established sensitivity inputs (the same flux, GENIE-based cross-section, and detector models as the 2020 TDR) into a Bayesian MCMC framework using MaCh3, with Adaptive Metropolis proposal tuning (~50× fewer steps than manual tuning, further reduced ~15× by 5% downsampling). This is explicitly not an updated sensitivity but a demonstration of what the Bayesian treatment adds. Two payoffs stand out. First, four-dimensional posteriors expose the strong sin²θ₂₃–sin²θ₁₃ correlation, producing two well-separated octant lobes; applying a reactor short-baseline θ₁₃ constraint post hoc via prior reweighting yields “a significant increase” in θ₂₃-octant sensitivity — the reactor prior breaks the appearance-channel degeneracy that otherwise smears the octant. Second, and the headline, this is the first study of DUNE’s sensitivity to the Jarlskog invariant J, a parametrization-independent CP measure derived trivially as a posterior of the sampled parameters. Studies span NuFIT 6.0 (NO, lower octant) and T2K-NOvA (IO, upper octant) Asimov points, δ_CP = 0, −π/4, −π/2, at 200 and 1000 kt-MW-yr.

Why it matters: it establishes the machinery for parametrization-independent CP inference and flexible constraint incorporation as DUNE moves toward real data, where robust systematic propagation and derived-quantity posteriors become essential. Caveats are honestly flagged: results are Asimov-based, mass-ordering sensitivity is not evaluated (assumed >5σ), θ₁₂ and Δm²₂₁ are fixed by Gaussian priors (no solar samples yet), and the ND is found to be systematics-limited with the current CC-inclusive binning.

arXiv:2608.04091 — Moving a Detector to Probe New Neutrino Interactions: IWCD at Hyper-Kamiokande (Thomas Schwemberger et al.)

Schwemberger and Takhistov reframe the movable IWCD not as a systematics-control tool but as an interaction spectrometer: sliding the same 300-ton water Cherenkov detector through the J-PARC off-axis beam (1°, 2.5°, 4°, peaking at ~1.0, 0.6, 0.4 GeV) exposes one target/apparatus to distinct incident spectra while keeping detector and interaction uncertainties correlated. Using the NCQE/CCQE event-rate ratio R^θ — in which common normalization largely cancels — they show that combining positions breaks vector-axial and normalization degeneracies that a single spectrum cannot, because the vector-axial interference term B carries a distinct energy dependence. Combining three positions with a 5% correlated normalization benchmark, they project 95% CL NSI sensitivities of −0.07 ≲ ε^{uA}{μμ} ≲ 0.06, −0.10 ≲ ε^{uV}{μμ} ≲ 0.12, and −0.05 ≲ ε^{udL}_{μμ} ≲ 0.05. Axial NC NSI, which do not contribute to the coherent matter potential, are the key complementary target to oscillation and high-energy scattering probes; the left-handed CC coefficient, which merely rescales CCQE, benefits little from multiple positions.

Why it matters: it gives movable/multi-position detectors a genuinely new physics use — spectroscopy of interaction structure — extensible to single-pion channels and other beams. Caveats are substantial and acknowledged: the analysis retains only the dominant ν_μ component, treats oxygen as an incoherent free-nucleon sum with a hard Pauli-blocking cutoff (yielding NCQE rates above NEUT), adopts an 80% flat NCQE efficiency and a schematic 5–10% systematic, and for light mediators the low-Q² cutoff removes most position-dependent discriminating power.

arXiv:2608.05150 — The QCD Axion and Neutrino Masses (Hridoy Debnath et al.)

Debnath, Fileviez Pérez, and Miller perform a unified analysis identifying the PQ-breaking scale with the neutrino-mass-generation scale (M_seesaw ~ v_S ~ f_a) across both DFSZ and KSVZ, for six mechanisms: Type-I/II/III seesaw, the Zee model, and colored seesaw I/II. For each they compute the E/N anomaly ratio and hence g_aγγ. Within DFSZ, Type-I, Type-II and Zee leave E/N unchanged from the minimal model (new fields are singlets or scalars), whereas Type-III’s fermionic electroweak triplets shift E/N (8/3→11/3 for DFSZ-I, 2/3→5/3 for DFSZ-II) — a measurable g_aγγ signature. In KSVZ, colored seesaw I and II predict E/N = 0 and 16/9, giving g_aγγ^I/g_aγγ^II ~ 14. A robust generic prediction across all frameworks is a derivative axion-neutrino coupling ∝ m_ν/f_a. If the axion is dark matter, a→νν decays produce a monochromatic flux peaked at E_ν = m_a/2 lying above both the CNB and solar thermal fluxes, with branching ratios and lifetimes sensitive to the neutrino mass ordering.

Why it matters: it ties the strong-CP solution, neutrino mass, and dark matter to one scale and yields correlated, testable handles — future haloscopes (ADMX, JWST bounds already excise parameter space), a distinguishing g_aγγ per mechanism, and a PTOLEMY-adjacent neutrino signal. Caveats: the axion-neutrino couplings are enormously f_a-suppressed, the neutrino-flux detectability is “very challenging,” and the seesaw–PQ identification is an assumed upper bound on f_a rather than a forced relation.

item.title: Wednesday, August 5, 2026
item.description:
The muon collider’s neutrino byproduct

The freshest thing today is a coincidence: two independent groups posted re-evaluations of the neutrino flux at a 10 TeV muon collider, and both conclude the intensity is far larger than earlier estimates — enough to make the machine an accidental neutrino factory. Around that, the collider-quantum-information program keeps spreading into new final states, ATLAS delivers a genuine first in forward-rapidity jet suppression, and the numerical bulk sits, as it did over the weekend, in hadron spectroscopy. One pointed reanalysis paper is worth flagging for anyone who cites the ATLAS doubly-charged-Higgs limit.

Themes

Neutrinos as a muon-collider byproduct

Burk et al. arXiv:2608.02714 find fluxes around the interaction region nearly two orders of magnitude above prior estimates for the latest 10 TeV design, with tau-neutrino events reachable in a ton-scale forward detector. Choi et al. arXiv:2608.02718 build a dedicated Monte Carlo (MINT) for the beam dynamics and forecast 𝒪(10⁹⁾ interactions per year in a ~3-tonne volume 5 km out, plus the secondary muons and wrong-sign backgrounds that come with it. A new thread — the neutrino-physics case for a machine sold as an energy-frontier precision tool.

Collider quantum information, still spreading

Ai et al. arXiv:2607.28346 show that missing neutrinos need not kill spin tomography: casting the visible measurement as a coarse-grained POVM, they prove that in τ⁺τ⁻→ππ+νν̅ only the antisymmetric C_nr-C_rn combination is unidentifiable, and give a template-free unfolding. Zhang et al. arXiv:2608.03131 compute Bell variable, concurrence and negativity for ΛΛ̅/ΣΣ̅/Λ_cΛ̅_c at BESIII. This is the same program that carried Erdogan et al.’s tt̅ tomography two days ago, now reaching hyperons and invisible final states.

Heavy-ion, forward and small

ATLAS arXiv:2608.03261 reports the first inclusive jet suppression at forward rapidity (2.8<|y|<3.6) in Pb+Pb, finding stronger suppression at 2.8<|y|<3.2 than in the central region — a new handle on the geometry and flavor dependence of energy loss. Pucillo for ALICE arXiv:2608.02874 adds first strangeness-enhancement results in OO, extending the “how small can QGP be” question that LHCb’s Υ and ALICE’s charm v_2 opened over the weekend. Fukushima et al. arXiv:2608.03945 dissect why longitudinal spin-polarization sign depends on the reference-frame formulation.

Hadron spectroscopy bulk

The day’s count leans on molecular and exotic-state model work: D^D̅^/B^B̅^ bound states via Bethe-Salpeter (Li et al. arXiv:2608.03104), Faddeev calculations for ϕNN/J/ψNN (Zhang arXiv:2608.03162), X(2370) as a glueball (Wang arXiv:2608.03362), and X(6900) nuclear photoproduction as a structure probe (Paryev arXiv:2608.03374). Plus real data: LHCb’s new B_c⁺→DX measurements arXiv:2608.03453, including a first observation.

Worth a look
