The design rests on three moves: commercial-off-the-shelf networking (an InfiniBand HDR fat-tree treating event-building as an all-to-all personalized exchange), second-scale host-memory buffering that eliminates incast without deep-buffer switches, and a “converged” node hosting readout, event-building, and GPU filtering together via zero-copy/RDMA. Algorithmically, a multi-event GPU scheduler batches ~600–800 events per sequence, with mixed-precision reconstruction (single precision for a truncated-region Kalman filter; half precision for VELO storage and SciFi seeding). They report 41 MHz peak combined throughput, 36% headroom over the 30 MHz requirement, and demonstrate a full EB+HLT1 integration test sustaining 160 GB/s memory and 115 GB/s PCIe per node with no performance drops.

Why it matters: this is the production endpoint of the month’s real-time-reconstruction wave (the July 17 GPU-Kalman work), and the comparison table makes the claim concrete — the highest software-processed data rate of any experiment, exceeding ATLAS/CMS (1.6 Tbps into software after a 300× L1 cut) and ALICE (7.2 Tbps). Removing the low-level trigger reduces selection bias by considering the whole event. It’s an engineering demonstration paper rather than a physics measurement; the throughput figures are commissioning-phase benchmarks.

arXiv:2607.20635 — What could an emerging Big Bang Nucleosynthesis discrepancy be hinting at? (Vivian Poulin et al.)

Using PRIMAT (rewritten in Python) with the Cooke et al. deuterium measurement (10⁵D/H = 2.527±0.030), the BBN-inferred baryon density ω_b ≃ 0.0219 sits ~2.1σ below the ΛCDM CMB value and ~3.1σ below the higher ω_b = 0.02272±0.00014 preferred in EDE fits — early-dark-energy solutions to H₀ generically raise ω_b and thus worsen the deuterium problem. The authors test three expansion histories against the EDE ω_b target: ΛCDM, a ΔN_eff extension, and a transient “very early dark energy” (vEDE) component peaking during deuterium burning. Constant extra radiation fails (Q_DMAP = 3.1σ, ΔAIC ≃ +1.2): it raises Y_p too efficiently at weak freeze-out. vEDE succeeds, because a boost localized at T_D ≃ 0.03 MeV shortens the residual deuterium-burning window (raising D/H at large ω_b) while barely touching ⁴He synthesis. The combined fit gives ΔH/H(T_D) = 0.087⁺⁰·⁰³⁶₋₀.₀₃₇, no residual tension (Q_DMAP = 0.7σ, ΔAIC ≃ −5.3).

Why it matters: this is the natural referee’s-follow-up to the H₀ World Cup — the very models that win on H₀ lose on primordial deuterium, and the resolution demands yet another light scalar, framed as an axiverse window at the BBN epoch. Caveats are candidly stated: the CMB is compressed to a single Gaussian ω_b likelihood (not a joint fit); nuclear-rate uncertainties enter only through tabulated MC errors; the discrepancy is partly rate-driven (PArthENoPE agrees better with the data), and the updated D/H = 2.508 softens the ΛCDM tension to 2.7σ.

arXiv:2607.21244 — Hubble tension: the shape wall (Miguel A. Sabogal et al.)

The standard no-go against late-time H₀ solutions is a normalization wall (BAO fixes r_d·H₀). This paper erects an independent shape wall: at fixed acoustic scale θ_s and sound horizon, δH₀/H₀ ≃ δI/I, where I ≡ ∫dz/E(z). Using Gaussian-process reconstructions of the dimensionless expansion rate E(z) from unanchored SNeIa (PantheonPlus, DESY5Dvk, Union3) and DESI DR2 BAO — marginalizing over the r_d·h amplitude to retain only shape information — they find E(z) can deviate at most ≈5–7% from fiducial ΛCDM. The directly-constrained low-redshift integral I_< (z ≲ 2.3) is pinned to the percent level: δI_</I_< ≲ 0.5% (68%), ≲1.5% (95%) across SNeIa+BAO combinations, mapping to (δH₀/H₀)_< ≲ 0.8% at 95%. Adding a model-guided estimate of the unconstrained high-z tail I_> (from ΛCDM/wCDM fits) yields a total δH₀/H₀ ≲ 2% (conservative) to ≲3.7% (maximally permissive) — versus the ≈9.3% needed to close the tension, leaving ≳4.3σ residual.

Why it matters: alongside Poulin et al., this is the day’s second wall against tension-solvers, and it is statistically stronger than the normalization wall since it survives redshift-independent BAO recalibration. The key methodological point — pointwise E(z) envelopes overstate freedom because integrating I preserves cross-redshift correlations — is well argued. Honest caveats: I_> bounds are model-dependent (not nonparametric); flat FLRW, smoothness, and the distance-duality relation are assumed. The explicit surviving loophole is new physics at z ≪ 0.01, below SNeIa reach.

Citation radar

This week’s radar splits cleanly between two currents. Three entries sit in gravitational-wave cosmology — phase-transition predictions, cosmological-collider loop signatures, and induced GWs from domain walls — reflecting a community still mining the early universe for signals across NANOGrav-to-LISA frequency bands. The other two are Feynman-integral technology: evaluating iterated integrals and solving canonical differential equations numerically. All five are young (a few weeks to two months) and each sits at ~5 citations, so these are early-momentum picks rather than established benchmarks. Where full text is unavailable I flag the guesswork.

arXiv:2605.15259 — TransitionListener v2.0: Robust gravitational wave predictions for cosmological phase transitions (Jonas Matuszak et al.)

No rendering was available, so this reads from title and metadata alone. The name signals a public code release: a “v2.0” update to a tool that maps particle-physics models of first-order phase transitions onto predicted stochastic GW spectra, with “robust” suggesting improved treatment of the notoriously uncertain transition parameters (nucleation rate, bubble-wall dynamics) that plague these forecasts. ~5 citations since mid-May. If the accumulation reflects anything, it is the standard pattern for phenomenology tooling: a maintained, ready-to-run pipeline gets cited by every follow-up model study that needs GW predictions without rebuilding the machinery. I cannot confirm the headline improvements from the text provided.

arXiv:2606.02744 — IterInt: Evaluating iterated integrals via differential equations (Gideon Baur et al.)

Text unavailable; I rely on the title plus a corroborating external reference. Notably, this paper is cited within Czakon–Tancredi (arXiv:2606.30354) below, which describes it as “a package that transforms iterated integrals into a differential-equation system and solves it numerically,” with the actual integration performed in C++ under a Mathematica interface. That framing — iterated integrals as the formal solutions of canonical differential equations — places IterInt squarely in the current push to make ε-factorized systems numerically tractable. ~5 citations since early June. The likely driver is the same one animating the whole subfield right now: a concrete, usable tool for evaluating the transcendental functions that appear beyond the polylogarithmic case, arriving just as multi-loop practitioners need exactly that.

arXiv:2605.21419 — Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-Handed Neutrino Loop (Jingtao You et al.)

No rendering available. The title places this in the cosmological-collider program, where heavy particles active during inflation imprint oscillatory, mass-dependent features in the primordial non-Gaussianity of curvature perturbations. The novelty signaled is a loop-level computation: right-handed neutrinos contributing at one loop rather than tree level, which is the natural way to probe fermions whose masses might otherwise leave no signal. This connects the collider formalism to leptogenesis-relevant physics, plausibly explaining early interest — it ties a fashionable inflationary observable to the seesaw sector. ~5 citations since May. Without the text I cannot verify the specific amplitude or the predicted signal strength.

arXiv:2604.25726 — Imprint of domain wall annihilation on induced gravitational waves (Rishav Roshan)

Roshan studies a minimal Z₂-symmetric real-scalar extension of the SM in which domain walls, made unstable by a small bias term, annihilate and dump most of their energy into the long-lived scalar. If that scalar dominates before decaying, it drives an early matter-dominated era that dramatically amplifies scalar-induced GWs (working in the non-linear regime via the Fernandez et al. simulation framework), while its eventual decay injects entropy that dilutes the direct domain-wall signal. The headline result is a distinctive double-peaked spectrum — a higher-frequency peak from wall annihilation, a lower-frequency peak from enhanced induced GWs — with both peaks potentially visible to THEIA and μARES, so detection in one band predicts the other.

The paper’s appeal is the correlated multi-band signature from a single symmetry-breaking event, a cleaner falsifiable target than isolated-source studies. ~5 citations in roughly two months, likely from the active domain-wall/induced-GW community (many self-citations to King, Borah, and collaborators are visible), reflecting momentum rather than settled impact.

arXiv:2606.30354 — Solution of Canonical Differential Equations for Integrals on Arbitrary Geometries (Michał Czakon et al.)

Czakon and Tancredi tackle a real bottleneck: canonical ε-factorized systems beyond the polylogarithmic case have connection matrices containing transcendental functions — elliptic or Calabi-Yau periods — for which closed forms are often unavailable, blocking numerical evaluation. Their key observation is that these functions are not arbitrary: since the original master integrals obey rational differential equations, so do the transcendental building blocks. Adjoining these auxiliary equations yields an enlarged purely-rational system solvable by standard numerical ODE methods, with correct analytic continuation guaranteed automatically. They demonstrate on the 220 two-loop masters for di-jet and γ+jet production through a heavy-quark loop — 16 square roots plus elliptic periods — and ship a lightweight, commercial-software-free C++ package built on Boost’s Bulirsch-Stoer solver, achieving sub-second double-precision evaluations.

~5 citations since late June. The draw is a general, deployable recipe that sidesteps the hardest obstacle to using canonical bases in realistic amplitudes: no special-function implementation needed, universally applicable to any Feynman integral. Given the surge of parallel efforts (Baur–Duhr, Liu–Zhang) it references, this lands in a hot and crowded space, positioned as the production-oriented option.

item.title: Thursday, July 23, 2026
item.description:
Spin polarization, Beijing and CERN

Two experiments made the day, both by measuring polarization in channels that were hard to reach. ATLAS reports 4.0σ evidence for a longitudinally polarized Z in electroweak W^±Zjj production (arXiv:2607.20246) — the direct sequel to last week’s doubly-longitudinal ZZ observation, pushing polarization fractions into the VBS-adjacent sector. At the other end of the mass scale, BESIII debuts a genuinely new trick: using secondary scattering off spectrometer material to measure final-state nucleon polarization, and turning it into the first determination of the relative phase between the proton’s psionic form factors (arXiv:2607.19948). Around these, a UHE-neutrino tension paper hardens the ANITA/KM3NeT/IceCube puzzle, and the neutrino-systematics thread the memory has tracked resurfaces on the energy-reconstruction side.

Themes

Polarization and EM measurements at colliders

The ATLAS WZjj result arXiv:2607.20246 (f_X0=0.32±0.09, SM-consistent) extends the electroweak-symmetry-breaking polarization program that produced the ZZ milestone on July 15 — the doubly-longitudinal fraction is still only bounded (<0.12). CMS delivers the most precise LHC measurement of γγ→ττ in ultraperipheral PbPb and tightens a_τ to [-0.039, 0.032] (arXiv:2607.20148). LHCb adds a clean null CP search in D⁺→ϕπ⁺ at the 10⁻⁴ level, plus a first hadron-collider look at the K⁰/K̅⁰π⁺ amplitude ratio (arXiv:2607.20276).

BESIII’s polarimetry gambit and a glueball claim

The pairing of arXiv:2607.19927 (proof of principle) and arXiv:2607.19948 (first relative-phase measurement) turns a general-purpose spectrometer into a large-acceptance polarimeter — a method with obvious reuse value across nuclear and particle facilities. Separately, BESIII argues the X(2370) is a flavor-singlet state and the dominant component of the lightest 0⁻⁺ glueball (arXiv:2607.20366), from the suppression of K^*(892)K̅. That continues the July heavy-hadron/glueball drumbeat (the N_f=1 glueball–ss̅ mixing result of July 21).

The UHE neutrino anomaly gets a number

Chattopadhyay et al. arXiv:2607.19487 do the joint ANITA-IV/KM3NeT/IceCube fit and quantify what has been a hand-wave: a diffuse power-law flux is in ~7.5σ tension, and even rare-transient populations stay at 5.9σ, given IceCube’s null. This sharpens the KM3-230213A thread the memory has followed (the July 14 grand-unification read of that event). Adjacent, Garcia-Garcia et al. arXiv:2607.19461 show light neutrinos must be kept in HNL t-channel amplitudes — their destructive interference kills LNV signatures, redirecting searches to lepton-flavor-violating eμjj.

Neutrino energy reconstruction, again

Lachner et al. arXiv:2607.20419 show calorimetric energy reconstruction carries an interaction-model-dependent bias from detector non-linearities (Birks quenching, recombination) — ~7–9 MeV in scintillator, 11–18 MeV in argon — separate from the missing-energy bias, and reducible with hybrid tracking+calorimetry. This is the same systematics anxiety as the Dolan review and T2K generator-spread work, now on the material-response side. JUNO’s ultrasonic source positioning (arXiv:2607.20354) and the ITk gamma-irradiation study (arXiv:2607.19936) round out the detector-hardware end.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.20246 — ATLAS finds a longitudinally polarized Z in WZjj-EW at 4.0σ; the direct continuation of last week’s ZZ polarization program.
  • arXiv:2607.19948 — First measurement of the proton psionic form-factor relative phase, via a novel secondary-scattering polarimetry that any spectrometer could adopt.
  • arXiv:2607.19487 — Puts a number on the UHE-neutrino puzzle: 7.5σ tension for a diffuse flux, 5.9σ even for rare transients.
  • arXiv:2607.20366 — BESIII argues X(2370) is the lightest 0⁻⁺ glueball; the first flavor-singlet light hadron above 1 GeV.
  • arXiv:2607.20148 — CMS’s most precise LHC a_τ constraint from ultraperipheral γγ→ττ.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.20337 Nucleon unpolarized second Mellin moments in the continuum limit — Alexandrou et al. (hep-lat) — quark and gluon gravitational form factors at physical masses, continuum-extrapolated.
  • arXiv:2607.19750 SymbolFit: automated parametric function discovery — Tsoi et al. (hep-ex) — symbolic regression rediscovers the published dijet/UA2 fit functions from CMS/ATLAS spectra.
  • arXiv:2607.19463 Higgs Couplings at a Future Wakefield Collider — Fraser et al. (hep-ph) — a γγ option reaches muon-collider-like Higgs sensitivity, sidestepping positron acceleration.
  • arXiv:2607.19469 Can the universe be matter-dominated after a supercooled transition? — Mansour et al. (hep-ph) — lattice study says no, not immediately; the equation of state is set by wall γ_⋆.

Deep dives

The Cross Section

arXiv:2607.20246 — Evidence for longitudinally polarised Z bosons in electroweak W^±Zjj production (ATLAS Collaboration)

Abstract only. ATLAS reports 4.0σ evidence for a longitudinally polarised Z in electroweak W^±Zjj production, combining 140 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV and 164 fb⁻¹ at 13.6 TeV in the fully leptonic (e/μ) channel. The integrated fiducial fraction is f_X0=0.32±0.09, consistent with the NLO-EW Standard Model prediction. Upper limits at 95% CL of 0.19 and 0.12 are set on longitudinally polarised W and on doubly-longitudinal WZ events, respectively. The 13.6 TeV fiducial cross-section is measured as 0.374±0.077 (stat)±0.053 (syst)±0.009 (lumi) fb per lepton flavour.

Why it matters: This is the direct sequel to last week’s doubly-longitudinal ZZ observation, extending the electroweak-symmetry-breaking polarization program into the VBS-adjacent WZjj sector — the channel most sensitive to longitudinal-boson scattering that probes unitarization by the Higgs. That the single-longitudinal Z fraction sits squarely on the SM prediction, while the doubly-longitudinal component remains only bounded (<0.12), reflects the statistical reach of current datasets rather than any tension. The caveat is intrinsic: a 4.0σ result on f_X0 with ±0.09 precision and the merged two-energy dataset means the harder doubly-longitudinal target awaits Run 3 luminosity.

arXiv:2607.19948 — First Measurement of the Relative Phase between Proton Psionic Form Factors (BESIII Collaboration et al.)

What they did: Using 10.09×10⁹ J/ψ events, BESIII measured the normal polarization 𝒫_y of protons from e⁺e⁻→J/ψ→pp̅ by exploiting secondary pp elastic scattering off hydrogen in the beam-pipe mineral-oil layer and MDC inner wall — turning the spectrometer itself into a polarimeter. Requiring a third track (the knocked-out target proton), vetoing quasi-free nuclear collisions via |p_target|<50 MeV/c, they isolate 2556 elastic events (15.2% efficiency) and extract, via the SAID analyzing powers, sinΔΦ=-0.20±0.34_stat±0.11_syst — the first determination of the relative phase between the proton’s psionic (complex G_E^ψ, G_M^ψ) form factors.

Why it matters: The relative TL-region phase had been unreachable for nucleons, which lack self-analyzing decays; hyperons (Λ, Σ, Ξ) had been mapped but the proton and neutron remained blank. Placing the proton near Σ⁺/0 and below Λ, Ξ⁻/0 gives a first SU(3)-symmetry test point. The method — validated by a pseudo-experiment recovering an injected sinΔΦ=-0.84 as -0.82±0.02 — is reusable at any large-acceptance spectrometer, with Σ⁻ and (with better neutron detection) the neutron as obvious next targets. Caveats: the result is statistics-limited and consistent with zero; two ΔΦ solutions remain degenerate, resolvable only with a polarized beam (𝒫_x) or antiproton polarization, e.g. at STCF.

arXiv:2607.19487 — Four, One, and None: Quantifying the UHE Neutrino Anomaly Across ANITA-IV, KM3NeT, and IceCube (Dibya S. Chattopadhyay et al.)

What they did: Chattopadhyay, Argüelles, and Brdar perform the first joint statistical fit of the four near-horizon ANITA-IV events, the single KM3-230213A event, and IceCube’s null result, using semi-analytic energy-, direction-, and time-dependent effective areas for all three detectors with realistic exposures (26.6 d for ANITA-IV, 287 d for ARCA-21, 5400 d for IceCube). For a common diffuse power-law flux, no normalization/spectral-index choice reproduces the observed (4,0,1) counts: the best fit predicts ~5 events at IceCube and 𝒪(10⁻³⁾/𝒪(10⁻¹⁾ at ANITA-IV/KM3NeT, a 7.5σ tension (7.9σ for fixed E⁻²). Modeling rare all-sky transients, with the probability of four favorable ANITA-IV overlaps fixed to ∼10⁻⁴ and scanning 10⁵ MC realizations, the least-anomalous benchmark (185 sources, 10-day duration) still leaves 5.9σ.

Why it matters: This converts the qualitative ANITA/KM3NeT-vs-IceCube “puzzle” into a hard number, sharpening the KM3-230213A thread. Crucially, the tension is driven by ANITA-IV, not KM3NeT: the ANITA-IV–IceCube-only fit gives 5.8–7.8σ, while KM3-230213A alone is a mild 1.8–2.5σ. The authors conclude neither diffuse flux nor rare identical transients works within the SM, pointing to structured source populations, detector/classification effects, or new physics. Caveats: the effective areas are semi-analytic, reproducing collaboration values only within a factor ~2 near the horizon; the trigger-efficiency parametrization and spherical detector approximation (especially for the anisotropic ARCA-21) carry acknowledged modeling uncertainty.

item.title: Wednesday, July 22, 2026
item.description:
The kaon program regroups after NA62

Yesterday’s NA62 golden-mode measurement already has its phenomenology sequel: Blanke et al. arXiv:2607.19055 work out what the SM-consistent K⁺→π⁺νν̅ result leaves open for KOTO II, showing K_L→π⁰νν̅ can still be enhanced tenfold with new complex phases and a right-handed s̅d current while keeping K⁺ and ε_K SM-like. That’s the day’s clearest thread of continuity. The other real weight is experimental and sits at the opposite end of the mass scale — QUALIPHIDE’s 13 meV superconducting sensor array arXiv:2607.19319 setting the strongest hidden-photon limits over 13–90 meV. Around them, a dense cluster of domain-wall/phase-transition GW model-building and a genuinely nice conceptual paper reframing astrophysical neutrino sources as colliders.

Themes

Dark matter detection at new thresholds

The diversifying-detection mood the memory has tracked all month keeps going, now with real limits attached. QUALIPHIDE arXiv:2607.19319 runs a 41-pixel MKID array at a 13 meV threshold with a data-driven on/off-focus background model, setting the strongest hidden-photon mixing limits in its window plus among the first terrestrial light-DM scattering bounds down to 5 MeV. Complementing it at the heavy end, RES-NOVA arXiv:2607.18378 uses archaeological-lead PbWO_4 to push inelastic-DM mass splittings past 500 keV, and Zhang et al. arXiv:2607.18647 turn magnetic white dwarfs into a time-domain axion probe — with an honest warning that higher-harmonic stellar variability fakes a signal.

Domain walls, transitions, and gravitational waves

A coherent early-universe cluster, mostly model-building this time rather than the systematics drumbeat of July 17/21. Missoni et al. arXiv:2607.18800 study confinement at finite θ in holographic SU(N_c) Yang-Mills, producing domain walls from bubble coalescence; Behera et al. arXiv:2607.18803 tie a modular-A_4 resonant-leptogenesis model to a double-peaked GW spectrum from DW annihilation plus a first-order transition. Barenboim et al. arXiv:2607.18449 map cosmological stasis onto BBO/DECIGO bands, and Inada et al. arXiv:2607.18381 probe quantum-corrected inflaton potentials via preheating GWs.

Sources and photons as colliders

Argüelles et al. arXiv:2607.19254 extract two-sided bounds on pp and pγ inelastic cross sections from IceCube/KM3NeT point sources by fixing every astrophysical input independently — reaching √(s) well beyond LHC and, for pγ, beyond HERA. It pairs naturally with the day’s ultra-peripheral work: Contreras et al.’s review arXiv:2607.18535 and Krauss et al.’s automated Sherpa framework for photon-induced processes with full impact-parameter dependence arXiv:2607.18834.

Heavy-flavor and lattice spectroscopy

Lachini et al. arXiv:2607.19009 revisit the T_cc⁺ on the lattice with nonperturbative one-pion exchange, turning the pole complex once the left-hand cut is handled correctly and predicting it moves toward the real axis at physical m_π. Alongside, coupled-channel Ξ_cc⁽)K⁽) molecular predictions arXiv:2607.18672 extend the doubly-charmed program.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.19319 — QUALIPHIDE’s 13 meV MKID array with a discovery-capable background model; strongest hidden-photon limits in its band and early light-DM scattering bounds.
  • arXiv:2607.19055 — The NA62 sequel: how much room remains for K_L→π⁰νν̅ and ε’/ε given yesterday’s SM-consistent K⁺ result.
  • arXiv:2607.19254 — Neutrino point sources as cross-section colliders past LHC/HERA reach; a clean recipe worth citing.
  • arXiv:2607.19009 — T_cc⁺ on the lattice with pion exchange done right; the left-hand cut changes the pole’s character.
  • arXiv:2607.18484 — ATLAS X→SH→bb̅ bb̅ across 300 GeV–6 TeV, with Gaussian-process/normalizing-flow background modeling; null, but methodologically notable.

From the community

Adıgüzel et al. arXiv:2607.19034 reimplement ATLAS Open Data benchmark analyses in ADL/CutLang, decoupling physics logic from experiment software for preservation and reproducibility — the open-data ethos the DPHEP thread has been paying off all month. And Blas et al.’s GUEST white paper arXiv:2607.18390 proposes passive satellite laser-ranging spheres as a µHz GW detector, a concrete mission concept for the band between PTAs and LISA.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.18464 Deep inelastic scattering as a probe of entanglement — Hentschinski et al. (hep-ph) — entanglement entropy from the full QCD dipole cascade against H1 data; QI-at-colliders continuing.
  • arXiv:2607.19220 Quarkyonic Stars with Strangeness — Hu et al. (nucl-th) — the quarkyonic mechanism stiffens the EoS and mitigates the hyperon puzzle.
  • arXiv:2607.18380 Fate of Metastable Vacua in the Type-II 2HDM — Chowdhury et al. (hep-ph) — a gauge-independent global fit excluding the metastable-vacuum regions.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.19319 — Dark matter searches with a 13 meV threshold superconducting sensor array (Christopher Albert et al.)

QUALIPHIDE-FIR ran a 41-pixel array of aluminum microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKIDs) — FIR astronomy photon-counters, peak-tuned at 25 µm/50 meV — as a dual-mode dark matter search with a 13 meV threshold, the lowest yet in a direct-detection experiment. The array couples to a gold-plated spherical dish (5163 mm²) that converts hidden-photon DM into real photons collected at the focus; four on-focus pixels see any signal while 37 off-focus pixels build a data-driven background model, giving genuine discovery potential rather than upper limits only. A blind analysis of 22 hours found no excess (peak local significance 1.33σ at 82 meV), setting the strongest hidden-photon kinetic-mixing limits over 13–90 meV, reaching χ = 1.5×10⁻¹² at 50 meV and improving on prior terrestrial bounds above 90 meV by >20×. The same Al inductors serve as scattering targets: with 1.33 ng·day exposure and the optimal-interval method, the search reaches DM masses of 5 MeV (nuclear) and 20 keV (electronic), roughly an order of magnitude below QROCODILE’s 0.11 eV threshold, carving out new sub-overburden parameter space.

Why it matters: this is the diversifying-detection theme with real limits, opening the meV “THz gap” where cavity and TPC methods fail. The 13 meV threshold also probes the low-energy-excess background at single-phonon energies (below Al’s ~41 meV maximum) for the first time. Caveats are honest: the dominant efficiency systematic η₀ = 0.46±0.06 lumps uncharacterized losses; resolution above 70 meV is uncalibrated (treated as a single counting bin); and the projected scattering sensitivity assumes an aggressive 1000× background reduction, versus the ~10× already demonstrated.

arXiv:2607.19055 — Prospects for K_L→π⁰νν̅, K_S→μ⁺μ⁻, K_L→π⁰ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ and ε’/ε after the new K⁺→π⁺νν̅ result from NA62 (Monika Blanke et al.)

Abstract only. Blanke et al. take yesterday’s NA62 result — a K⁺→π⁺νν̅ branching ratio (2016–2024 data) fully consistent with the precise SM prediction — and ask what room remains for its neutral counterpart. The answer: with suitably large new complex phases and a small right-handed s̅d coupling added to the left-handed structure, K_L→π⁰νν̅ can still be enhanced by an order of magnitude relative to the SM while keeping both K⁺→π⁺νν̅ and ε_K SM-like. In the same scenario K_S→μ⁺μ⁻ (LHCb) and K_L→π⁰ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ (KOTO II) are strongly enhanced and the Dual-QCD ε’/ε anomaly is removed, illustrated with a specific Z’ model.

Why it matters: this is the direct phenomenology sequel to the NA62 golden-mode measurement, showing that an SM-like charged channel does not close the door on KOTO II’s discovery target — the golden K_L mode retains up to tenfold enhancement. The construction is explicitly a proof-of-existence within a chosen Z’ framework, and hinges on tuning new phases plus right-handed currents; the authors note the final NA62 result (2016–2026) could still shift.

arXiv:2607.19254 — Astrophysical Neutrino Sources as Colliders (Carlos A. Argüelles et al.)

Argüelles et al. present a recipe to extract two-sided bounds on the inelastic pp and pγ cross sections from neutrino point sources by independently pinning every astrophysical input — cosmic-ray luminosity (bounded above by Eddington/relativistic-beaming limits, below by the power needed to sustain observed neutrino and X-ray fluxes) and target column density (from X-ray spectroscopy, Thomson depth, or variability) — leaving σ as the only free parameter. Applied to IceCube’s TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane, the stacked 11-source Seyfert population, and KM3NeT’s 220-PeV KM3-230213A, the bounds span √(s)∼1 GeV to ∼10⁵ GeV. Concrete bands: TXS 10-year data gives σ_pp≃0.5–70 mb at √(s)≃0.9–2.8 TeV; the Seyfert stack gives σ_pp∈[2.3,70] mb and σ_pγ∈[0.08,9] mb with the smallest astrophysical uncertainties. Dedicated Pythia 8 simulations revise the per-flavor neutrino energy fraction upward to ξ_ν^pp≃0.086–0.099, ~1.8× the canonical leading-pion estimate, relaxing lower bounds by nearly 2×. Several bounds are more stringent than the Froissart–Martin unitarity limit, and pγ constraints reach beyond HERA’s √(s)≃209 GeV.

Why it matters: it reframes neutrino telescopes as flux-based hadronic colliders scanning continuously in √(s), complementary to the shape-based (flux-independent) Auger air-shower method and to collider fixed points. The SM cross section sits inside every band — a nontrivial consistency check. Caveats are prominent: band widths (factors of ~30) are set by astrophysical systematics, not neutrino statistics; TXS relies on an upper-bound-only column density and requires super-Eddington CR power even after beaming correction; and KM3/UHE bounds are projections under a “standard-candle” idealization awaiting source association.

item.title: Tuesday, July 21, 2026
item.description:
Rare kaons and a first exotic Reggeon

Two experimental results carry the day, both clean and both in channels that have been chased for years. NA62 posts an updated K⁺→π⁺νν̅ branching ratio of (9.6⁺¹.9_-1.8)×10⁻¹¹ over 2016–2024 — 20% precision on the golden mode, and consistent with the SM (arXiv:2607.16413). Meanwhile COMPASS/JPAC report the first observation in high-energy scattering of an exotic Reggeon, above 5σ in both ηπ⁻ and η’π⁻, most likely tied to the π_1(1600) (arXiv:2607.17850). Around these, a substantial first-order-phase-transition cluster picks up exactly the systematics thread that ran through July 17, and heavy-flavor spectroscopy keeps consolidating.

Themes

Rare kaons and exotic mesons

The NA62 measurement (arXiv:2607.16413) is the headline: the world’s most precise handle on a mode where the SM prediction is exceptionally clean, still sitting on top of theory. The COMPASS exotic-Reggeon observation (Alexeev et al. arXiv:2607.17850) is the more novel result — an unbinned high-mass analysis disentangling the exchange mechanism, giving the spin-exotic π_1 program a production-side foothold. Two very different corners of QCD, both reporting firsts.

First-order transitions and their gravitational waves

A coherent methods cluster, all sharpening the microphysics-to-spectrum map. Dorsch et al. arXiv:2607.18207 benchmark the fluid ansatz against WallGo for wall velocities, finding agreement for mild transitions but a discrepancy once scattering enters and non-linearities matter as α→1. Kierkla et al. arXiv:2607.18233 show that in supercooled conformal models the daisy-resummation scheme is strongly disfavored — its theoretical error swamps LISA reconstruction uncertainty. An et al. arXiv:2607.16398 revise the UV scaling of heavy-particle production in boosted wall collisions, and Barbini et al. arXiv:2607.18107 deliver lattice GW spectra for biased domain-wall networks. This directly extends July 17’s wall-friction and cosmic-string-reach papers: the message keeps being that GW “signals” hinge on poorly controlled non-equilibrium inputs.

Ultralight and dark-sector detection

Kalia et al. arXiv:2607.16342 review the “Earth transducer” effect — using the planet’s radius rather than an apparatus size to probe EM-coupled ultralight DM below ∼3×10⁻¹⁴ eV. Brax et al. arXiv:2607.17727 build repulsive ultralight DM from a Hosotani/Scherk-Schwarz construction, and Rosenzweig et al. arXiv:2607.18221 propose correlated dual-species comagnetometry for high-frequency background suppression. Olea-Romacho arXiv:2607.18185 uses wide binaries in Boötes I to bound extended dark objects. The diversifying-search mood, now firmly on the detection side.

Heavy-flavor spectroscopy consolidation

Luo et al. arXiv:2607.17923 use HQET sum rules to assign quantum numbers to excited Ξ_c’/Ω_c states and predict four resolvable P-wave Σ_c states overlapping the observed Σ_c(2800)/Σ_c(2900) — a direct theory follow-up to LHCb’s July 14 discovery of two new Σ_c⁰ states. Gui et al. arXiv:2607.17294 find a large glueball–ss̅ mixing angle (∼41°) in N_f=1 lattice QCD, and several QCD-sum-rule pentaquark and doubly-heavy-baryon analyses round it out.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.16413 — NA62’s golden-mode branching ratio at 20% precision, still SM-consistent; the number the kaon community will quote.
  • arXiv:2607.17850 — First high-energy-scattering observation of an exotic Reggeon (>5σ), tied to the π_1(1600).
  • arXiv:2607.18233 — A sobering result: for supercooled transitions, the standard daisy-resummation scheme is disfavored because its theory error dominates LISA’s reconstruction.
  • arXiv:2607.17923 — Sum-rule quantum-number assignments that connect the narrow Ξ_c/Ω_c states to the recently observed Σ_c structures.
  • arXiv:2607.16342 — The Earth-as-transducer review: a planet-scale probe of ultralight EM-coupled DM with unusually favorable coherence properties.

From the community

Two field-facing pieces. Dudko’s muon-collider review arXiv:2607.16904 argues for housing a 10–20 TeV machine in the existing 21 km UNK tunnel at Protvino — a concrete siting proposal amid the ongoing collider-strategy debate. And Pancheri’s history of Touschek and the first e⁺e⁻ collider arXiv:2607.16825 is a timely reminder of how intergovernmental accelerator collaboration got started.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.17903 First measurement of Ξ_c⁰ production in Pb–Pb — ALICE Collaboration (nucl-ex) — R_AA up to 3, the largest yet for charm hadrons.
  • arXiv:2607.17509 Final assessment of radioactive impurities in JUNO — Adam et al. (physics.ins-det) — detector complete and radiopurity budget met.
  • arXiv:2607.17277 Charm-coupled GeV-scale QCD axion in HMChPT — Lu (hep-ph) — follow-up to this month’s charm-axion revival; no fatal constraint, testable rare decays.
  • arXiv:2607.17744 Measuring the acceleration-dependent temperature of the Minkowski vacuum — Danielson et al. (hep-ex) — a wakefield-based proposal to observe the Unruh effect.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.16413 — Measurement of the branching ratio of the K⁺→π⁺νν̅ decay (NA62 Collaboration)

NA62 reports ℬ_2023-2024(K⁺→π⁺νν̅)=(7.2⁺².3_-2.1)×10⁻¹¹ from 33 candidates against 22.9±1.1 SM signal and 12.0⁺².9_-2.2 background events, then combines with 2016–2022 to obtain (9.6⁺¹.9_-1.8)×10⁻¹¹ — 20% precision and consistent with SM predictions near 8×10⁻¹¹. Across 2016–2024, 84 observed events against 30⁺⁴_-3 background give background-only rejection exceeding 6σ, and the SM-observation significance passes 5σ for the first time. The 2023–2024 data were taken at lower intensity (440 MHz vs. the 580 MHz design max), sitting on a broad signal-per-spill maximum around 450 MHz where DAQ dead time and accidental vetoes are balanced; this improved the random-veto efficiency by 1.14 and roughly halved several relative backgrounds. New deep-learning tools — a transformer-based 4D GTK tracker (false-track rate 13%→4%, purity 87%→97%) and a ResNet-based calorimetric π/μ classifier (~2% higher pion ID, 40% lower μ→π misID) — sharpen the selection. A KTAG upgrade to H_2 radiator cut material budget from 3.9% to 0.7% X_0.

Why it matters: this is now the world’s most precise handle on the theoretically cleanest FCNC kaon mode (SM intrinsic uncertainty ~3%, dominated by long-distance charm), and it lands squarely on the SM. The dominant background remains upstream (accidental K⁺/π matching), estimated fully data-driven with ~30% uncertainty. NA62 expects a further ~50% more signal events after 2025–2026 running.

arXiv:2607.17850 — First Observation of an Exotic Reggeon (G. D. Alexeev (for JPAC Collaboration) et al.)

(Abstract only.) COMPASS presents high-statistics measurements of peripheral ηπ⁻ and η’π⁻ production in π⁻ p→η⁽’)π⁻ p, performing for the first time an unbinned analysis of the high-mass region to disentangle the exchange mechanisms governing production. They report the first observation in high-energy scattering of an exotic Reggeon, at significance exceeding 5σ in both channels, most likely related to the spin-exotic π_1(1600).

Why it matters: this establishes a production-side foothold for the π_1 spin-exotic program, complementing the decades of resonance-spectrum work. Where earlier analyses focused on identifying the exotic state in the produced system, disentangling the exchange mechanism gives independent evidence that exotic quantum numbers propagate in the t-channel — a genuinely new handle on QCD’s exotic sector. As only the abstract is available, the details of the exchange decomposition and systematic treatment cannot be assessed here.

arXiv:2607.18233 — Theoretical uncertainties in reconstructing model parameters with gravitational waves from supercooled phase transitions (Maciej Kierkla et al.)

Taking the classically conformal U(1)_X model as representative of strongly supercooled transitions, the authors scan {g_X,M_X} over 𝒪(10⁴⁾ points and compute GW spectra with two nucleation-rate schemes: a 4D daisy-resummed potential with dimensionally-estimated prefactor, and a full NLO calculation (two-loop 3D-EFT matching plus exact scalar and vector fluctuation determinants, “NLOdet”). Injecting the resulting signals into LISA and running a Fisher-matrix reconstruction of the fundamental parameters, they find the daisy scheme strongly disfavored: the two methods disagree by 𝒪(10%) in the reconstructed gauge coupling g_X, an order of magnitude larger than the daisy RG-scale ambiguity (𝒪(1%)) and more than an order of magnitude above the sub-percent Fisher reconstruction uncertainty. The hierarchy is δ_g^exp∼δ_g^μ̅,NLOdet≪δ_g^μ̅,daisy≪δ_g^meth∼𝒪(10%). Crucially, no reasonable RG-scale choice reconciles daisy with NLOdet — contradicting a recent claim that scale-shifting suffices — because the discrepancy stems from genuinely missing higher-order physics (the scale-shifting gauge modes require exact determinants, not a derivative expansion). M_X is essentially unaffected, since it just sets the low-T Hubble scale.

Why it matters: this extends the digest’s recurring message — GW “signals” from first-order transitions hinge on poorly controlled non-equilibrium/thermal inputs. For high-SNR LISA targets, theoretical diligence, not detector sensitivity, limits the inverse problem. Caveats: dynamical prefactor uses the no-damping approximation (neglecting back-reaction), and the hierarchy inverts in the lower-SNR PTA band.

item.title: Monday, July 20, 2026
item.description:
What the data teaches without being told

A modest-volume day (27 papers) with no collaboration headline, but the center of gravity has shifted from reconstructing physics with ML to learning it — three generative/graph models today extract Standard Model structure, tagger knowledge, and robust tracking straight from data or across experiments. The other real weight is cosmological: Khoury et al.’s dark-axion/dark-baryon model (arXiv:2607.16191) fits DESI DR2 phantom-crossing with Δχ²=−14.48, and two non-Gaussianity papers push the excursion-set and bispectrum machinery into strongly non-Gaussian tails. Underneath, a steady stream of novel dark-matter detection proposals and scotogenic neutrino model-building. A tool-and-idea day rather than a measurement one.

Themes

Machine learning that discovers rather than reconstructs

The month’s ML thread — trigger GNNs, transformer calorimetry, LQCDMaster — takes a conceptual step today. Kato et al.’s ShellFlow arXiv:2607.16144 is the standout: a Riemannian flow-matching model trained on ~10⁹ real ATLAS 13 TeV open-data events, given only the on-shell condition and the invariant-mass formula, that recovers the J/ψ, Υ, Z, W and top masses at their PDG values and the leptonic Weinberg angle — none of it a training target. Gao et al.’s JetCoRD arXiv:2607.15531 distills ATLAS GN2 and CMS ParT into a single 82k-parameter student that beats both teachers at high-purity working points, notably by building in teacher unreliability. And Reuter et al. arXiv:2607.15361 show a Belle II GNN track finder treats detector ageing as a domain shift — halving the efficiency loss of baseline tracking after retraining.

Novel dark-matter detection targets

A cluster of “new target class” proposals. Zhang et al. arXiv:2607.15338 propose metallic carbon nanotubes as a 1D Luttinger-liquid plasmon target reaching the keV freeze-in benchmark, with sidereal-day modulation from the aligned geometry. Li et al. arXiv:2607.15612 push chip-scale Rydberg-atom superheterodyne detection of >10 GHz hidden photons 3–4 orders below current limits. And Dev et al. arXiv:2607.15368 turn the collimated muon beam at neutrino facilities into a bremsstrahlung source for HNLs beyond meson-decay kinematic reach at SBND/DUNE. The diversifying-search mood the memory has tracked, now on the detection side.

Dark energy and non-Gaussian cosmology

Khoury et al. arXiv:2607.16191 give the day’s most consequential cosmology entry — a concrete dark-sector realization of apparent phantom crossing that improves on ΛCDM by Δχ²=−14.48, with an EDE-like injection near equality that is, honestly, too small to move H₀. Natural sequel to the H₀ World Cup’s early-dark-energy verdict. On non-Gaussianity, Yang et al. arXiv:2607.15337 forecast folded PNG from the galaxy bispectrum, and Teuscher et al. arXiv:2607.16152 apply large-deviation theory to halo/void abundances beyond perturbative moment expansion. Cembranos et al. arXiv:2607.15354 raise Starobinsky’s n_s toward ACT-preferred values via a tunnelling exit — the latest in the running effort to rescue Starobinsky from ACT data.

Scotogenic neutrino masses

Two minimal-model entries: Rizzo arXiv:2607.15965 generates ~0.05 eV Dirac masses at one loop from E₆-like portal matter, and Peinado et al. arXiv:2607.16049 find D₄ the smallest flavor symmetry unifying seesaw-scotogenic masses with a 50–200 GeV dark-matter candidate.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.16144 — ShellFlow learns W, top, Z masses and the Weinberg angle from raw ATLAS open data with only two physics priors; a genuinely surprising demonstration.
  • arXiv:2607.16191 — Khoury et al.’s dark-axion/dark-baryon model fits DESI phantom crossing at Δχ²=−14.48; the concrete particle realization the DESI-anomaly literature needed.
  • arXiv:2607.15338 — Carbon nanotubes as a 1D plasmon target reaching the keV freeze-in benchmark, with a built-in directional handle.
  • arXiv:2607.15392 — Solar-system p-nuclide abundances (Mo, Ru, ⁹²Nb) as a fossil signature of fast collective neutrino oscillations in supernovae; an unexpected observational handle on an elusive phenomenon.
  • arXiv:2607.15531 — First cross-experiment tagger distillation in HEP, with a reliability signal that lets the 82k-param student beat its ATLAS and CMS teachers.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2607.15985 Gluon Saturation — Mueller (hep-ph) — a review from the field’s originator; occupancies capped at (1/α)^{3/2} once Sudakov effects enter.
  • arXiv:2607.15927 Operation and performance of ProtoDUNE Dual Phase — DUNE Collaboration (physics.ins-det) — candid post-mortem on the CRP/LEM problems that reshaped the Vertical Drift design.
  • arXiv:2607.16041 P_c(4312/4440/4457) productions in e⁺e⁻ — Guo et al. (hep-ph) — predicts a resolvable Pc(4440)/Pc(4457) splitting in the J/ψp spectrum at √s=6 GeV.
  • arXiv:2607.16182 Geometric scaling in elastic pp collisions — Praszałowicz (hep-ph) — the ISR-era bump/dip ratio holds constant from 23 GeV to 13 TeV.

item.title: Friday, July 17, 2026
item.description:
Down in the detector shop

After a fortnight where theorists and phenomenologists held the floor, today the hardware people walked back in and put their tools on the table. Six instrumentation and reconstruction papers landed at once — a production-grade Kalman filter running in LHCb’s real-time trigger, a multi-year quality-control census of ATLAS ITk strip sensors, gamma-irradiation damage studies, scintillator timing, calorimeter energy reconstruction, a Timepix4 DAQ. It reads less like a coincidence than like the HL-LHC and future-collider machines reminding everyone that all the precision phenomenology of recent weeks eventually has to survive contact with silicon and firmware.

Around that core the day spread wide but not thin. Two threads the memory has been watching kept their momentum: quantum information is still creeping from novelty into working vocabulary — three papers today treat spin states and entanglement as collider observables — and the EIC-facing structure program produced a genuinely pretty result on the proton’s gluon cloud. Dark matter, meanwhile, was in a constraining rather than model-building mood: several papers today are about bounding things, and one of them quietly kills a benchmark GUT-scale naturalness scenario.

No collaboration bombshell, but a satisfying working day: things measured, things excluded, things fitted.

Themes

Instrumentation and real-time reconstruction

The standout is LHCb’s Billoir et al. arXiv:2607.14793: a parameterised Kalman filter replacing magnetic-field-map lookups and numerical integration with fast analytical forms, deployed on ~500 GPUs in the first trigger stage, delivering a factor-of-two improvement in D⁰ and J/ψ mass resolution and more than doubling accidental-track rejection — all at a 2% cost in processing time. This is the real-time-reconstruction wave reaching production, the hardware counterpart to the ML-trigger papers the memory tracked earlier this month. Alongside it, Federičová et al. arXiv:2607.14691 report the ATLAS ITk strip-sensor QC census (>91% of 590+ batches accepted), and Mikestikova et al. arXiv:2607.15056 characterize bulk damage in gamma-irradiated n⁺-in-p diodes — the unglamorous radiation-tolerance groundwork HL-LHC rests on. Che et al. arXiv:2607.14290 (scintillator/WLS/SiPM timing), Biesuz et al. arXiv:2607.14847 (Timepix4 DAQ), and Pasquier et al. arXiv:2607.15023 (SDHCAL hadronic reconstruction for a future lepton collider) round out an unusually dense hardware cluster.

Quantum information at colliders

Yesterday this looked like an emerging coalescence; today it consolidates. Cheng et al. arXiv:2607.12015 (cross-listed) dissect the τ⁻τ⁺γ spin state across phase space and find final-state radiation can either decohere the pair or monotonically boost its entanglement. ShivaSankar K. A. et al. arXiv:2607.15153 show that entanglement markers, concurrence and the CHSH parameter in Z’-mediated tt̅ at future lepton colliders carry information complementary to cross sections — with beam polarization as a direct handle on chiral U(1)_X charges. And Mao et al. arXiv:2607.14558 compute spin-resolved ALP→e⁺e⁻ decay in strong laser fields, using pair entanglement (singlet-like near threshold, triplet-like in the strong-field regime) as a signature of the production mechanism. Spin and entanglement are becoming ordinary columns in the observable table.

Nucleon structure toward the EIC

A coherent structure cluster, all pointing at future machines. Toll et al. arXiv:2607.14955 fit the hotspot model to all HERA exclusive J/ψ photoproduction data and extract a precise proton gluon-cloud shape — a perturbative Gaussian core of 0.105 fm inside a non-perturbative 0.220 fm halo, with an excellent χ²/ndf=0.77. Bellotti et al. arXiv:2607.14964 work out gluon GTMDs in exclusive heavy-quark-pair electroproduction; Cong Li arXiv:2607.14958 proposes a cross-section-ratio inversion to extract the photon distribution function at the EIC; Nefedov arXiv:2607.14986 adds O(v²⁾ relativistic corrections to high-energy-resummed quarkonium photoproduction; and Jia et al. arXiv:2607.15214 compute substantial NNLO QCD corrections to pion- and kaon-induced exclusive Drell-Yan for J-PARC.

Dark matter bounds and attenuation

The mood is exclusionary. Mosbech et al. arXiv:2607.15020 run full hydrodynamical simulations plus an emulator on high-resolution Lyman-α data to set the strongest direct bound to date on DM–neutrino scattering, explicitly ruling out earlier hints. Gu et al. arXiv:2607.15098 fold resonant and deep-inelastic channels into boosted-DM Earth attenuation, refining PandaX-4T constraints. Chanda et al. arXiv:2607.14253 bound coexisting PBH-plus-particle-DM minispikes with neutrino data. And in the most striking entry, Lonardi et al. arXiv:2607.14243 mount the first experimental search for the N-naturalness tower of neutrinos, excluding — for Majorana neutrinos — the N=10⁴ GUT-unification benchmark that had been the framework’s tidy no-fine-tuning selling point. On the model side, Chen et al. arXiv:2607.14210 embed scotogenic DM in SU(6)/Sp(6) composite Higgs, and Issifu arXiv:2607.14979 threads Higgs-portal DM through neutron-star EOSs.

Phase transitions and GW backgrounds

The early-universe modeling continues to sharpen its systematics. Branchina et al. arXiv:2607.14867 show that consistently including thermal masses in bubble-wall friction suppresses the troublesome infrared gauge-boson contribution, so wall velocities end up close to top-quark friction alone — a welcome reduction of a poorly-controlled uncertainty. Ghoshal et al. arXiv:2607.15279 argue that the standard off-shell-decay picture of particle production in bubble collisions parametrically overestimates hard production and is gauge-dependent, offering a partonic reformulation. And Dimitriou et al. arXiv:2607.15219 deliver a sobering number: reconstructing cosmic-string tensions at LISA once all astrophysical foregrounds are included demands Gμ≳10⁻¹¹ — a factor ∼10⁵ worse than foreground-free forecasts.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.14793 — LHCb’s parameterised Kalman filter in production at 30 MHz on 500 GPUs, doubling mass resolution for a 2% timing cost; real-time reconstruction crossing into the trigger.
  • arXiv:2607.14955 — A precise, excellent-fit extraction of the proton’s gluon-cloud shape from HERA, resolving a perturbative core inside a non-perturbative halo.
  • arXiv:2607.14243 — The first experimental test of the N-naturalness tower, ruling out its GUT-scale benchmark with existing neutrino data.
  • arXiv:2607.15020 — The strongest direct bound yet on DM–neutrino scattering, from hydro-simulated high-resolution Lyman-α data, excluding prior hints.
  • arXiv:2607.15219 — A hard dose of realism: astrophysical foregrounds degrade LISA’s cosmic-string reach by five orders of magnitude in Gμ.

From the community

Gao et al.’s LQCDMaster arXiv:2607.15001 is an agentic AI system that turns natural-language lattice-QCD tasks into executable PyQUDA workflows, reproducing expert implementations at machine precision on 63 of 70 benchmark tasks — and it demonstrates a genuinely new computation along the way. It’s the natural next step after this month’s LLM-auditing and ML-verification discussions: not just checking AI-generated analysis, but handing the agent the keyboard.

Also noted

  • A tidy formal-QCD triad on collinear behavior: Barcaro et al. arXiv:2607.14259 on factorization-violation and Reggeization, Chen et al. arXiv:2607.15126 locating a “hidden region” responsible for spacelike-collinear factorization breaking, and Wang et al. arXiv:2607.15191 deriving massive on-shell splitting functions for all SM particles.
  • arXiv:2607.14151 Candia-v2: Logarithmic expansions for DGLAP evolution in x-space — Hampson et al. (hep-ph) — an efficient N³LO x-space DGLAP solver, open-source.
  • arXiv:2607.14942 A Differential Neutral-to-Charged Current Double-Proton Observable… — Bueno et al. (hep-ex) — a clever NC/CC two-proton ratio to isolate short-range correlations in neutrino–argon scattering.
  • arXiv:2607.15188 One more radiative-recoil correction to the Lamb shift in muonium — Eides et al. (physics.atom-ph) — precision input for ongoing muonium 1S–2S and 2S–2P measurements.

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.14793 — Track fitting at the full LHC collision rate (Pierre Billoir et al.)

(Abstract only.) LHCb deployed a fast parameterised Kalman filter in the first trigger stage from the 2025 run, fitting charged-particle trajectories at the full 30 MHz collision rate on ~500 GPUs. The trick is to replace magnetic-field-map lookups and numerical integration with analytical parameterisations while keeping the Kalman mathematical framework intact. Against the previous partial fitter it delivers a factor-of-two improvement in D⁰ and J/ψ invariant-mass resolution (from improved momentum resolution), greater robustness to misalignment, and more than doubled rejection of accidental tracks at no loss of genuine-track efficiency — for only a 2% processing-time increase.

Why it matters: this is real-time reconstruction crossing from R&D into production in an all-software trigger, the hardware counterpart to the month’s ML-trigger work. Sharper online mass resolution and background rejection directly widen what LHCb’s first stage can select and store, a template for HL-LHC-era triggering. As an abstract, the numbers are headline-level; the underlying validation (efficiency turn-ons, systematics of the parameterisation across the field volume) isn’t visible here.

arXiv:2607.14955 — A Precise Determination of the Shape of the Proton’s Gluon Cloud from HERA data (Tobias Toll et al.)

(Abstract only.) An analytic leading-twist calculation of coherent and incoherent exclusive J/ψ photoproduction cross sections in the hotspot model is fit to all H1 and ZEUS diffractive data, yielding χ²/ndf=0.77. The extracted gluon-cloud profile has a perturbative Gaussian core of 0.105(1) fm sitting inside a non-perturbative exponential halo of 0.220(2) fm — a two-scale structure the authors report as independent of x_Pom or hotspot number, with a stable energy dependence α’_eff=0.046(19).

Why it matters: a clean, tightly-fit picture of the proton’s small-x gluonic transverse structure, resolving core from halo, is exactly the input the EIC structure program needs, and the excellent fit lends the hotspot framework credibility as an interpretive tool. As an abstract, the key caveats — leading-twist/leading-order treatment and the model-dependence of the incoherent-to-fluctuation mapping — can’t be assessed from the text provided.

arXiv:2607.14243 — Searching for the N-naturalness tower of neutrinos (Sofia Lonardi et al.)

First experimental test of the N-naturalness neutrino tower, via a global fit of public data (Daya Bay, GERDA, LEGEND-200) plus projections (JUNO+TAO, LEGEND-1000) in the Newtrinos.jl framework. The model solves the hierarchy problem with N dark sectors of varying Higgs mass, encoding residual fine-tuning in a parameter r (r=1 = no tuning); implemented via the many-mixing-partners mechanism, it generates suppressed neutrino masses and a tower of extra light states that distort oscillations and shift m_ββ. Numerically diagonalising the full N-sector mass matrix (avoiding the perturbative breakdown at small N), they set 90% CL contours. For Majorana neutrinos, current GERDA+Daya Bay data already exclude non-fine-tuned scenarios (r=1) up to N=10⁴ for both orderings — killing the tidy N=10⁴ GUT-unification benchmark that let the framework address the hierarchy problem without ad-hoc tuning. JUNO+TAO projections push lower bounds to N≳500 and require r≲0.1 in 500≤N≤10⁴.

Why it matters: it converts a “no-fine-tuning” selling point into a falsified benchmark using existing neutrino data, exactly the constraining mood of today’s DM-and-naturalness cluster. Caveats are honestly flagged: the Dirac case is far weaker (no 0νββ handle, excluded only to N∼50); results assume m_0=0.01 eV and η=1+1/N; and m_ββ rests on a single benchmark set of nuclear matrix elements (varied only for robustness checks).

Citation radar

This week’s radar leans toward infrastructure and framing: papers that hand the community a reusable tool, a systematic classification, or a reference review rather than a single headline number. Two automation/formalism papers (finite-temperature matching, multi-axion classification), a major experimental-systematics review, and a collider quantum-information study round out a set where the common thread is enabling other people’s calculations. All four sit at five citations, consistent with their recent posting.

arXiv:2604.21332 — Disentangling new physics with quantum entanglement in tt̅ production at future lepton colliders (Masato Arai et al.)

Arai, Mawatari and Okada compute quantum-information observables—the entanglement marker D_min, the concurrence, and the maximal CHSH parameter B_max—for l⁻l⁺→tt̅ in the SM and three s-channel extensions: a scalar mediator, a U(1)_B-L Z’, and Randall–Sundrum KK gravitons. Working from helicity amplitudes and the two-qubit density matrix, they find each Lorentz structure reorganizes spin correlations distinctively: the scalar reduces entanglement, U(1)_B-L induces energy-dependent interference distortions, and RS gravitons produce qualitatively new high-energy angular structures with multiple local extrema. Results are cross-checked against MadGraph event-by-event spin-density-matrix simulation.

At ~5 citations since April, the paper rides the fast-growing “entanglement at colliders” wave triggered by the ATLAS/CMS tt̅ entanglement observations. Its appeal is likely as a concrete worked template for applying these observables as BSM probes at future lepton colliders (ILC, muon collider)—a natural next-step reference for a subfield actively hunting for new discriminating variables. The honest read: citations reflect topical momentum more than a singular result.

arXiv:2605.06787 — The structure of multi-axion solutions to the strong CP problem (Mario Fernández Navarro et al.)

Fernández Navarro and collaborators build a general framework for multi-axion solutions, organizing the theory space by two structural conditions: whether a PQ symmetry is broken only by QCD (“QCD-PQ”) versus more generally (“general-PQ”), and whether the QED and QCD anomaly vectors E and N are parallel (universal E_i/N_i) or not. Relaxing the assumptions behind the known sum rule of Ref. [89], they derive a generalized N-axion sum rule (via Sherman–Morrison inversion) that admits values above or below one, and show axions can now populate regions to the left of the QCD band—not only the right. They map these regimes onto UV completions, noting e.g. that non-universal anomaly coefficients would rule out simple GUTs.

The ~5 citations in roughly a month likely reflect its value as a classification scheme: it gives the axion-search community a clean language (“where can axions sit relative to the QCD line, and why”) that motivates broadening experimental targets beyond the canonical band. Framework papers with explicit sum rules and a theory-space figure tend to become quick reference points.

arXiv:2605.28671 — CP-violation or Nuclear Excitation: Reviewing the Role of Neutrino Interaction Model Uncertainties on Accelerator-Based Neutrino Oscillation Measurements (Stephen Dolan et al.)

Dolan, Pickering, Stowell, Wilkinson and Wret provide a Reports on Progress in Physics review of how few-GeV neutrino–nucleus interaction modeling limits accelerator oscillation measurements at T2K, NOvA, Hyper-K and DUNE. It walks through neutrino–nucleon cross sections (CCQE, resonant/shallow/deep inelastic, diffractive/coherent pion production, radiative corrections) and nuclear effects (spectral functions, RPA, FSI, 2p2h), then quantifies why near-to-far-detector extrapolation does not trivially cancel systematics—different targets, detector responses, oscillated fluxes, and ν_e/ν_μ cross-section differences. A recurring device is “model spread” across event generators (NEUT, NuWro, GENIE, GiBUU) as a lower bound on interaction uncertainty.

As a comprehensive, up-to-date review with extensive tables and generator comparisons, it is a natural citation anchor: authors of DUNE/Hyper-K systematics studies can point to it for context and for the argument that interaction uncertainties are “the least clear” path to control. The ~5 citations so soon after a May posting reflect the standard trajectory of an authoritative review that consolidates a sprawling literature into one referenceable document.

arXiv:2604.21972 — Matchotter: An Automated Tool for Dimensional Reduction at Finite Temperature (Javier Fuentes-Martín et al.)

Fuentes-Martín, López Miras and Moreno-Sánchez present Matchotter, a finite-temperature module inside the Matchete package that automates one-loop dimensional reduction—integrating out heavy Matsubara modes to build the purely spatial 3D EFT used for cosmological phase-transition computations—for generic Lagrangians including SMEFT. They adapt functional matching techniques to the thermal path integral (identifying the EFT with the “hard region” of the effective action), handle Lorentz-breaking sum-integrals, and additionally automate supersoft matching (integrating out Debye-massive temporal gauge bosons). The tool is validated against SU(N) Yang–Mills, the Abelian Higgs model, a Yukawa toy model, and the electroweak SMEFT, with benchmark timings from seconds to ~30 minutes.

The headline selling point is systematic inclusion of higher-dimensional operators, filling a gap left by the widely used DRalgo (restricted mostly to renormalizable interactions). Given rising interest in higher-precision phase-transition predictions for gravitational-wave observables, a public, automated code addressing a “tedious and highly error-prone” bottleneck is exactly the kind of deliverable that accrues citations quickly—~5 already—as groups adopt it for BSM phase-transition studies.

item.title: Thursday, July 16, 2026
item.description:
The vibe today

A quiet-volume, high-variety day — 32 papers, no single collaboration bombshell, but an unusually rich spread of the field’s standing preoccupations. If yesterday belonged to axions and quantum information, today the flavor physicists reclaimed the room: rare kaon and B decays, CKM unitarity, QED corrections to leptonic modes, and a lattice attack on K_L→μμ all landed together, and the through-line is precision — squeezing new-physics reach out of well-measured channels rather than hunting for bumps.

The other headline is cosmological and faintly competitive: the “H_0 World Cup,” a two-paper systematic bake-off pitting fourteen proposed Hubble-tension solutions against a common dataset. It’s the kind of referee’s-verdict paper the field has been waiting for as the tension crosses 7σ, and it delivers a clear hierarchy. Around these two poles, the day carries a strong gravity-and-cosmology undertow — extra GW polarization modes from Weyl and gauge-field gravity theories, evaporating cosmologically-coupled black holes, topological-defect networks — and the axion thread the memory has tracked all fortnight keeps flowing, now in the guise of fields asked to do double cosmological duty.

And a genuinely nice sociological note: two independent open-data reanalyses posted today, one on CMS Run 2015D and one on DELPHI’s 1990s Z sample. The data-preservation ethos the DPHEP report championed last week is visibly paying dividends. A diffuse, tool-tending, breadth-over-depth morning — but a satisfying one.

Themes

Flavor precision and rare decays

The densest cluster today. Dery arXiv:2607.13136 identifies a genuine CKM blind spot: a uniform rescaling of the b-column that unitarity-triangle fits are structurally insensitive to, since B physics over-constrains the triangle’s angles but only calibrates its normalization. The punchline is that |ε_K| already constrains this flat direction at the level of the direct measurement — promoting kaons to the leading probe of a scenario B factories can’t see. Abada et al. arXiv:2607.13142 tackle the Belle II B⁺→K⁺νν excess head-on, showing that lepton-number-violating SMEFT operators can’t explain it without severe fine-tuning of neutrino masses — unless one adds a light right-handed neutrino, which reopens the window. Cornella et al. arXiv:2607.13144 build a factorization theorem for QED corrections to B⁻→τ⁻ν̅_τ, exploiting the heavy τ to get a structurally simpler EFT than the muon case, with naively-large Λ_QCDm_B/m_τ² terms cancelling. On the lattice side, Chao et al. arXiv:2607.14077 and En-Hung Chao’s collaborators show how to fix the extra low-energy constants that appear in a three-flavor treatment of the two-photon K_L→μ⁺μ⁻ long-distance contribution. Rounding it out, Prasad et al. arXiv:2607.13743 compute polarization observables in τ→VVν. Collectively this extends the precision-flavor lineage the memory has followed — the b→sℓℓ and Belle II b→u work of the past two weeks — but pushes it toward CKM structure and QED systematics rather than the C_9 debate.

The H0 World Cup

Schöneberg et al.’s twin papers arXiv:2607.13282, arXiv:2607.13283 are the day’s most consequential cosmology entry: a systematic, common-framework contest of fourteen tension solutions against current CMB (ACT/SPT), BAO (DESI) and supernova data, judged by both frequentist and Bayesian criteria. The verdict is unambiguous — early dark energy and early modified gravity win, shifting the inferred H_0 toward 70 and cutting the residual SH0ES discrepancy to ∼2.5–3.6σ, while varying the electron mass lands intermediate and both enhanced-radiation and late-time scenarios fail to beat ΛCDM. This is the natural sequel to the scattered dark-energy work the memory noted (the smooth sign-switching DE model of July 6, the DESI evolving-w threads) — but now as a refereed tournament rather than individual pleas. Paper II’s robustness gauntlet is the part model-builders will actually cite.

Extra gravitational-wave polarizations

A coherent modified-gravity cluster, all asking the same question: does the LVK/LISA/Taiji era see polarization modes beyond GR’s two tensor states? Ghilencea et al. arXiv:2607.13146 work out Weyl quadratic gauge gravity, finding two extra vector modes from the Weyl gauge field’s transverse fluctuations, and stress the analysis must be done around a de Sitter background to get the GW content right. Xu et al. arXiv:2607.13483 target the transverse scalar (breathing) mode of Gravitational Quantum Field Theory with Taiji, using a null-response channel to isolate it cleanly. And Hua et al. arXiv:2607.13066 simulate a hybrid domain-wall/cosmic-string network in a 3:1 U(1) model, with preliminary GW spectra. Three different UV frameworks, one shared bet: gravitational-wave polarimetry as a discriminator among gauge theories of gravity. This isn’t a thread the recent memory has tracked — it reads as a fresh coalescence.

Axions and inflatons carrying cosmological loads

The axion diversification the memory has flagged for weeks continues, today with fields asked to solve more than one problem at once. Bittar et al. arXiv:2607.13128 identify a “weak axion” as the phase of the SM’s anomalous U(1)_B+L, whose radiatively-stable potential — controlled by two Weinberg operators and a spontaneously-broken S_3 lepton symmetry — comes out parametrically near the dark-energy scale, with the amplitude set by the departure from tribimaximal mixing so that Hyper-K and DUNE’s δ_CP/θ_23 measurements directly test it. Deng et al. arXiv:2607.13592 use an axion-like inflaton’s derivative coupling to produce heavy right-handed neutrinos during inflation and preheating, feeding non-thermal leptogenesis. And Grimaud et al. arXiv:2607.13637 assess ALP-photon oscillation signatures in stacked VHE gamma-ray spectra of AGN behind galaxy clusters, targeting the neV window with H.E.S.S.-class telescopes. The Bittar paper is the standout: tying dark energy to observable neutrino mixing is a rare falsifiable handle on quintessence.

Open data, reanalyzed

Two independent analyses today lean entirely on archived data, a quiet vindication of the preservation push. Rasineni arXiv:2607.13771 runs a mono-Z dark-matter search on CMS Run 2015D open data using neural spline flows for likelihood-ratio scoring across a 37-dimensional feature space — methodologically novel even if statistics-limited. Fan et al. arXiv:2607.13804 mine DELPHI’s 1992–1995 Z→ hadrons sample for the first measurement of Ξ⁻/Ξ̅⁺ production in energy-ranked jets, finding gluon/quark ratios consistent with JETSET. Neither is a blockbuster, but together they show open data functioning as intended — as a live resource for both new methods and new observables, exactly the payoff the DPHEP Global Report argued for last week.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2607.13283 — The H_0 World Cup’s comprehensive round: fourteen tension solutions, one framework, a clear early-dark-energy verdict. The reference bake-off going forward.
  • arXiv:2607.13128 — A “weak axion” tying dynamical dark energy to neutrino mixing, testable at Hyper-K/DUNE via δ_CP and θ_23 — a genuinely falsifiable quintessence model.
  • arXiv:2607.13758 — CMS reports evidence for sequential Υ(nS) suppression in oxygen-oxygen and neon-neon collisions; QGP-like behavior appearing in light-ion systems, with Υ(3S)/Υ(2S) suppression above 3σ.
  • arXiv:2607.13136 — A clean, model-independent CKM blind spot, with ε_K already the leading constraint on b-column rescaling.
  • arXiv:2607.13144 — A state-of-the-art QED-corrected B→τν rate with a factorization theorem and a surprising cancellation of naively-large power corrections.

Also noted

  • **[arXiv:2607.13

Deep dives

arXiv:2607.13283 — The H_0 World Cup II: A comprehensive competition between proposed Hubble tension solutions (Nils Schöneberg et al.)

(Abstract only.) An updated systematic bake-off — the sequel to the “H_0 Olympics” — subjecting fourteen representative alternatives to ΛCDM to a common analysis of current CMB (ACT/SPT), BAO (DESI) and Type Ia SN data, now with the Hubble tension quoted above 7σ. The contenders span four mechanisms: late-time expansion modifications, modified recombination, extra pre-recombination radiation, and early non-radiative energy injection. Every model is scored with both Bayesian and frequentist tension/performance metrics, with the neutrino mass sum left free, and tested for whether adding curvature or CPL dark energy improves the fit. Leading contenders face a robustness gauntlet: alternative CMB likelihoods and multipole cuts, different SN samples, LSS information, and BBN constraints.

Per the digest, the verdict favors early dark energy and early modified gravity (shifting H_0 toward 70 and cutting the SH0ES residual to ∼2.5–3.6σ), places varying-electron-mass models intermediate, and finds enhanced-radiation and late-time scenarios failing to beat ΛCDM. Why it matters: it converts a scattered literature of individual tension “solutions” into a refereed, common-framework ranking — the reference tournament model-builders will cite, with Paper II’s robustness tests being the operative part. The honest caveat is intrinsic to any such contest: conclusions depend on the chosen dataset combination and priors, which is precisely why the robustness suite is included; results not visible here beyond the digest summary.

arXiv:2607.13128 — Dark Energy and Neutrino Flavor from the Weak Axion (Pedro Bittar et al.)

Bittar and Wagner identify dark energy with a “weak axion” — the phase of a complex scalar carrying the SM’s anomalous U(1)B+L charge — and show its potential can be radiatively stable at the meV scale. Electroweak-instanton contributions come out ∼10 orders of magnitude too small (Λ_inst⁴≃(6×10⁻⁶ eV)⁴|c_BL|³), so the dominant potential arises from two inequivalent Weinberg operators generating an axion-dependent Majorana mass. A spontaneously-broken S_3 lepton permutation symmetry enforces the orthogonality condition Tr[M_Φ^†M⋆]=0, which simultaneously kills the quadratic divergence and the leading T_ν² m_ν² thermal force, pushing the first axion-dependent Coleman-Weinberg term to quartic order in neutrino masses. The amplitude vanishes in the exact tribimaximal limit, so the observed departure sets the scale: Λ_ν≃2.3 meV√(|cosδ_CP/0.52+sin(θ_23-π/4)/0.055|), landing in the 1–4 meV range for current oscillation data.

Why it matters: this is a rare falsifiable quintessence model — the dark-energy scale becomes a prediction from PMNS parameters, with δ_CP accounting for ∼80% of the variance, so Hyper-K/DUNE directly test it. It also predicts m_ββ≃1.5–3.7 meV (below next-gen reach) and behaves as instability-free thawing quintessence for f∼M_pl. Caveats, stated frankly: it does not address the cosmological-constant problem (vacuum energy assumed zero), faces a “severe axion-quality problem” requiring |ΔV_UV|≲ρ_DE, and needs near-Planckian f — treated as low-energy assumptions rather than derived. NuFit and long-baseline (T2K/NOvA) best-fits currently map to different Λ_ν.

arXiv:2607.13758 — Evidence for sequential Υ(nS) suppression in light ion collisions (CMS Collaboration)

CMS reports the first measurements of Υ(1S,2S,3S) in oxygen-oxygen and Υ(1S,2S) in neon-neon collisions at √(s_NN)=5.36 TeV, with a pp reference at the same energy (integrated luminosities 8.4 nb⁻¹, 0.81 nb⁻¹, 456 pb⁻¹). Double ratios of excited-to-ground-state yields relative to pp come out below unity in OO: D_21=0.664±0.055±0.007, D_31=0.392±0.077±0.023, D_32=0.59±0.12±0.04 — the last below unity by 3.2σ, the headline “evidence” for sequential suppression in a light-ion system. In NeNe, D_21=0.27±0.12±0.01, lower than OO by 3.0σ. The OO Υ(3S)/Υ(2S) ratio is compatible with PbPb across p_T and integrated, supporting a common QGP-medium interpretation.

Why it matters: it extends state-dependent bottomonium suppression to ⟨N_part⟩≈10, a system size an order of magnitude below PbPb, reinforcing that QGP-like final-state effects need not require large volumes — bearing on the long-running debate over deconfinement in small systems. Caveats the paper flags: the D_32 significance is modest (3.2σ); event-activity trends “should be carefully interpreted” since multiplicity alone does not fix suppression (head-on OO can rival PbPb particle production per participant); and the shinchon transport model “significantly underestimates” the measured suppression, hinting at missing medium dynamics.
